But if they have not read them at all, or have read them carelessly, what shame is it for disciples to sit in judgment on their own masters, not even their hearers? And that foolish objection, that those words are not found in Scripture, when it has been raised, heard, rejected and condemned by the judgment of all good and learned men, what is it worth? Certainly, if we must use no words except those found in the same letters in the sacred books, and if whoever uses some proper and fitting words to explain the meaning of the divine Word is to be considered a sophist, into what narrow straits shall we be driven? Indeed, what will those very men do when they come to defend their own positions, who now, under the pretext of the Word of God, are working for this single purpose, that they may crush you disarmed? For my part I hold this: although the truth of sacred things depends on nothing other than the single Word of God, and every empty talk [κενοφωνία] must be carefully avoided by us, nevertheless, if the distinction between essence and hypostases is removed (in whatever words), and homoousios is abolished, the frauds and errors of those blasphemers can hardly, or scarcely at all, be exposed and sufficiently clearly refuted. I also deny that, with the words nature, property, hypostatic union and communication of properties [ἰδιωμάτων κοινωνίας] removed, the blasphemies of Nestorius and Eutyches can be conveniently refuted by anyone. In this matter, if I am perhaps mistaken, let whoever can show me how, and we will crown him. Yet I by no means deny that the doctrine of the Christian religion ought to be set forth most simply, especially in catechisms; that obscure controversies are to be avoided among the people; that the fact [τὸ ὅτι] should always be explained, while the reason [τὸ διότι] should never be touched except soberly and prudently; and finally, that in this age we ought to labour rather to bring people to the amendment of their lives than to explain those most difficult questions subtly and at length. All of this, I say, I do not deny. But should those things, which the truth itself declares were dictated by the Holy Spirit himself and which the outcome of events shows to be so, be condemned as sophistical under the pretext of simplicity? Does he stir up obscure controversies who, even among a simple people already bewitched by heretics, exposes the errors in which they are engaged, and refutes the frauds and lies of false prophets with firm and solid arguments, never departing from the Word of God? Does Paul, writing to the Galatians, treat only the fact [τὸ ὅτι] simply? Does he therefore ask in vain that a bishop be not only a teacher [διδασκαλος] but also unreprovable [ἀλεγκτος]? Or, because all curiosity must be avoided, is no account to be taken of necessity? Those who, through great ignorance, dream that dialectic is opposed to theology are indeed more worthy of pity than of any answer. For first, to think that anyone can reason without reasoning, whether you do it by art or by nature alone, is the mark of a man utterly out of his mind, one who has quite forgotten that he is a man. Next, these men seem not to know that dialectic is not among those disciplines which supply the very matter under discussion; rather, it shows how matter taken from any source is to be used, so that it may show what agrees or does not agree with what, and what follows from what or does not, lest, deceived by false reasonings, we follow a lie for the truth. Since this is so, it is necessary that these men want sacred things to be inquired into and disputed either in no way at all or without any reasoning. Both of these are manifestly absurd and inept, since not even the enemies of this most divine art can attack it except by reasoning. But this escapes the unlearned, that they think there is no reasoning except what someone draws from his own brain; and so, since theology does not rest at all on human reason, they suppose that dialectic is also excluded. This fiction again deserves no refutation. For who does not see that reason is one thing and reasoning another? Reason is supplied to each person by his subject matter, as it were; reasoning is taught by nature and polished by art, which is called dialectic because it teaches people to speak aptly and to the point about any matter whatever that is put before them. This gift, which is a clear trace of the image of God in human beings, those who despise it must either condemn what they do not understand (which is certainly not the mark of a wise man), or belong to the class of those who want to seem to be mad with reason. Now it remains that, since this opportunity has been offered, I urge all who care for the truth in the matter of greatest importance of all, that is, in religion, to maintain it, and to look most diligently at where things stand and what their duty is. The records of our law are settled. If the question is one of interpretation, it is also clear in what ways and by what means that chief enemy of ours has tried from the beginning to corrupt them, and by what methods the evil arts of that enemy were exposed by the leaders and the truth bravely defended. Nor will it be difficult now to understand this and to turn it to our use, since Satan has been reduced to the point where, as if his most fruitful breast of all lies were exhausted, he is compelled to practise magic [μαγγανεύειν] and to bring back those old interpolations, as we have just shown. The truth, I admit, rests on the Word of God, and the Fathers must be read with judgment. But who will concede that there was no Church until now (as there certainly was none, if these men speak the truth)? Unless perhaps the Church is that body which does not know who the true God is. Then, if it also pleases us to judge these men from other sources, namely from the manifest judgments of God, by which he has avenged in the sight of all the blasphemies hurled against his Son, what is more manifest than this judgment too? Servetus, who denied with blasphemous tongue the eternity, that is the deity, of Christ, died, thrusting that eternal fire before the eyes of spectators, not without great horror to all. Gribaldus, seized by plague, was found with difficulty by anyone who would bury him, since everyone fled from him. Lismaninus, by whom Blandrata was introduced, threw himself into a well. What spectacle of death did that man, the guest of these lost men, afford? How wretchedly the apostate Ochinus died with his followers, all Poland knows. And what took away from that man, who was about to curse Christ the next day in Transylvania, from the extreme exile of body and soul, when his house suddenly collapsed, except that long-suffering of God? By what death did Gentilis finally end his unhappy life last year? Although these things are not strictly demonstrative, yet whoever compares the former with the latter and looks more closely at everything will certainly find in these men such clear testimonies of divine wrath that they seem to me alone sufficient to deserve it. Let them be warned by these things, and let those whom the patience of God still awaits be called back to a better mind, and let the rest be roused, lest they wish to perish with these men of their own accord. But it is for you above all, most august King of the most valiant Polish nation, to persevere most steadily in what you have so happily begun, and not to permit that those who curse the Son of God (and who curses him more plainly than those who restrict the name of the One God, or the true God, to the Father alone, since there can be no several true gods by nature, or who transform him into a creature?) return to you, to whom the kingdom has been committed by the Son of God, a kingdom made liable to the wrath of Almighty God by such blasphemies. It is also for you, most serene King of Transylvania, whom you almost unwittingly cherish in your bosom, to watch carefully lest anyone, no better than Muhammad himself, abusing the authority of your royal name, make an attack upon the whole Christian world out of that kingdom which the Lord has so wonderfully preserved for you for so many years and has lately begun to consecrate to himself. Such a man would certainly do more harm to souls than if the Muscovite, the Tartar or the Turk were to gain some notable victory. Nor, most august kings, will it be difficult for you to recognise the architects of these evils, if you apply yourselves seriously to this matter, since these controversies, which have been debated so often and in so many ways from the very times of the Apostles, and so happily set forth, have always been agreed upon by all good and learned men, so that now no one who is at all versed in the Word of God and in ecclesiastical books could, with a good conscience, appear to doubt them. And you, illustrious and noble lords, whom the Lord of lords has deigned to bring to true knowledge of himself in both of those kingdoms, kiss the Son, and do not allow him, whom they strip of his deity, to remain among those whom above all it behoves to show themselves the defenders and champions of his glory and dignity. And you, respected brothers, to whom the Lord has committed the feeding of his flocks, will you, I beg you, allow even one little sheep to be snatched from you by those savage wolves through your silence? You Threcius, you Lasicius, you Sarnicius (whom I address by name, as I know you among the great number of learned and godly men), and finally you other ministers and teachers of the Churches, I beseech and adjure you in the Lord, that you attack with all your hearts this enemy, so often conquered and so often overthrown, and that you not rest until, relying on the two-edged sword of the Word of God [ἀμφιδέξιῳ] drawn out, you either win back these now lost men to the Lord, or at least keep your flocks safe from the attacks of those wolves. Behold, we send to you as fellow champions [συναγωνιστὰς] men chosen from the leading teachers of the Christian academies, from whose name alone we hope you will be refreshed. We, indeed absent in body but present in spirit, know that we shall contend with you before the eyes of that great Judge of our contest, and that before long, by God's favour, we shall share with you the fruit of the common victory.

units.la: Genevae Nonis Augusti.
units.tr: Geneva, on the Nones of August.

units.la: VALENTINI GENTILIS impietatum & triplicis perfidiæ ac periurii, de quibus cognouit Senatus Geneuensis, breuis explicatio ex actis publicis descripta.
units.tr: The impieties and threefold treachery and perjury of Valentinus Gentilis, of which the Senate of Geneva took cognizance: a brief account drawn from the public records.

units.la: QUum ante annos quatuor subolfecissent Ita-licæ ecclesiæ, quæ apud nos est, Seniores, inter quosdã è suo grege peruersos sermones cōtra primũ fidei nostræ caput de tribus in vna Dei essentia personis agitari: nullum melius remedium illis visum est, quàm edita confessionis forma, cui omnes subscriberent, detegere si quod occultum virus lateret: quam hîc è verbo ad verbum Latinè redditam inseruimus.
units.tr: When four years ago the elders of the Italian church, which is among us, sensed that certain perverse discourses were being stirred up among some of their flock against the first article of our faith, concerning the three persons in the one essence of God, they judged that no better remedy was available than a published form of confession, to which all would subscribe, so that any hidden poison lying concealed might be brought to light. We have inserted it here, translated word for word into Latin.

units.la: CONFESSIO FIDEI EDITA IN ITALICA ECCLESIA GENEVAE, XVIII. Maii, anno M. D. LVIII.
units.tr: THE CONFESSION OF FAITH PUBLISHED IN THE ITALIAN CHURCH AT GENEVA, 18 MAY, 1558.

units.la: Potuit[?] quidem modestis omnibus Christianis sufficere fidei confessionem, Symbolo Apostolico comprehensam. Quia tamen nonnulli, quos sua quædam curiositas à pura & vera fide abdu-xit, sparsis quibusdam falsis opinionibus & erroribus, pacem ac consensum huius Ecclesiæ perturbarunt, visum est nobis edere præsentem fidei confessionem de vna & simplice Dei essentia, & trium personarum di-stinctione, tum vt occurramus omnibus istis Satanæ versutijs, tum etiam vt aduersus istos impostores satis instructi simus, atque adeò vt demonstremus nos vno corde idem sentire & ore loqui, paritérque reiicere ac detestari omnes hæreses illi puræ fidei contrarias, quam adhuc retinuimus, & ad extremum vsque sequi decreuimus.
units.tr: Indeed, the confession of faith comprised in the Apostles' Creed might have sufficed for all modest Christians. But since some, whom a certain curiosity has drawn away from the pure and true faith, have disturbed the peace and agreement of this Church by scattering certain false opinions and errors, it has seemed good to us to publish the present confession of faith concerning the one and simple essence of God and the distinction of the three persons: partly so that we may meet all the crafty devices of Satan, and partly so that we may be sufficiently armed against those impostors, and so that we may show that we think with one heart and speak with one mouth, and equally reject and detest all heresies contrary to that pure faith which we have hitherto held and have resolved to follow to the very end.

units.la: Profitemur ergo Deum Patrem ita genuisse ab æterno suum Verbum, sive Sapientiam, quæ est vnicus ipsius Filius, & Spiritum sanctum ab vtroque illo-rum ita processisse, vt vnica sit ac simplex essentia, Patris, Filij, & Spiritus sancti. Quod autem Pater à Filio, & ab vtroque Spiritus sanctus sit distinctus, id fieri personarum respectu.
units.tr: We therefore profess that God the Father has from eternity so begotten his Word, or Wisdom, which is his only Son, and that the Holy Spirit has so proceeded from both of them, that there is one and simple essence of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. That the Father is distinguished from the Son, and the Holy Spirit from both, takes place by reason of the persons.

units.la: Itaque damnamus ac detestamur eorum errorem, qui dicunt Patrem sim-pliciter suae essentiae respectu, & quatenus (ut ipsi loquuntur) solus est ac verus Deus, Filium suum genuisse, perinde ac si divina maiestas, gloria, essentia, de-nique vera illa deitas esset solius Patris propria, aut Iesus Christus & Spiritus sanctus essent di[?]versi ab illo procedentes, ac proinde divisa esset ac separata divinæ essentiæ unitas.
units.tr: Therefore we condemn and detest the error of those who say that the Father, simply with respect to his essence, and insofar as (as they put it) he alone is the true God, begat his Son, just as if the divine majesty, glory, essence, and finally that true deity were the proper possession of the Father alone, or as if Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit were different beings proceeding from him, and consequently the unity of the divine essence were divided and separated.

units.la: Cæterum quum unum duntaxat Deum profitemur, agnoscimus quicquid eius deitati, gloriæ, & essentiæ attribuitur, tam convenire Filio quam Spiritui sancto, quum simpliciter agitur de Deo, absque mutua inter se personarum comparatione. Sin autem personæ inter se comparentur, observandæ sunt singulorum proprietates, quibus ita distinguantur, ut Filius non sit Pater, nec Spiritus sanctus sit Filius.
units.tr: Moreover, since we profess only one God, we acknowledge that whatever is attributed to his deity, glory and essence belongs equally to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, when God is spoken of simply, without any mutual comparison of the persons among themselves. But if the persons are compared with one another, the properties of each must be observed, by which they are so distinguished that the Son is not the Father, nor is the Holy Spirit the Son.

units.la: Quod attinet ad personam Domini nostri Iesu Christi, præterquam quod ab omni æternitate genitus est à Deo Patre, & est persona ab eo distincta, credimus eum in humana quoque natura, quam nostræ salutis causa induit, verum ac naturalem esse Dei Filium: quoniam videlicet duas naturas ita in unum conjunxit, ut sit unicus Mediator, Deus manifestatus in carne, servatis tamen utriusque naturæ proprietatibus.
units.tr: As for the person of our Lord Jesus Christ, besides the fact that he was begotten by God the Father from all eternity and is a person distinct from him, we believe that he, in the human nature also, which he put on for the cause of our salvation, is the true and natural Son of God: since, namely, he so joined the two natures into one that he is the only Mediator, God manifested in the flesh, the properties of each nature nevertheless being preserved.

units.la: Porrò ita hanc Confessionem edimus, ut sancte testemur ac polliceamur per eam fidem quam Deo sumus obstricti, nos hanc doctrinam observaturos, & in ea ita perseveraturos, ut nunquam directe vel oblique, consulto quidem ac malitiose, illi repugnemus, ad fovendam ullam dissidij speciem, quo possit ab ista concordia discedi. Denique, ut omnibus discordiis in posterum occurratur, profitemur nos vivere ac mori decreuisse secundum huius Ecclesiæ doctrinam, & contrariis omnibus sectis restituros. Hæc omnia comprobamus, recipimus, ac confirmamus, ea conditione, ut qui secus faxit, pro periuro ac perfido habeatur.
units.tr: Furthermore, we publish this Confession in such a way that we solemnly testify and promise, by the faith which we are bound to God, that we will observe this doctrine and persevere in it, so that we never, directly or indirectly, deliberately and maliciously, oppose it, nor foster any appearance of dissension by which one might depart from this agreement. Finally, so that all discords may be prevented in future, we profess that we have resolved to live and die according to the doctrine of this Church, and to resist all contrary sects. We approve, receive and confirm all these things, on the condition that whoever acts otherwise be regarded as a perjurer and a traitor.

units.la: Ioh. Sylvester Telius, suprascriptam confessionem approbo, & quicquid ei repugnat detestor.
units.tr: I, Giovanni Silvestro Telio, approve the aforesaid confession, and detest whatever is contrary to it.

units.la: Fr. Porcellinus, recipio & approbo quicquid suprascripta confessio complectitur.
units.tr: I, Fr. Porcellino, receive and approve whatever the aforesaid confession contains.

units.la: Ioh. Valentinus Gentilis Cosentinus, accipio ut supra.
units.tr: I, Giovanni Valentino Gentile of Cosenza, accept as above.

units.la: Hippolytus Pelerinus Carignanus, accipio ut supra.
units.tr: I, Ippolito Pellerino of Carignano, accept as above.

units.la: Ioh. Nicolaus Gallus, accipio ut supra.
units.tr: I, Giovanni Niccolò Gallo, accept as above.

units.la: Ea in conuentu propositia fuit, ut liberum singulis esset in medium contra proferre, si quid reprehensione dignum censerent. Itaque proterui homines impunè tribus circiter horis linguas suas blaterādo exercuerūt: inter quos princeps fuit Iohānes quidā Paulus Alciatus, homo non stolidi tantùm ac uæsani ingenii, sed planè phreneticus ad rabiem usq;. Tantū illis licentiæ fuit concessum, ne postea obstreperent, sibi ius loquendi fuisse ademptum. Sedata omni contentione, nulli fuit vel controuersia vel mora quin omnes subscriberent, sex duntaxat exceptis, quorum unus erat Valentinus: qui tamen vocati, manu sua testati sunt consensum. Hoc modo qui Ecclesiæ tranquillitati studebant, putarunt obuiam itum fuisse malo, ne longius serperet. Ecce paulò post Valentinus, spreto iureiurando, suos susurros in obscuris angulis spargere, & tentare simplices ac imperitos, an quos irretire suis insidiis posset. Reper-specta, Senatus cognitionem suscepit: ac statim multorum testimoniis periurii conuictus, quia tergiuersando locus non erat, causari coepit conscientiæ stimulis se fuisse impulsum. Auditus est in splen-dido gravium & doctorum hominum coetu. Quum eius obiecta refelleremus, uno effugio usus est, se disputandi artificium non tenere. Ita rationibus eum urgere ac premere nihil profuit. Postea farraginem, quam diu meditatus fuerat, scriptam obtulit Senatui: cuius exemplar subiecimus.
units.tr: This was put before the assembly so that each might be free to bring forward against it, if they thought anything deserving of censure. Accordingly, shameless men, unpunished, exercised their tongues in babbling for about three hours: among them the leader was a certain Giovanni Paolo Alciati, a man not merely of a stupid and foolish mind, but plainly frenetic to the point of madness. So much licence was granted to them that afterwards they should not clamour, and that the right to speak had been taken from them. When all contention had subsided, there was no dispute or delay about everyone subscribing, except six, of whom one was Valentinus; yet when called upon, they attested their consent by their own hand. In this way those who cared for the tranquillity of the Church thought that the evil had been met, lest it creep further. Behold, shortly afterwards Valentinus, having scorned his oath, began to spread his whisperings in dark corners, and to try whether he could entrap the simple and the unskilled in his snares. The Senate took up the inquiry; and immediately, convicted by the testimony of many of perjury, since there was no room for evasion, he began to plead that he had been driven on by the goads of conscience. He was heard in the splendid assembly of grave and learned men. When we refuted his objections, he had recourse to one escape, that he did not have the art of disputation. Thus pressing and crushing him with arguments availed nothing. Afterwards he presented to the Senate a medley, which he had long meditated and written out, a copy of which we have appended.

units.la: CONFESSIO VALENTINI GEN-TILIS ILLUSTRISSIMIS DOMINIS GE-nebensibus oblata.
units.tr: THE CONFESSION OF VALENTINE GENTILIS, PRESENTED TO THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS LORDS OF GENEVA.

units.la: Iateor unicum illum Deum Israel, quem Sacræ literæ nobis proponunt, solum verum Deum, & quem ventosi Sophistæ negant habere Filium, esse Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi: ipsumque Iesum Christum quem ille misit, quatenus est Verbum, esse verum ac naturalem Filium illius unici Dei Patris omnipotentis. Hæc est summa sententiæ meæ in articulo de æterna generatione Filij Dei, & doctrinæ Genebensis Ecclesiæ penitus subscribo.
units.tr: I confess that that one God of Israel, whom the Holy Scriptures set before us, is the only true God, and that he is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, though the windy Sophists deny that he has a Son. And I confess that Jesus Christ himself, whom he sent, is, as the Word, the true and natural Son of that one almighty God the Father. This is the sum of my opinion on the article concerning the eternal generation of the Son of God, and I wholly subscribe to the doctrine of the Church of Geneva.

units.la: Altera confessio eiusdem, iussu illustrium Dominorum exarata.
units.tr: Second confession of the same man, written at the command of the illustrious Lords.

units.la: Equidem censeo primam personam Patris in unica essentia esse Sophisticam, atque ideo hoc sensu a mysterio Trinitatis penitus expungendam. Nam si Pater esset individuum in essentia simile Verbo, non diceretur verè neque solus Pater, neque ingenitus, neque principium totius divinitatis. Præterea eiusmodi sententia Quaternitatem potius quàm Trinitatem videtur constituere. Quod facile sic probari posset,
units.tr: Indeed, I judge that the first person, the Father, within the one essence is a Sophistical notion, and therefore in this sense must be wholly expunged from the mystery of the Trinity. For if the Father were an individual in essence like the Word, he would not truly be called either the sole Father, or unbegotten, or the principle of the whole divinity. Moreover, such an opinion seems rather to constitute a Quaternity than a Trinity. This could easily be proved as follows.

units.la: Unica illa essentia absque ulla consideratione personarum est ex semetipsa verus Deus: & quælibet trium personarum est item essentialiter Deus. Sequitur ergo Quaternitas, non Trinitas. Quamobrem assero Patrem esse ipsam unicam essentiam: Verbum autem splendorem gloriæ Dei, & expressam imaginem substantiæ illius, hac ratione à Patre distinctum, quòd Pater (ut ait Christus) est solus verus Deus, & essentiator, hoc est informator individuorum: Verbum verò est Filius, simul & verus Deus: neque tamen duo dii, sed unus idémque Deus. Hæc est summa sententiæ meæ de vero Patre, veróque Filio: nam de Spiritu sancto nulla est quæstio, & tamen iudicio Ecclesiarum libentissimè subscribam.
units.tr: That one essence, without any consideration of persons, is of itself the true God, and each of the three persons is likewise essentially God. Therefore a Quaternity follows, not a Trinity. Wherefore I affirm that the Father is the one essence itself; but the Word, the brightness of God's glory and the express image of his substance, is distinguished from the Father on this ground: that the Father (as Christ says) is the only true God and the essentiator, that is, the informer of individuals; but the Word is the Son, and at the same time true God, yet not two gods but one and the same God. This is the sum of my opinion concerning the true Father and the true Son. For concerning the Holy Spirit there is no question, and yet I will most willingly subscribe to the judgement of the Churches.

units.la: Idem Valentinus Gentilis inutilis servus Iesu Christi, captivus Genevæ propter confessionem veri Dei, Domino Copo, Raymundo, Henoco, cæterisque fidelibus verbi Dei dispensatoribus, gratiam & pacem ab illo unico Deo Israel vero Patre, & ab Iesu Christo, vero ac naturali eius Filio per Spiritum sanctum, Amen.
units.tr: Valentine Gentile, the same, useless servant of Jesus Christ, a prisoner at Geneva on account of confessing the true God, to Lord Copus, Raymundus, Henoch, and the other faithful dispensers of the Word of God: grace and peace from that one God of Israel, the true Father, and from Jesus Christ, his true and natural Son, through the Holy Spirit. Amen.

units.la: Si quis unquam indignè persecutionem passus est ab iis qui veram pietatem profitentur, ego quidem, optimi viri Dei, verè & sine fuco is dici possum. Nam quum ab extremis Italiæ finibus propter Verbum Dei in longinquas & peregrinas regiones me contulissem, nulla alia de causa hanc vestram Ecclesiam potissimùm elegi, nisi ut dominum Calvinum, quem antea nomine observabam, de facie cognoscerem & audirem. Postea verò quum apud nostros Italos quæstio de Trinitate agitaretur, equidem meam sententiam liberè in medium protuli, cupiens doceri de iis quæ tum occurrebat, haud vulgaria illa quidem, sed cœlesti potius spiritualique speculatione dignissima. Ac ne quis quicquam mea fide indignum (ut est hominum libido prona ad malum) suspicaretur, disertis verbis declaravi, me omnē pluralitatem deorum, & minoritatem Filii toto pectore detestari. Sed quidam imperiosi homines, qui purissimam fidem meam denigrare conati sunt, dominum Calvinum adeò in me irritaverunt, ut ille de me apertè malè sentire non dubitarit. Tandem contetio[?] per illustrissimum Magistratum sedata fuit, egóque cum aliis doctis ac probis viris subscripsi confessioni domini Caluini, putans fore vt in posterum omnia tuta & tranquilla cernerentur. Quum interim ecce tibi minister noster, nescio quo æstro percitus, nos omnes qui subscripseramus apud exteras nationes oratione publica non solum vt Arianos & Seruetanos notauit, verumetiam vt Georgianos, aut si quid peius dici cogitarive potest. Quod quum ego resciuissem, statim me conuerti ad vnicum illum Deum Israel, quem toto pectore colo, purásque manus in cælum extollens, rogaui illum qui solus innocentiam meam nouit, vt veritatem suam patefaceret, méque ab hisce calumniis, & imposturis [?] tandem (si vellet) liberaret. Exaudiuit ille preces meas, & veritatem, quam hactenus subobscuram & implicitam tenebam, fugatis tenebris Sole ipso sua benignitate clariorem ostendit. Quam veritatem ipsemet Deus Israel, qui hanc Ecclesiam suam singulari amore prosequitur, sua diuina prouidentia fecit vt ego iussu illustrissimorum Dominorum frequenti tribunali confiterer. Quod quidem (vt bonum ac fidelem seruum decet) sincere & sine vllo fuco feci iuxta modulum fidei, quæ mihi tradita est.
units.tr: If anyone has ever suffered unworthy persecution at the hands of those who profess true piety, I, best men of God, may truly and without pretence be called such a one. For when I had betaken myself from the farthest borders of Italy into distant and foreign regions for the sake of the Word of God, I chose this your Church above all for no other reason than to know Lord Calvin, whom I had before revered by name, face to face, and to hear him. Afterwards, however, when the question of the Trinity was being debated among our Italians, I freely put my opinion forward in the midst, desiring to be taught about the matters that then arose, which were indeed not commonplace but most worthy of heavenly and spiritual contemplation. And lest anyone suspect anything unworthy of my faith (as human inclination is prone to evil), I declared in plain words that I detest with my whole heart every plurality of gods and any inferiority of the Son. But certain domineering men, who tried to blacken my most pure faith, so provoked Lord Calvin against me that he did not hesitate to think ill of me openly. At last the contention was calmed by the most illustrious Magistrate, and I, with other learned and upright men, subscribed to the confession of Lord Calvin, thinking that all would be seen to be safe and calm in future. Meanwhile, behold, our minister, roused by I know not what gadfly, in a public address among foreign nations denounced us all who had subscribed not only as Arians and Servetians, but also as Georgians, or whatever worse can be said or thought. When I learned this, I immediately turned to that one God of Israel, whom I worship with my whole heart, and, lifting pure hands to heaven, I asked him, who alone knows my innocence, to reveal his truth and to free me at last from these calumnies and impostures, if he would. He heard my prayers, and the truth, which hitherto I had held somewhat obscured and entangled, he showed clearer than the sun itself, the darkness being dispelled by his kindness. This truth the very God of Israel, who pursues this his Church with singular love, by his divine providence brought it about that I, at the command of the most illustrious Lords, made confession before a crowded tribunal. This I did (as befits a good and faithful servant) sincerely and without any pretence, according to the measure of faith that has been delivered to me.

units.la: Hæc pauca eo præfari visum est, optimi viri Dei, vt inde intelligeretis verum illum Patrem nostrum maximè esse veracem, nec vllo pacto iis qui toto corde illi fidunt, vnquam defuturum. Cætera quæ acta sunt, quando longè notiora sunt, quàm vt vlla indigeant narratione, reliquum est vt ad firmas ratiocinationes sententiæ meæ breuiter descendam. Quod sic me facere Dominus ipse Spiritu suo præcepit.
units.tr: I thought fit to premise these few things, best men of God, so that from them you might understand that that true Father of ours is supremely truthful, and that he will by no means fail those who trust in him with their whole heart. As for the other things that were done, since they are far too well known to need any narrative, it remains for me to descend briefly to the firm reasonings of my opinion. The Lord himself commanded me by his Spirit to do so.

units.la: Vtrum vnica essentia concurrat in Trinitatem necne? Si non concurrit, necessario Trinitas erit sine Deo, imò vana, imò nulla: sin autem concurrit, communis opinio doctorum Quaternitatem statuit, non Trinitatem.
units.tr: Does the one essence concur into the Trinity or not? If it does not concur, the Trinity will necessarily be without God, indeed empty, indeed nothing. But if it does concur, the common opinion of the learned establishes a Quaternity, not a Trinity.

units.la: Quæritur: Vtrum vnica illa essentia, quam dominus Caluinus negat concurrere in Trinitatem, sit ex semetipsa verus Deus absque vllo respectu personarum? Puto id eum minimè negaturum. Quare quum quilibet trium personarum sit essentialiter Deus, nũquam poterit inficiari hanc communem doctorum sententiam constituere Quaternitatem.
units.tr: The question is: is that one essence, which Lord Calvin denies concurs into the Trinity, of itself the true God without any respect to persons? I think he will by no means deny this. Wherefore, since each of the three persons is essentially God, he will never be able to deny that this common opinion of the learned constitutes a Quaternity.

units.la: Tria igitur concurrunt in Trinitatem, Essentia quæ dicitur Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus. Atque hæc est vera Trinitas, quæ est trium vnitas, non autem quatuor: quicquid dicat dominus Caluinus de etymo.
units.tr: Therefore three things concur into the Trinity: the Essence, which is called the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. And this is the true Trinity, which is the unity of three, not of four, whatever Lord Calvin may say about etymology.

units.la: Quæritur: Vtrum Essentia, Pater, & vnicus ille Deus Israel sint synonyma, quæ possint inter se inuicem supponi & prædicari?
units.tr: The question is: are Essence, Father, and that one God of Israel synonyms, which can be substituted for one another and predicated of one another?

units.la: Quæritur: Vtrum Deus Legis & Prophetarum sit Pater Verbi? Qui hoc negauerit, sciat se in Cerdonis & Archonticorum dogma incurrisse. Præterea plures deos Patres fateatur oporter.
units.tr: The question is: is the God of the Law and the Prophets the Father of the Word? Whoever denies this should know that he has fallen into the doctrine of Cerdo and the Archontics. Moreover, one must admit that there are several gods who are Fathers.

units.la: Quæritur: An neget dominus Caluinus, vnicum illum Deum Israel esse Patrem Verbi? Si affirmarit, nulla (vt dixi) erit inter nos controuersia: sin autem negarit, sic probabo.
units.tr: The question is: does Lord Calvin deny that that one God of Israel is the Father of the Word? If he affirms it, there will be (as I said) no controversy between us; but if he denies it, I will prove it as follows.

units.la: Quæro ab eo: Vtrum Patriarchæ & Prophetæ inuocauerint vnicum illum Deum Israel? Neque id puto eum negaturum. Sed quando frustra inuocatur Deus sine Mediatore, quæritur per quem Mediatorem inuocarint illum? Aperte quæso hic respondeat: (nam vana est illa tergiuersatio, Non necesse est illum semper occurrere.) volo enim doceri, an habuerint Mediatorem, necne. Per Christum respondeat oportet. Per Christum, inquam, (est enim ipse Christus verè Filius Dei, & verus Deus) vt Filium, an vt Deum? Absit vt Christus fuerit illius Mediator vt Deus. Si igitur fuit illis Mediator quatenus Filius, sequitur ergo, quòd vnicus ille Deus Israel est verus & naturalis Pater Christi, vt Verbi, sine respectu alicuius personæ.
units.tr: I ask him: did the Patriarchs and Prophets invoke that one God of Israel? I do not think he will deny this. But since God is invoked in vain without a Mediator, the question is through what Mediator they invoked him. Let him answer plainly on this point (for that evasion, "It is not necessary that he always be present," is empty), for I wish to be taught whether they had a Mediator or not. He must answer: through Christ. Through Christ, I say (for Christ himself is truly the Son of God and true God), but as Son or as God? Far be it that Christ was their Mediator as God. If therefore he was their Mediator as Son, it follows that that one God of Israel is the true and natural Father of Christ as Word, without respect to any person.

units.la: Quare, qui asserùt Christum esse Filium Dei respectu illius personæ Sophisticæ, magnam illi quidem iniuriam faciunt, tum vnico illi Deo Israel, tum etiam Christo eius Filio. Sic enim asserétes, fatentur se non minus ignorare verum Patrem quàm verum Filium, in quorum pura cognitione consistit vita æterna, vt ipse Christus Patrem alloquens ait: Hæc est vita æterna, vt cognoscât te solum verum Deum, & quem misisti Iesum Christum. Quomodo enim solum verum Deum, Patrem cognoscent, qui negat illum habere synonymiam cum Essentia, quæ est solus verus Deus? Quomodo etiam cognoscent Iesum Christum, qui contra authoritatem Scripturarum faciunt eum Filium illius Sophisticæ personæ? Licet enim Sophistæ Christum Filium Dei prædicent, quum tamen vnicum illum Deum sterilem & infœcundum sibi fabricati sint, non verum ac naturalem, sed suppositiritium Filium intelligant, necesse est. Quasi vnicus ille Deus Israel nequierit sibi Filiu gignere, nisi illa diabolica persona sibi illum supposuerit. Quis vnquam talia fando, audierit? Quis non videt, optimi viri Dei, hoc diabolico commento totam Trinitatem adulterasse Sophistas, Deum illum fœcundum, sterilem facientes: Patrem, personam illam Sophisticam: Verbum, Filium eiusmodi personæ: Spiritum sanctum quoque procedentem ex ambabus illis personis fictitiis & adulterinis? Quapropter haud impropriè in hos torqueri posset illud Danielis vaticinium: Adorabunt Deum quem non cognouerunt Patres eorum. Quis enim vel Patriarcharum, vel Prophetarum, vel Apostolorum cognouit vnquam eiusmodi Deum, qui sibi Filium non genuerit? Turcarum Deus is est, non Christianorum.
units.tr: Wherefore those who assert that Christ is the Son of God with respect to that Sophistical person do great injury both to that one God of Israel and to Christ his Son. For those who assert this confess that they are no less ignorant of the true Father than of the true Son, in whose pure knowledge eternal life consists, as Christ himself, addressing the Father, says: "This is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent." For how will they know the Father, the only true God, who deny that he has synonymy with the Essence, which is the only true God? How will they also know Jesus Christ, who, against the authority of the Scriptures, make him the Son of that Sophistical person? For although the Sophists proclaim Christ the Son of God, yet since they have fashioned for themselves that one God of Israel as barren and unfruitful, they must understand the Son not as true and natural but as a supposititious Son. As if the one God of Israel could not beget a Son for himself, unless that diabolical person had substituted one for him. Who has ever heard such things said? Who does not see, best men of God, that by this diabolical invention the Sophists have adulterated the whole Trinity, making God, who is fruitful, into a barren one; the Father, into that Sophistical person; the Word, into a Son of such a person; and the Holy Spirit too, proceeding from those two fictitious and adulterine persons? Wherefore that prophecy of Daniel could not be inappropriately turned against them: "They will worship a God whom their fathers did not know." For who of the Patriarchs, or Prophets, or Apostles has ever known such a God, one who did not beget a Son for himself? He is the God of the Turks, not of Christians.

units.la: Quæritur: Dum contendunt Christũ esse Filium Dei respectu personæ, an intelligant eum esse natura Dei Filium, necne? Si affirmarint, sanè quæso tandem valere illum respectum personalem, & liberè cum Scripturis pronuntient eum verè Filium Dei: sin autem negarint, sciant universam Scripturam adversum se stare. Quamobrem etiam atque etiam viderint pij Ecclesiarum Pasto-res, ne hac in parte Sophistarum errorem sequantur, qui Patrem negant & Verbum. negant enim Patrem, dum non ipsum Essentiatorem dicũt, sed personam in Essentia fingunt: & negant Verbum, dum personæ fictitiæ[?] Filium credunt, non autem unici ac veri Dei omnium conditoris, dando illis quæ non sunt, auferendo quæ sunt. Quis est qui vincit mundum (clamat dilectus ille) nisi qui credit quòd Iesus est Filius Dei? Qui verò confessus fuerit Christum Filium Dei, (Dei inquam, non autem personæ) Deus in illo manet, & ipse in Deo. Nos credimus testimonium Dei, quo testatus est de Filio suo: Qui Filium non habet, nec vitam habet. Non habet autem Filium, qui eum negat esse Filium illius invisibilis Pa-tris, qui est solus & verus Deus.
units.tr: The question is this: while they contend that Christ is the Son of God with respect to person, do they understand that he is the Son of God by nature or not? If they affirm it, then I earnestly ask that this personal respect be allowed to stand, and that they freely declare with the Scriptures that he is truly the Son of God. But if they deny it, let them know that the whole of Scripture stands against them. Wherefore let the godly ministers of the Churches look to this point well, lest they follow the error of the Sophists, who deny the Father and deny the Word. For they deny the Father, since they do not call him the very Begetter of the essence but feign a person within the essence; and they deny the Word, since they believe in a fictitious person as Son and not in the one true God, maker of all, giving to those things that are not and taking away from those that are. "Who is it that overcomes the world," cries that beloved disciple, "but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? Whoever confesses Christ to be the Son of God (of God, I say, not of a person), God abides in him and he in God. We believe the testimony of God, by which he bore witness concerning his Son: he who does not have the Son does not have life." But he does not have the Son who denies that he is the Son of that invisible Father, who alone is the true God.

units.la: Quæritur: Utrum unicus ille Deus Israel fuerit semper Pater, necne? Qui negat illum vel tantillum temporis Patrem non fuisse: & Deum mutabilem facit, & in familiam Arij migrat. Fuit igitur semper Pater: sed cuius fuit Pa-ter, nisi Verbi?
units.tr: The question is: was that one God of Israel always Father or not? He who denies that he was Father even for the smallest span of time both makes God mutable and migrates into the household of Arius. He was therefore always Father; but of whom was he Father, if not of the Word?

units.la: Item quæritur: Ubi ait Apostolus, Quum autem venit plenitudo tempo-ris, misit Deus Filium suum: Quisnam Deus Filium suum miserit? Illéne qui est Deus Legis & Prophetarum, an illa persona Sophistica?
units.tr: Again the question is: where the Apostle says, "But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son," which God sent his Son? Is it that God who is the God of the Law and the Prophets, or that Sophistic person?

units.la: Mitto multas alias ratiocinationes, & innumeras ferè absurditates, quas lõ-gum esset recensere. Hæc pauca attigi tantùm, ut intelligeretis veritatem ipsam & universam Scripturam à me stare. Unum illud addam, optimi viri Dei, me ob nullam aliam causam persecutionem pati, quàm quòd constanter affirmem Christum esse Filium illius unici Dei Israel, Dei inquam, Abrahã, Isaac & Iacob. Quasi vos non idem sentiatis, & quotidie concionemini: imprimif-que dominus Raymundus, qui nunquam non in diuinis suis concionibus hanc sententiam inculcat. Sed ne quis existimet me aliquid detrahere æternæ maie-statis Filij Dei, testatum omnibus facio, me illum, exceptis proprietatibus, sive distinctionibus, æqualem Patri facere. Pater enim est solus verus Deus: Christus autem est Filius simul & verus Deus: neque tamen duo dij, sed unus idemque Deus. Habet enim Christus unam eandemque Essentiam cum Patre.
units.tr: I pass over many other arguments and almost countless absurdities, which would take too long to list. I have touched on only these few, so that you may understand that the truth itself and all of Scripture stand with me. I will add one thing more, best men of God: I suffer persecution for no other cause than that I steadfastly affirm that Christ is the Son of that one God of Israel, of God, I say, of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. As if you did not hold the same view and preach it every day, above all Lord Raymundus, who never fails in his divine sermons to impress this opinion. But lest anyone think I detract anything from the eternal majesty of the Son of God, I declare to all that I make him, apart from the properties or distinctions, equal to the Father. For the Father is the only true God; Christ is the Son and at the same time the true God; yet they are not two gods but one and the same God. For Christ has one and the same essence with the Father.

units.la: Vestrum esto nunc iudicium, optimi viri Dei, an hæc mea sententia Arium sapiat, aut Servetū, ut adversarij cavillantur. Mihi quidem illi certè potius videntur vana Serveti somnia sectari, qui afferunt Christum esse Filium nescio cuius personæ phantasticæ, Scripturis sacris prorsus incognitæ.
units.tr: Now let the judgment be yours, best men of God, whether this my opinion savours of Arius or of Servetus, as my adversaries sneer. To me indeed those others seem rather to pursue the empty dreams of Servetus, who assert that Christ is the Son of I know not what phantastic person, wholly unknown to the holy Scriptures.

units.la: Præterea hanc meam sententiam delirium appellat dominus Caluinus. V-tinam veteres doctores sic delirassent! Nunquam enim tantas tenebras offu-dissent hominum mentibus. Sed non est meum de me dicere. Si vera sunt quæ vobis propono, soli Deo laudes debentur, non mihi, qui nunquam talia odora-tus essem, nisi à Deo didicissem. Illud unum bona cum venia vestra addam, hanc solam distinctionem satis esse ad probandam veram Trinitatem aduersus omnes hæreticos & infideles. Præterea vniuersa Scriptura est adeò aperta, ac vbique sibi similis, vt nullus fuci faciendi locus hæreticis amplius relictus sit. Quam quidem distinctionem, vt tenacius cuiuslibet[?] hæreat, visum est hisce exem-plis quasi quadam in tabella spectandam omnibus proponere. Pater Verbi est Deus Israel. Verbum est Deus Israel.
units.tr: Besides, Lord Calvin calls this my opinion a delirium. Would that the ancient teachers had so delirated! For they would never have cast such darkness over men's minds. But it is not mine to speak of myself. If what I set before you is true, praise is due to God alone, not to me, who would never have sniffed out such things had I not learned them from God. This one thing I will add, with your good leave: this single distinction is enough to prove the true Trinity against all heretics and unbelievers. Moreover, Scripture is so open and everywhere so consistent with itself that no room for deceit is left to heretics. So that this distinction may cling more tenaciously to anyone, I have thought fit to set it before all to be viewed, as it were on a tablet, in these examples: The Father of the Word is the God of Israel. The Word is the God of Israel.

units.la: Hæ propositiones ambæ veræ sunt, sed conversiones non ambæ. Si quidem, Deus Israel est Pater Verbi, vera est: non autem,
units.tr: Both these propositions are true, but not both their converses. For the proposition that the God of Israel is the Father of the Word is true; but not

units.la: Deus Israel est Verbum. propterea quòd Verbum Filiationem & Essentiam designat: Deus autem Essentiam tantum, vt Pater. Quod ignorās Sabellius, confundit omnia, terram mari, mareque cælo permiscens.
units.tr: the proposition that the God of Israel is the Word. For the Word designates the Filiation and the Essence, whereas God designates the Essence only, as Father. Sabellius, not knowing this, confounds all things, mixing earth with sea and sea with sky.

units.la: Quamobrem optimi viri Dei, innocentiam meam etiam atque etiam vobis commendo. Equidem in tam optima causa nullum alium judicem quæro, præterquam ipsam Trinitatem, vosque etiam omnes. Quomodo enim qui verbo Dei nitor, Ministrorum fidelium Verbi Dei judicium recusabo? Vestrum igitur erit, de quæstione tam seria sententiam ferre. Equidem polliceor me (modò personas quas sustinetis, optima fide referatis) ne latum quidem unguem à vestra sententia discessurum. Valete viri Dei omnes in Domino, & me vestris precibus sedulò juvate, ipsumque dominum Caluinum æquiorem, si pote est, mihi reddite. Datum è carceribus.
units.tr: Wherefore, best men of God, I commend my innocence to you again and again. Indeed, in so good a cause I seek no other judge than the Trinity itself, and you all besides. For how, since I rest upon the Word of God, could I refuse the judgment of the faithful ministers of the Word of God? It will therefore be yours to pass sentence on so grave a question. For my part I promise that (provided you report the persons you represent in good faith) I shall not depart a hair's breadth from your sentence. Farewell, all you men of God, in the Lord; help me diligently with your prayers, and restore to me, if it can be, Lord Calvin himself more favourable. Given from the prisons.

units.la: Ego qui supra, Valentinus Gentilis, manu propria.
units.tr: I, the above-named Valentinus Gentilis, in my own hand.

units.la: Dominus Philippus Melanchthon vir nunquam satis laudatus, sol.53 Locorum communium,de Spiritu sancto agens: Necesse est, inquit, personam esse distinctam, quæ est aliquid Dei: quæ definitio, meo quidem judicio, ut maximè convenit Filio & Spiritui sancto, ita plurimum abhorret à Patre. Persona enim sive proprietas Patris non est aliquid Dei, sed est ipse unicus Deus, ipsamet Essentia: veluti quum ipse Deus dicit, Ioel 2, Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Nam sicut passim legere est in Scripturis sacris, Spiritus Dei, Christus Dei, Verbum Dei, Sermo erat apud Patrem: ita nusquam legitur, Pater Dei, Pater erat apud Deum. Quare recte ab Irenaeo & Tertulliano per Patrem seu Patris personam ubique unicus ille Deus atque Essentia ipsa designatur, ut in sequentibus sententiis licebit animadvertere.
units.tr: Lord Philip Melanchthon, a man never sufficiently praised, in his Commonplaces, treating of the Holy Spirit (sol.53): "It is necessary," he says, "that the person be distinct, which is something of God." This definition, in my judgment, fits the Son and the Holy Spirit very well, but is far removed from the Father. For the person or property of the Father is not something of God, but is the one God himself, the very Essence, as when God himself says, Joel 2, "I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh." For as one reads everywhere in the holy Scriptures, the Spirit of God, the Christ of God, the Word of God, "the Word was with the Father," so nowhere is it read "the Father of God," or "the Father was with God." Wherefore rightly, by Irenaeus and Tertullian, through the Father or the person of the Father that one God and the Essence itself is designated everywhere, as will be seen in the following sentences.

units.la: EX IRENÆO.
units.tr: FROM IRENAEUS.

units.la: Ex libro primo,sol.47.lite.A.
units.tr: From the first book, fol. 47, letter A.

units.la: Hic qui Deus est Abraham, Deus Isaac, & Deus Iacob, super quem alius Deus non est, neque initium, neque virtus, neque pleroma, hic Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Ex lib.2.Fol.66.lite.B.
units.tr: He who is the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, above whom there is no other God, nor beginning, nor power, nor pleroma: he is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. From book 2, fol. 66, letter B.

units.la: Quoniam autem hic Deus est Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, & de hoc Paulus Apostolus dixit, 1.Cor.8, Nobis tamen unus Deus Pater ille, ex quo omnia, & nos in illum. Fol.126.lite.A.
units.tr: Since, then, this one is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of him the Apostle Paul said (1 Cor. 8): "Yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and we are for him." Fol. 126, letter A.

units.la: Hic Deus Abraham, & Deus Isaac, & Deus Iacob, Deus viuorũ, quem & Lex annuntiat, quem Prophetæ præconizant, quem Spiritus reuelat, quem Apostoli tradunt, quem Ecclesia credidit: hic Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, per Verbum suum, qui est Filius eius, per eum reuelatur & manifestatur omnibus quibus reuelatur. Ex lib.3.sol.145.lite.A.
units.tr: This is the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of the living, whom the Law also proclaims, whom the Prophets foretell, whom the Spirit reveals, whom the Apostles hand down, whom the Church has believed: he is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who through his Word, which is his Son, is revealed and made manifest through him to all to whom he is revealed. From book 3, fol. 145, letter A.

units.la: Te igitur invoco Domine Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, Deus Iacob, (qui est & Israel) Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi: Deus qui per multitudinem misericordiæ tuæ & bene sensisti in nobis, ut te cognoscamus: qui fecisti cælum & terram, & dominaris omnium: qui es solus & verus Deus, super quem alius Deus non est. Fol.166.lite.B.
units.tr: So I call upon you, Lord God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob (who is also Israel), Father of our Lord Jesus Christ: God who, through the abundance of your mercy, have also been well pleased with us, that we might know you; who made heaven and earth, and rule over all things; who alone are the true God, above whom there is no other God. Fol. 166, letter B.

units.la: Sed cum omni fiducia Iudæis & Græcis prædicabat: Iudæis quidem Iesum, qui ab ipsis crucifixus est, esse Filium Dei: Iudicem viuorum & mortuorum: a Patre accepisse æternum regnum in Israel, quemadmodum ostendimus: Græcis vero, unum Deum, qui omnia fecit, & huius Filium Iesum Christum annuntiantes.
units.tr: But he preached with all confidence to Jews and Greeks: to the Jews, that Jesus, who was crucified by them, is the Son of God, the Judge of the living and the dead, who received from the Father the eternal kingdom in Israel, as we have shown; but to the Greeks, announcing one God, who made all things, and his Son Jesus Christ.

units.la: Fol.173.lit.A.
units.tr: Fol. 173, letter A.

units.la: Quoniam neminem alium Deum invocaverunt, vel Dominum nomina-verũt[?], qui veritatis fuerunt prædicatores, & Apostoli libertatis, nisi solum verum Deum Patrem, & Verbum eius.
units.tr: For they called upon no other God, nor named [the Lord?], those who were preachers of the truth and apostles of liberty, except only the true God the Father and his Word.

units.la: Fol.144.lit.A.lib.3.cap.6.
units.tr: Fol. 144, letter A, book 3, chapter 6.

units.la: Per Filium itaque, qui est in Patre, & habet in se Patrem, iis quibus est manifestatus, Patre testimonium præbente Filio, & Filio annuntiante Patrem. Perpendenda sunt hæc verba, Qui est in Patre, & Habet in se Patrem.
units.tr: Through the Son, then, who is in the Father and has the Father in himself, the Father bearing witness to those to whom he has been made manifest, and the Son announcing the Father. These words must be weighed: "who is in the Father" and "has the Father in himself".

units.la: Ex lib.4.cap.8.sol.211.lit.A.
units.tr: From book 4, chapter 8, fol. 211, letter A.

units.la: Et bene qui dixit, ipsum immensum Patrem in Filio mensuratum. Mensura enim Patris Filius, quoniam & capit eum.
units.tr: And he rightly said that the immeasurable Father is measured in the Son. For the Son is the measure of the Father, since he also contains him.

units.la: Hæc verba procul dubio Patrem Essentiatorem constituunt.
units.tr: Beyond doubt these words make the Father the one who gives being to all things.

units.la: Fol.276.lit.A.
units.tr: Fol. 276, letter A.

units.la: Unus ergo & idem Deus Pater, qui plantavit vineam, qui populum eduxit, qui Prophetas misit, qui Filium suum promisit, qui vineam dedit aliis colonis, iis qui reddunt fructum in temporibus suis.
units.tr: One and the same God the Father, therefore, who planted the vineyard, who led out the people, who sent the Prophets, who promised his Son, who gave the vineyard to other tenants, those who render the fruit in their seasons.

units.la: Ex lib.5.sol.326.lit.B.
units.tr: From book 5, fol. 326, letter B.

units.la: Ostendimus autem & in tertio libro, nullum ab Apostolis ex sua persona Deum appellari, nisi eum qui verè sit Deus Pater Domini nostri.
units.tr: But we have also shown in the third book that the Apostles never call anyone God in their own person, except him who is truly God the Father of our Lord.

units.la: EX TERTVLLIANO AD-VERSVS PRAXEAM.
units.tr: FROM TERTULLIAN, AGAINST PRAXEAS.

units.la: Fol.146.lit.C.
units.tr: Fol. 146, lit. C.

units.la: Quæcunque ergo substantia Sermonis fuit, illam dico personam, & illi nomen Filij vindico: & dum Filium agnosco, secundum à Patre defendo.
units.tr: Whatever the substance of the Word was, I call that a person, and I claim for it the name of Son. And while I acknowledge the Son, I maintain that he is second to the Father.

units.la: Ibidem, lit.G.
units.tr: Ibid., lit. G.

units.la: Non tamen divisione alium Filium à Patre, sed distinctione, quia non sit i-dem Pater & Filius vel modulo alius ab alio. Pater enim tota substantia est, Filius verò derivatio totius & portio.
units.tr: Yet the Son is not another from the Father by division but by distinction, because the Father and the Son are not the same, nor is one a different mode of the other. For the Father is the whole substance, but the Son is a derivation of the whole and a portion of it.

units.la: Hic substantiam posuit pro Essentia.
units.tr: Here he uses "substance" for "essence."

units.la: Fol.148.lit.C.
units.tr: Fol. 148, lit. C.

units.la: Consequens erit, ut invisibilem Patrem intelligamus pro plenitudine maie-statis: visibilem verò Filium agnoscamus pro modulo derivationis.
units.tr: It follows that we should understand the invisible Father as the fullness of majesty, but acknowledge the visible Son as a mode of derivation.

units.la: Solet enim Tertullianus personas Verbi & Spiritus sancti distinctas, sed in-dividuas ab Essentia, derivationes appellare, & quasi portiones totius: ita ta-men ut ea totum capiant ac complectantur.
units.tr: Tertullian usually calls the persons of the Word and of the Holy Spirit, which are distinct from the Essence yet inseparable from it, derivations, and as it were portions of the whole; yet in such a way that they take in and embrace the whole.

units.la: Fol.149.lit.F.
units.tr: Fol. 149, lit. F.

units.la: Non enim definit esse qui habet Filium, ipse vnicus, suo scilicet nomine, quoties sine Filio nominatur. Sine Filio autem nominatur, quum principaliter determinatur vt prima persona, quae ante Filij nomen erat proponenda. Quia Pater ante cognoscitur, & post Patrem Filius nominatur. Igitur vnus Pater, & absque eo alius non est.
units.tr: For he who has the Son is not himself ceasing to be the only one, under his own name, whenever he is named without the Son. He is named without the Son when he is principally designated as the first person, which must be set forth before the name of the Son. For the Father is known first, and the Son is named after the Father. Therefore there is one Father, and there is no other apart from him.

units.la: Etiam hic graphicè proprietatem Patris depingit.
units.tr: Here too he vividly portrays the property of the Father.

units.la: Fol.152.lit.A.
units.tr: Fol. 152, lit. A.

units.la: Sicut ergo Sermo Dei nō est ipse cuius est: ita nec Spiritus, etsi Deus dictus, non tamen ipse est cuius est dictus. Nulla res alicuius ipsa est cuius est. Planè quum quid ex ipso est, & sic eius est, dum ex ipso sit, potestate quid esse, quale & ipse ex quo est, & cuius est. Et ideò Spiritus Deus, & Sermo Deus, quia in Deo: non tamen ipse ex quo est. Quòd Deus Dei tanquam substantiua res non erit ipse Deus, sed hactenus Deus, quia ex ipsius Dei substantia: quae & substantiua res est, & vt portio aliqua totius.
units.tr: Therefore, just as the Word of God is not the very one whose Word he is, so neither is the Spirit, although he is called God, the very one whose Spirit he is called. No thing is the very thing of which it is. Clearly, when something comes from another and so belongs to it, it is by that power that it is what it is, of the same kind as the one from whom it comes and whose it is. And so the Spirit is God, and the Word is God, because they are in God; yet they are not themselves that from which they come. Since God is not the substance of God as a substantial thing, he will not be God himself, but is God only so far as he is from the substance of God himself, which is also a substantial thing and as it were a portion of the whole.

units.la: EX EODEM IN LIBRO de Trinitate.
units.tr: FROM THE SAME BOOK, On the Trinity.

units.la: Fol.234.lit.M.de Patre differens.
units.tr: Fol. 234, letter M, differing concerning the Father.

units.la: Henoc transtulit, in amicitiae societatem Abraham adlegit, Isaac protexit, Iacob auxit, Mosen ducem populo praefecit, ingemiscentes filios Israel è iugo seruitutis eripuit, Legem scripsit, Patrum sobolem in terram repromissionis induxit, Prophetas Spiritu instruxit, & per hos omnes Filium suum Christum repromisit, & quando daturum se spopondit, misit.
units.tr: Henoch he translated; he chose Abraham into the fellowship of friendship; he protected Isaac; he increased Jacob; he set Moses over the people as leader; he snatched the groaning sons of Israel from the yoke of servitude; he wrote the Law; he led the offspring of the Fathers into the promised land; he instructed the Prophets by the Spirit; and through all of these he promised his Son Christ again, and when he had promised he would give him, he sent him.

units.la: Fol.235.lit.D.
units.tr: Fol. 235, letter D.

units.la: Eadem regula veritatis docet nos credere post Patrem etiam in Filium Dei Christum Iesum Dominum Deum nostrum: sed Dei Filium, huius Dei qui & vnus & solus est, conditor scilicet rerum omnium.
units.tr: The same rule of truth teaches us to believe, after the Father, also in the Son of God, Christ Jesus, our Lord God; but the Son of God, of this God who is both one and alone, namely the maker of all things.

units.la: Fol.236.lit.B.
units.tr: Fol. 236, letter B.

units.la: Hæc enim cōtumelia hæreticorum ad ipsum quoque Deum Patrem redundabit, si Deus Pater Filium Deum generare non potuit.
units.tr: For this insult of the heretics will also fall back upon God the Father himself, if God the Father could not beget a God as Son.

units.la: Ibidem, litera D.
units.tr: Ibidem, letter D.

units.la: Vt enim præscripsit ipsa natura, hominem credendum esse qui ex homine sit: ita & Scriptura Deum esse, qui ex Deo sit.
units.tr: For just as nature itself has laid down that the one who is from a man must be believed to be a man, so Scripture teaches that the one who is from God must be God.

units.la: Fol.237.lit.M.
units.tr: Fol. 237, letter M.

units.la: Quique Sermo caro factus habuit[?] in nobis, ex nobis hic Christus non homo tātum, quia hominis filius, sed etiam Deus, quia Filius Dei comprobatur.
units.tr: And this Christ, the Word made flesh, who dwelt among us, from among us, is not only man, because he is the Son of man, but also God, because he is proved to be the Son of God.

units.la: Fol.138.lit.I.
units.tr: Fol. 138, letter I.

units.la: Quum ratio & temperamentum Scripturarum caelestium Christum ostendat Deum, sed quem Filium Dei, & assumpto à Deo etiam Filio hominis, credendum & hominem.
units.tr: Since the reason and the tenor of the heavenly Scriptures show Christ to be God, but God as Son of God, and, since the Son of God has taken on flesh, man is also to be believed.

units.la: Fol.239.lit.M.
units.tr: Fol. 239, letter M.

units.la: Quandoquidem non tam veteris quàm noui Testamenti Scriptura diuina vbique ostendat illum ex Patre genitum, per quem facta sunt omnia, & sine quo factum est nihil, qui obedierit semper Patri, & obediat, semper habentem rerum omnium potestatem, sed quam traditam, sed quam concessam, sed quam à Patre proprie sibi indultam.
units.tr: Since the divine Scripture shows everywhere, not only of the Old Testament but of the New, that he was begotten of the Father, through whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made, who always obeyed the Father and still obeys him, always having the power of all things, but a power handed on, granted, and bestowed upon him by the Father as his own.

units.la: Fol.240.lit.E.
units.tr: Fol. 240, letter E.

units.la: Missum præterea esse dicit, vt hanc obedientiam, qua venit Dominus Christus missus, non Pater, sed Filius probetur. Qui misisset vtique, si Pater fuisset. Missus autem non fuit Pater, ne Pater subditus alteri Deo, dum mittitur, probaretur.
units.tr: Furthermore, it says that he was sent, so that this obedience, by which the Lord Christ came as one sent, might be shown to belong to the Son and not to the Father. For the one who sent would surely have been the Father. But the Father was not sent, lest the Father be shown to be subject to another God, while he is sent.

units.la: Fol.241.lit.A.
units.tr: Fol. 241, letter A.

units.la: Quomodo enim ego & Pater vnum sumus, si non Deus est & Filius? Qui idcirco vnum potest dici dum ex ipso est, & dū Filius eius est, & dum ex ipso nascitur, dum ex ipso processisse reperitur, per quem & Deus est.
units.tr: For how are I and the Father one, if he is not God and Son? He can therefore be called one, in that he is from him, and in that he is his Son, and in that he is born from him, and in that he is found to have proceeded from him, through whom he is also God.

units.la: Ibidem, litera B.
units.tr: Ibidem, letter B.

units.la: Deus est ergo. Deus autem sic, vt Filius sit, non Pater.
units.tr: He is God, then. But he is God in such a way that he is the Son, not the Father.

units.la: Fol.242.lite.C.
units.tr: Fol. 242, letter C.

units.la: Imago est enim inuisibilis Dei, vt mediocritas & fragilitas conditionis humanæ Deum Patrem videre aliquando iam tunc assuesceret in imagine Dei. Gradatim enim & per incrementa humana fragilitas nutriri debuit per imaginem ad istam gloriam, vt Deum Patrem videre posset aliquando. Pericula enim sunt quæ magna sunt, si repentina sunt.
units.tr: For he is the invisible image of God, so that the mediocrity and frailty of the human condition might grow accustomed, even then, to seeing God the Father in the image of God at some time. For human frailty had to be nourished step by step, through increments, by the image, up to that glory, so that it might at some time be able to see God the Father. For dangers are great if they are sudden.

units.la: Ibidem, lite.E
units.tr: Ibidem, letter E.

units.la: Quomodo ergo Deus erit, si Angelus fuerit, quum non sit hoc nomen Angelis vnquam concessum, nisi quoniam ex vtroque latere nos veritas in istam concludit sententiam, quia debeamus intelligere Dei Filiu fuisse, qui quoniam ex Deo, est merito Deus, quia Dei Filius dictus sit: quoniam annuntiator paternæ voluntatis est, magni consilij Angelus pronuntiatus est.
units.tr: How then will he be God, if he was an angel, since this name was never granted to angels, except that truth from both sides leads us to this conclusion: that we ought to understand him to be the Son of God, who, since he is from God, is rightly God, because he is called the Son of God; and since he is the announcer of the Father's will, he is proclaimed the Angel of great counsel.

units.la: Fol.243.lite.A.
units.tr: Fol. 243, letter A.

units.la: Hic autem qui ista promittit, Deus atque Angelus esse perhibetur, vt mevitò distinctio sit inter eum, qui non Deus simpliciter, sed & Angelus pronuntiatur.
units.tr: Moreover, the one who makes these promises is said to be God and Angel, so that there is rightly a distinction between him who is not God simply, but is also proclaimed as Angel.

units.la: Fol.24r.lite.E.
units.tr: Fol. 24r, letter E.

units.la: Est ergo Deus Pater omnium institutor & creator, solus originem nescies, inuisibilis, immensus, immortalis, æternus, unus Deus: cuius neque magnitudini, neque maiestati, neque virtuti quicquam, non dixerim præferri, sed nec comparari potest.
units.tr: God the Father, therefore, is the founder and creator of all things, alone without origin, invisible, immeasurable, immortal, eternal, one God; to whose greatness, majesty, and power nothing can be preferred, I will not say, but nor even compared.

units.la: Ibidem, lit.G.
units.tr: Ibidem, letter G.

units.la: Deus utique procedens ex Deo, secundum personam efficiens, sed non eri-piens illud Patri, quòd unus est Deus.
units.tr: God indeed, proceeding from God, efficient according to person, but not snatching from the Father that he is the one God.

units.la: Ibidem, lit.I.
units.tr: Ibidem, letter I.

units.la: Nam quum id sit principium cæteris, quod ingenitum, Deus solus Pater est, qui extra originem est, ex quo hic est qui genitus est.
units.tr: For since that which is unbegotten is the principle of all others, God the Father alone is the one who is outside origin, from whom is the one who is begotten.

units.la: Ibidem, lit.K.
units.tr: Ibidem, letter K.

units.la: Deus quidem ostenditur Filius, cui diuinitas tradita & porrecta conspicitur. Et tamen nihilominus unus Deus Pater probatur.
units.tr: God indeed is shown to be the Son, to whom divinity is seen to be handed over and extended. And yet, nevertheless, one God the Father is proved.

units.la: Si singulas sententias quæ pro me faciunt, calamo persequi vellem, ingens mihi opus scribendum esset. Nullus enim extat doctor, quin aliquando hanc meam sententiam non attigerit, etiam ipse dominus Caluinus. Sed quando Irenæus & Tertullianus videntur ex professo illam tueri, cæteris relictis, his contentus esse volui. Res est maximi momenti, optimi viri Dei. Agitur enim de cognitione veri Patris, & de vera cognitione Filij & Spiritus sancti: quorum veram gloriam & maiestatem si quisquam alius tuendam susceperit, vos probè scio usque ad supremam guttulam sanguinis tuiturum. Quamobrem, optimi viri Dei, vestrum est, prius quàm sententiam feratis, hæsce authoritates diligenter dispicere, locos Scripturarum perpendere, & vestram operam unico illi Deo bona fide præstare. Sic enim facientes, pro certo habeo, tot monstra, quæ tandiu Trinitatem invaserunt, Spiritu Dei qui habitat in vobis, vos facilè interemptu-ros: ipsamque Trinitatem, tot hactenus impetitam blasphemiis & con-spurcatam, in pristinum suum nitorem ac candorem vindicaturos. Quòd si qui meam distin-ctionem reijciunt, veram illam quidem, & Sacris literis apprimè consentaneam, ipsi suam in lucem proferant. Nam quæ vanitas est hæc, distin-ctionem asserere, & interim nullam proferre? Expecto igitur magno cum desyderio vestrum oraculum, imò Dei per vos. Valete Christiani Hercules, ve-rique heroes, non immemores captiuitatis mee[?]. E carceribus.
units.tr: If I wished to pursue with my pen each of the sentences that favour me, I would have a huge work to write. For there is no teacher who has not at some time touched upon this view of mine, not even the lord Calvin himself. But since Irenaeus and Tertullian seem to defend it expressly, I wished to be content with these, leaving the rest aside. The matter is of the greatest importance, best men of God. For it concerns the knowledge of the true Father, and the true knowledge of the Son and the Holy Spirit; and if anyone else has undertaken to defend their true glory and majesty, I know well that you will defend them to the last drop of blood. Therefore, best men of God, it is your task, before you pronounce your judgment, to examine these authorities diligently, to weigh the passages of Scripture, and to render your labour in good faith to that one God. For if you do this, I am certain that you will easily destroy, by the Spirit of God who dwells in you, the many monsters that have so long assailed the Trinity, and that you will vindicate the Trinity, hitherto so often attacked with blasphemies and defiled, to its former brightness and purity. But if those who reject my distinction should do so, let them bring forward their own, which is indeed true and most consonant with the sacred letters. For what vanity is this, to assert a distinction and meanwhile to produce none? I therefore await your oracle with great desire, or rather that of God through you. Farewell, Christian Hercules and true heroes, not forgetful of my captivity. From the prisons.

units.la: HAEC tum ille. Nos vero postridie scripto quoque respondimus, in eum qui sequitur modum:
units.tr: So he spoke then. But we also replied in writing the next day, in the following manner:

units.la: Antehac putauimus errore te labi ac ignorantia: nūc ex postremo tuo sermone & scripto deprehendimus & peruersi ingenij hominem, & fastus intolerabilis, & virulentiæ deditum, & maligno spiritu imbutum, denique hæreticum peruicacem. Quod non dicimus conuitiandi causa, sed vt hanc prauitatem exuere discas, & ad docilitatem flectaris: quia initiu[?] resipiscentiæ tuæ erit (si tamen resipiscere tibi dabitur) modestia & humilitas cum sincero pietatis studio coniuncta. Zelum apud nos martyris Christi frustra obtendis, quem perspicimus mera arrogantia fuisse adductum, vt impium errorem & absurdissimum obtruderes.
units.tr: We had earlier thought that you were slipping into error through ignorance. Now, from your last speech and writing, we perceive that you are a man of a perverse mind, of intolerable pride, given to virulence, imbued with an evil spirit, and in short a stubborn heretic. We do not say this for the sake of insult, but so that you may learn to cast off this wickedness and be turned to docility; for the beginning of your repentance will be (if indeed it is granted you to repent) modesty and humility joined with a sincere zeal for piety. You vainly put forward before us the zeal of the martyr of Christ, which we see was prompted by mere arrogance, so that you might thrust forth an impious and most absurd error.

units.la: Plausibile tibi est principium illud, Deum Israel, quem Sacræ literæ asserunt, verum Deum, esse Patrem Iesu Christi: ipsum vero Christū esse vnici Dei Filium. Atqui clarè apparet, quū Patrem opponis Filio, & vni duntaxat veram Deitatem tribuis, te excludere alterum, quem cum illo confers. Nos quoque ingenuè fatemur, non alium esse Deum, quàm Deum Israel: & hunc Deum esse Patrem Christi. Sed tunc nō opponimus inter se Patrem & Filium, ac si in solo Patre esset Dei Essentia: sed eadem ratione qua docemus Patrem Christi esse Deum Abraham, Isaac & Iacob, sequitur Christum esse illum eundem Deum. Hic diligenter expende quò impingas, dum in cōparatione fingis duo antithe-ta. Exclames licet Christū à te agnosci verum Deum, si solus eius Pater est u-nicus Deus & Deus Israel, non obscurè deiicis eum è gradu in quo Patrem u-num eius respectu locas. Facessat antithesis inter Patrem & Filium, tibi nobis-cum non male cōueniet: quia quum una sit utriusque Essentia, in Patre inclu-sus est Filius, vbi fit Deitatis mentio.
units.tr: That principle is plausible for you: that the God of Israel, whom the sacred letters declare to be the true God, is the Father of Jesus Christ, and that Christ himself is the Son of the only God. Yet it is clear that when you set the Father over against the Son, and attribute true Deity to the one alone, you exclude the other, whom you compare with him. We too frankly confess that there is no other God than the God of Israel, and that this God is the Father of Christ. But we do not then set the Father and the Son against each other, as if the Essence of God were in the Father alone; rather, by the same reasoning by which we teach that the Father of Christ is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, it follows that Christ is that same God. Consider carefully where you are driving, when in your comparison you invent two opposed terms. You may cry out that Christ is acknowledged by you as true God, but if his Father alone is the only God and the God of Israel, you do not obscurely throw him down from the rank in which, with respect to him, you place the one Father. Let the antithesis between Father and Son cease, and you will agree not badly with us; for since the Essence of both is one, the Son is included in the Father wherever mention is made of the Deity.

units.la: Venenū erroris quod vafrè occultas, sic melius detegetur. Deus qui Isaiæ ap-paruit, fuit verus Deus Israel, & unicus Deus. Hunc Ioannes affirmat fuisse Christum. Deus qui pronūtiat per Isaiam, se fore in lapidem offendiculi Iudæis, fuit unicus Israelis Deus: Paulus Christū fuisse docet. Qui per Isaiam clamat, Vivo ego, mihi flectetur omne genu: certè solus verus Deus fuit. Atqui idem Paulus Christum interpretatur. Nec verò quæ recitat Apostolus testimonia, nisi in unicum Israelis Deum cōpetunt, Tu Deus fundasti terram, &c. Hinc clarè colligimus, æternum Dei Sermonem illum fuisse Israelis Deum. Si excipias hoc te fateri, quid tu futiliter in utramque partem garrias, nō curamus: quia interim manet convicta hæc impietas, Solum Patrem esse Deum verum.
units.tr: The poison of error that you craftily conceal will be exposed more clearly in this way. The God who appeared to Isaiah was the true God of Israel and the only God. John affirms that this God was Christ. The God who declares through Isaiah that he will be a stone of stumbling to the Jews was the only God of Israel, and Paul teaches that this was Christ. He who cries out through Isaiah, "As I live, every knee shall bow to me," was certainly the only true God. Yet Paul interprets this of Christ. Nor do the testimonies the Apostle cites fit anyone but the one God of Israel: "You, God, founded the earth," and so on. From this we clearly gather that the eternal Word of God was the God of Israel. If you except this and admit it, why do you chatter futilely on both sides? We do not care, for meanwhile this impiety, that the Father alone is the true God, remains refuted.

units.la: Concidit etiam alter ille non minus detestabilis error, In solo Patre esse Essentiam. Nam qui in locis nuper citatis ponatur nomen Jehouae, sequitur Filium Dei ex seipso esse, solius Deitatis respectu. Nam si est Jehova, negari non potest quin idem sit ille Deus, qui per Jsaiam alibi clamat, Ego, ego sum: & praeter me non est Deus. Utile etiam tibi esset expendere quid illud Jeremiae sibi velit, Dij qui non fecerunt caelum & terram, pereant de terra quae sub caelo est. Nisi enim palam maledicere velis Filio Dei, fateri necesse erit, illum esse cuius Deitas saepius apud Jsaiam probatur ex mundi creatione. Quomodo autem Creator qui omnibus esse dat, non erit ex seipso, sed Essentiam aliunde quasi precario mutuabitur? Neque est quod fucum hic facere tentes, de aeterna Filij generatione te nobis subscribere. Nam quum Essentiatum a Patre dicis, a seipso esse negas. Reclamat ex opposito Spiritus sanctus, illum Jehoua nominans. Jam si tota Essentia est in solo Patre: vel tu eam partibilem nobis fingis, vel eripies eam Filio. Utcunque nunc centies concedas esse verum Deum, spoliatus tamen sua Essentia, titularis solum erit Deus. Hic attende rursus, an non vel Essentiam Diuinam Filio detrahat, vel deriuationem partis a toto somniet, quisquis Essentiam in Patre loco personae substituit. Essentia Dei secundum te soli Patri competit, quatenus ipse solus est, & est Filij Essentiator. Ubi erit Diuinitas Filij, si est aliquid abstractum a Dei Essentia? Jam de Spiritu sancto quid dices? Si enim solus Pater Essentiator est, non erit communis Patris & Filij Spiritus. Vis personam Spiritus nihil aliud esse, quàm deriuationem a prima Essentia, quae Patri uni propria est. Hinc tibi extorquebitur a solo Patre esse Spiritum, & perperam a Paulo, Rom.cap.8. vocari Spiritum Christi. Videsne ut tua deliria quasi multiplices laquei te inuoluant, adeoque strangulent?
