units.la: R. Maior non est firma. Nam dicere de essentia, non tollit Trinitate personarum. Per calumniam igitur hanc loquutionem lacerant noui Ariani. Quando enim dicitur, Vna est essentia, Vnus Deus, non fit exclusio personarum ab hac Vnitate, seu Deitate. Nam tali modo est vnicus Deus, vt tamen sit Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus. Item, etsi sit vnicus tantum Deus, tamen personæ non sunt confusæ. Hic est articulus non rationis, sed fidei. Ad Minorem. Naturam diuinam siue Deitatem, sicut & ipsi noui Ariani loquuntur, dicimus esse Vnam, communem illis tribus, Patri, Filio, & Spiritui sancto. Sed tres illi ita distinguntur, vt sit Pater, sit Filius, sit Spiritus sanctus, qui tres sunt tres existentes, necsunt confundendæ. Pater non est Filius, neque Filius Pater, neque Spiritus sanctus vel Pater, vel Filius. Nam scriptu-ra sacra inquit, esse tres. Nihilominus isti tres, vt dictum est, nō sunt plures Dii, sed sunt vnicus & verus Deus, contra omnem Arithmeticam & ratiocina-tionem omnium hominum. Quia de Deo sentiendum & loquendum est, sicu-ti in Verbo certo est traditum & patefactum.
units.tr: R. The major premise is not sound. For to speak of essence does not remove the Trinity of persons. The new Arians therefore tear this expression apart by calumny. When it is said, "there is one essence, one God," no exclusion of persons from this unity or Deity is made. For God is so one that he is yet Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Likewise, although God is only one, the persons are not confused. This is an article not of reason but of faith. To the minor: we say that the divine nature or Deity, as the new Arians themselves also speak, is one, common to those three, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. But those three are so distinguished that there is the Father, there is the Son, there is the Holy Spirit, three who exist as three, and they are not to be confused. The Father is not the Son, nor the Son the Father, nor the Holy Spirit either the Father or the Son. For holy Scripture says there are three. Nevertheless these three, as has been said, are not several Gods, but are the one and true God, against all arithmetic and all human reasoning, because we must think and speak of God as it has been certainly handed down and revealed in the Word.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Qui docet vnum esse Deum essentia, & trinum in personis, conatur vnum & verum Deum Patrem, cum vnigenito eius Filio abolere.
units.tr: Whoever teaches that God is one in essence and three in persons tries to abolish, together with his only-begotten Son, the one and true God the Father.

units.la: Sed vos hoc facitis.
units.tr: But you do this.

units.la: Ergo tantum nefas committitis.
units.tr: Therefore you commit such a great crime.

units.la: R. Maior nullam habet connexionem, & salsissima est. Nascitur autem ex illa calumnia Arianorum, quemadmodum & pleraque alia argumenta, quòd dicant scholastici, Essentiam non generare. Sed vsque ad fastidium hoc inculcandum est. Quando Ecclesia Christi vnitatem profitetur, nō excludit tres personas: quando trinitatem docet, non excludit vnitatem. Verum isti criminatores essentiam à tribus personis maliciose diuellunt, ac reuera diaboli artem imitantur, qui mutilata dicta Christo obiiciebat. Sic isti spiritus, tantum hanc partem arripiunt, Vna est Essentia diuina, quæ tamen concordat cum hac oratione, Vnus est Deus. Alterum verò, quod additur in Ecclesia orthodoxa, Tres esse, Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum, & hosce tres esse vnum, vt inquit Iohannes, seu vnum Deum: nam id vult Apostolus: id inquam isti Nebulones omittunt. Ita carpunt priorem partem eius doctrinæ, & posteriorem, sine qua prior illa pars non existit, prætergrediuntur. De Scholasticorum autem sententia antea diximus.
units.tr: R. The major premise has no connection and is very silly. It arises from that calumny of the Arians, as do many of their other arguments, that the scholastics say the essence does not beget. But this must be pressed home until it is tiresome. When the Church of Christ professes unity, it does not exclude the three persons; when it teaches the Trinity, it does not exclude unity. But these accusers wickedly tear the essence away from the three persons, and truly imitate the art of the devil, who threw mutilated sayings at Christ. So these spirits seize only this part, "there is one divine essence," which nevertheless agrees with the statement "there is one God." But the other part, which is added in the orthodox Church, that there are three, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and that these three are one, as John says, or one God (for this is what the Apostle means), these scoundrels omit. Thus they pick at the former part of that doctrine and pass over the latter, without which the former part does not stand. But we have already spoken of the opinion of the scholastics.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Qui quatuor constituunt personas diuinitatis, impiè faciunt.
units.tr: Those who posit four persons of the Godhead act impiously.

units.la: Sed qui vnicum dicunt esse Deum, & tamen tres personas, quatuor faciunt personas.
units.tr: But those who say God is one and yet three persons make four persons.

units.la: Ergo quaternitatem asseritis.
units.tr: Therefore you assert a quaternity.

units.la: R. Minor est salsissima. Nam verbum Dei docet vnicū esse Deum, & hos tres, Patrem, & Filium, & Spiritum sanctum esse vnicum illum Deum, Itaque nō sunt quatuor personæ, sed tres tantùm personæ, quæ tres persona sunt unicus & verus Deus. In hac parte isti Ariani sacrae scripturae bellum inferunt, & sine causa blasphemant. Nam Minor non habet ullam firmam ratiocinationem.
units.tr: R. The minor is very silly. For the Word of God teaches that God is one, and that these three, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, are that one God. So there are not four persons but only three persons, which three persons are the one and true God. In this matter these Arians wage war on holy Scripture and blaspheme without cause. For the minor has no firm reasoning.

units.la: Similes ineptias gignunt, quando dicunt, Scriptura inquit, Tres sunt unus. Ergo unus Deus non est trinus. Observet Lector vertiginosos istos spiritus, contra manifestissimum textum insanientes, & blasphema verba ex impuris palatis eructantes.
units.tr: They produce similar absurdities when they say: Scripture says, "three are one." Therefore one God is not three. Let the reader observe these dizzy spirits, raving against the most manifest text and belching blasphemous words from impure palates.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Sabellius ita docuit, genitorem, genitum & procedentem, esse Trinomium. Ergo vos estis haeretici.
units.tr: Sabellius taught that the begetter, the begotten and the proceeding are a threefold name. Therefore you are heretics.

units.la: R. Vide quid faciat calumnia? Nō dicimus nominetenus tantum esse tres, ut Sabellius insaniebat: sed Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum esse tres res existentes, non spectra quaedam, non diversum habitum, gestus aut repraesentationem unius duntaxat personae, sed tamen istas tres res esse unum Deum, non plures. Non quidem iuxta caliginosam cuiusquam hominis mentem, sed iuxta Verbum Dei, quod credendum est, licet omnis omnium creaturarum ratio, hoc mysterium divinum, nempe QUOMODO Deus sit Unus, & tamen tres sint personae istius Unici Dei, assequi & explicare nequeat.
units.tr: R. See what calumny does! We do not say that there are three merely in name, as Sabellius raved, but that the Father, Son and Holy Spirit are three existing realities, not certain phantoms, not a different habit, gesture or representation of one person only. Yet these three realities are one God, not more. This is not according to the clouded mind of any man, but according to the Word of God, which must be believed, although the reason of every creature cannot grasp or explain this divine mystery, namely HOW God is one, and yet there are three persons of that one God.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Patres, qui statim post Apostolos vixerunt, docuerunt Unum Deum esse Patrem, non dixerunt Filium & Spiritum sanctum cum Patre esse illum uni cum Deum, aut trinum esse Unum, &c.
units.tr: The Fathers who lived immediately after the Apostles taught that the one God is the Father; they did not say that the Son and the Holy Spirit with the Father are that one God, or that the one is three, etc.

units.la: Ergo vos erratis.
units.tr: Therefore you err.

units.la: R. Nequiter & maliciose hosce Patres citatis. Nam Martialis ad Burdegalenses inquit, Sola trinitas in divinitate Unitatis seipsam novit. Ite, Rursum trinitate in Unitate designavit. Item, Vobis Unus & idem Deus, qui cuncta creavit, Pater: & Unus & idem Dominus, per quem omnia facta sunt, Filius eius Iesus Christus: & Unus idèque Deus Spiritus sanctus, in quo omnia subsistūt. Et haec in PERSONIS tria divisa, in divinitate UNUS Deo indivisus est
units.tr: R. You cite these Fathers wickedly and maliciously. For Martial, to the Burdegalenses, says: "The Trinity alone has known itself in the divinity of Unity." Again: "He has designated the Trinity in Unity." Also: "For you there is one and the same God, who created all things, the Father; and one and the same Lord, through whom all things were made, his Son Jesus Christ; and one and so God the Holy Spirit, in whom all things subsist. And these three, divided in PERSONS, are in the divinity one God, undivided."

units.la: Arnobius super Psal. 134. inquit: Ita Trinitatem in una Deitate coniungit, ut tres verè dicam esse personas, & unam verè dicā esse substantiam. Epiphanius lib. 2. tomo. 1. Confitemur Trinitatem, Unitatem in Trinitate, & Trinitatem in Unitate, Unam Deitatem Patris, Filii & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Arnobius on Psalm 134 says: "So he joins the Trinity in one Deity, that I may truly say there are three persons, and I may truly say one substance." Epiphanius, book 2, tome 1: "We confess a Trinity, a Unity in the Trinity, and a Trinity in the Unity, one Deity of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit."

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Ubicunque sunt variae loquutiones de eadem re, ibi est error.
units.tr: Wherever there are various expressions about the same thing, there is error.

units.la: Vestrae loquutiones de Deo variant. Ergo erratis de Deo.
units.tr: Your expressions about God vary. Therefore you err about God.

units.la: Minor probatur, quia dicitis, Unum esse Deum essentia, & trinum per-onis. Item, In Deo esse distinctas personas. Item alius aliter vocabula Essen-tia & Substantia interpretatur.
units.tr: The minor premise is proved, because you say that God is one in essence and three in persons. Likewise, that there are distinct persons in God. Likewise, that different men interpret the words essence and substance differently.

units.la: R. Maior falsa est. Nam ubi verborum variatio non mutat res ipsas, ibi non est error. Eandem rem aliis verbis Prophetæ, aliis Christus, aliis Apostoli exponunt, & tamen congruunt in rebus, neque sunt hæretici.
units.tr: Reply: The major premise is false. For where a variation of words does not change the things themselves, there is no error. The prophets, Christ and the apostles express the same thing in different words, and yet they agree in the things and are not heretics.

units.la: Ad Minorem: In rebus est consensus, licet verba & declarationes interdum varient. Alius enim alio clarius loquitur: sic interpretationes aliæ sunt concinniores aliis. Attamen in unico quasi scopo collimat, nempè ut asserant unum esse Deum, & Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum esse illum Unicum Deum. Si qui vero hæc res peruertunt (id quod nefariè audent isti noui Ariani) illi sine omni dubitatione iudicandi sunt hæretici, præsertim si moniti per-tinaciter in erroribus persistant.
units.tr: As to the minor premise: there is agreement in the things, although the words and explanations sometimes vary. For one speaks more clearly than another, and so some explanations are more elegant than others. Yet they all aim at one and the same goal, namely that God is one, and that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are that one God. If anyone perverts this matter, as these new Arians wickedly dare to do, such people are without any doubt to be judged heretics, especially if, when warned, they persist stubbornly in their errors.

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: Absurda non sunt asserenda.
units.tr: Absurd things must not be asserted.

units.la: Si Christus ideo unus Deus est cum Patre, quia est unius naturæ, unus erit idem Christus cum Abrahamo patre suo, quia unius naturæ est cum illo. Nota hæc verba.
units.tr: If Christ is one God with the Father because he is of one nature, then Christ will be one with Abraham his father, because he is of one nature with him. Note these words.

units.la: Ideo Christus non est unus Deus cum Patre.
units.tr: Therefore Christ is not one God with the Father.

units.la: R. Ecce hisce verbis isti spiritus, veluti ex opaca sua spelunca caput exe-runt, atque declarant, sese caput Arii ex stygia palude iterum in hanc lucem proferre. Nam impudentissimo ore effutire non verentur, Christum non esse unũ Deum cum Patre. Sed cur ipse Christus inquit Iohan.10. Ego & Pater UNUM sumus? Cur dicit Iohan.14. Pater in me est, & ego in Patre? Cur Thomas inquit, Dominus meus & Deus meus? Cur Iohannes docet, Hi TRES, nempe Pater, λόγος & Spiritus sanctus, UNUM sunt?
units.tr: Reply: Look, with these words these spirits thrust their heads, as it were, out of their dark cave, and show that they are bringing the head of Arius back into this light from the Stygian marsh. For they are not ashamed to babble with the most shameless mouth that Christ is not one God with the Father. But why does Christ himself say in John 10, "I and the Father are ONE"? Why does he say in John 14, "The Father is in me, and I in the Father"? Why does Thomas say, "My Lord and my God"? Why does John teach that "these THREE, namely the Father, the λόγος and the Holy Spirit, are ONE"?

units.la: Deinde ad Maiorem respondendum est. In rebus diuinis alia sunt absur-da fidei, alia rationis. Absurda fidei sunt, quæ in sacris literis non sunt tradi-ta. Ea verò vitanda & fugienda sunt. Absurda verò rationis, in sacris literis caveri nequeunt. Nam fidei articuli omnes, coram ratione hominum sunt ab-surdi, eámque ob causam credendi, non sapientia hominum æstimandi sunt.
units.tr: Next, the major premise must be answered. In divine matters some things are absurd to faith, others to reason. Things absurd to faith are those not handed down in Holy Scripture. These must indeed be avoided and shunned. But things absurd to reason cannot be avoided in Holy Scripture. For all the articles of faith are absurd before the reason of men, and for that very reason they are to be believed, not weighed by human wisdom.

units.la: Tertiò ad Minorem: Amentes Ariani à rebus humanis ad diuinas argu-mentatur, in quibus est diuersissima ratio: id quod omnes sana mente præditi norunt. Insuper rectissimè sequitur, Christus est ex sanguine Abrahæ pro-geatus[?], Ergo est verus homo, & habet carnem, sanguinem, animam, perinde vt Pater Abraham, licet persona distincta sit, & non sit peccato originali aut actuali exsese depravatus, vt Abraham. Sic etiam optima & firmissima consequentia dicitur, Filius est genitus à Patre, Ergo Filius est Deus, est coessentialis Patri. Praeterea nihil potest esse de essentia Patris, seu eiusdem naturæ, vel coessentiale Patri, quomodocunque alicui libeat efferre, quod nō sit Deus.
units.tr: Thirdly, as to the minor premise: the mad Arians argue from human things to divine ones, in which the reasoning is most dissimilar, as all people of sound mind know. Moreover, it follows most rightly that Christ is descended from the blood of Abraham; therefore he is a true man and has flesh, blood and soul, just as Abraham the father [had them], although he is a distinct person, and is not himself wholly corrupted by original or actual sin, as Abraham was. So also the best and firmest inference is stated: the Son is begotten of the Father; therefore the Son is God and is coessential with the Father. Furthermore, nothing can be of the essence of the Father, or of the same nature, or coessential with the Father, however anyone may choose to put it, that is not God.

units.la: XXI.
units.tr: XXI.

units.la: Ordo est inter mittentem & missum.
units.tr: There is an order between the one who sends and the one who is sent.

units.la: Ergo non est Deus trinus.
units.tr: Therefore God is not triune.

units.la: R. Ab ordine ad essentiam nulla est firma consequentia. Nam ordo distinctus non tollit communem essentiam siue deitatem. Regula enim est, Alia dicta scripturæ loquuntur de essentia Dei, alia de ordine atque de officio. Hoc verò in loco disputatio est de Deitate siue de essentia Dei præcipuè, non de ordine seu officio. Debebant igitur hic allegari talia dicta, quæ proprie & perspicuè de ipsa Essentia loquerentur.
units.tr: Reply: From order to essence there is no sound inference. For a distinct order does not remove the common essence or deity. The rule is this: some sayings of Scripture speak of the essence of God, others of order and of office. But in this place the dispute is chiefly about the Deity, or the essence of God, not about order or office. Therefore such sayings should have been cited here as speak properly and plainly about the essence itself.

units.la: XXII.
units.tr: XXII.

units.la: Deus vult inuocari per Filium.
units.tr: God wills to be invoked through the Son.

units.la: Ergo Deus non est trinus.
units.tr: Therefore God is not triune.

units.la: R. Nulla est connexio, éstque impostura, secundum non causam vt causam. Nam dicta de inuocatione, non loquuntur de ipsa essentia Dei: verùm de officio. Sic autem se Deus reuelauit, quòd solus Filius, non Pater, sit factus homo & victima pro peccatis totius mundi. Constitutus est igitur hic propiciator generis humani, Mediator & Sacerdos, in cuius nomine preces sunt offerendæ. Licet tamen etiam ad ipsum Christum inuocationem dirigere, atque petere, vt propter suum sanguinem pro nobis effusum, nos clementer respiciat & saluet. Licet dicere, Iesu Christe Fili Dauid, miserere mei. Item: Domine Iesu, suscipe spiritum meum, &c.
units.tr: Reply: There is no connection, and it is an imposture, a non causa pro causa. For the sayings about invocation do not speak of the essence of God itself, but of office. God has revealed himself in such a way that the Son alone, not the Father, became man and victim for the sins of the whole world. He is therefore appointed here as the propitiator of the human race, Mediator and Priest, in whose name prayers are to be offered. Yet it is permitted also to direct the invocation to Christ himself, and to ask that, for the sake of his blood shed for us, he would mercifully look upon us and save us. One may say, "Jesus Christ, Son of David, have mercy on me." Likewise: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit," etc.

units.la: XXIII.
units.tr: XXIII.

units.la: Deus absolutè acceptus, non generat, vt Sophistæ affirmant.
units.tr: God, taken absolutely, does not beget, as the Sophists affirm.

units.la: Sed non est Pater Deus, qui non generârit.
units.tr: But the Father is not God if he has not begotten.

units.la: Ergo doctrina Sophistica euertit doctrinam de Deo.
units.tr: Therefore the Sophistic doctrine overturns the doctrine of God.

units.la: R. Sunt quatuor termini, & fallacia in voce Deus. Maior enim de natura seu Deitate loquitur, Minor de personis. Ac necesse est in sacris literis obseruare, quæ dicta de ipsa Deitate, & quæ de personis distinctè loquantur: quam quidem regulam isti Ariani euertere non poterunt. Deinde in Maiori simpliciter hoc affirmatur, vnam esse deitatem communem tribus: & rudiores monentur, generationem sic in sacris literis esse reuelatam, vt ad personanas referatur, nempe ad Patrem, qui generat solus, & ad Filium, qui natus est solus. Pater enim non est generatus, nec Spiritus sanctus est natus, qui habet suam proprietatem in procedendo ab utroque. Malitiosè igitur hanc loquutionem isti Ariani exagitant. Etsi autem Scholastici doctores quaedam nimis subtiliter differunt, tamen discernendum est inter ea, quae recte dicta sunt, & inter ea, quae palam sunt falsa.
units.tr: Reply: There are four terms, and the fallacy lies in the word God. For the major premise speaks of the nature or Deity, the minor of the persons. And it is necessary in Holy Scripture to observe which sayings speak distinctly of the Deity itself and which of the persons; this rule these Arians will not be able to overturn. Next, the major premise simply affirms that there is one common deity for the three; and the less learned are reminded that generation is so revealed in Holy Scripture as to be referred to the persons, namely to the Father, who alone begets, and to the Son, who alone is born. For the Father is not begotten, nor is the Holy Spirit born, who has his own property in proceeding from both. Therefore these Arians wrongly harass this expression. Although the Scholastic teachers distinguish some things too subtly, nevertheless one must discern between those things that are rightly said and those that are plainly false.

units.la: XXIIII.
units.tr: XXIIII.

units.la: Deus Pater nihil quicquam nobiscum agit, nisi per Filium.
units.tr: God the Father does nothing at all with us except through the Son.

units.la: Ergo solus Pater est Deus, non Filius & Spiritus sanctus cum Patre sunt Vnus & verus Deus.
units.tr: Therefore the Father alone is God; the Son and the Holy Spirit are not, with the Father, the one and true God.

units.la: R. Antecedes falsum est. Nā[?] Genes. 1. Elohim deliberat, Faciamꝰ[?] inquit, hominem. Ergo Deus Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus, ibi simul agunt de homine. Sic Pater inquit Matth.3.17. Hic est Filius meus, &c. Ibi Pater ipse docet nos immediatè de Filio suo, eúmque nobis exhibet. Deinde dicta scripturae de officio vniuscuiusque personae non tollunt neque destruunt communem, seu vnicam essentiam, seu Deitatem.
units.tr: Reply: The antecedent is false. For in Genesis 1, Elohim deliberates, he says, "Let us make man." There, therefore, God the Father, Son and Holy Spirit act together concerning man. Likewise the Father says in Matthew 3:17, "This is my beloved Son," etc. There the Father himself teaches us directly about his Son and presents him to us. Next, the sayings of Scripture about the office of each person do not remove or destroy the common, or single, essence or Deity.

units.la: XXV.
units.tr: XXV.

units.la: Vnum possunt esse multi, non vnus. Nam vnus & vnum differunt.
units.tr: There can be many things one, but not one one. For "one" and "one thing" differ.

units.la: Pater & Filius vnum sunt, Deitate, potentia, aeternitate.
units.tr: The Father and the Son are one in Deity, power and eternity.

units.la: Ergo non vnus & idem Deus est Filius cum Patre.
units.tr: Therefore the Son is not one and the same God with the Father.

units.la: Declaratio Minoris additur, Christus est vnū nobiscū natura vel humanitate, non vnus. Ita etiam cū Patre est Filius Dei vnū natura, nō vnus Deus.
units.tr: A declaration of the minor premise is added: Christ is one with us in nature or humanity, not one person. So too the Son of God is one with the Father in nature, not one God.

units.la: R. Multiplex est impostura in hoc argumento. Primum enim à principio philosophico, quod locum habet in creaturis, ad ipsum creatorem proceditur. Itaque Maior tantum de creaturis loquitur, non de vnitate essentiae Dei. Si vero ad Deum referendum esset, rectè intelligendum esset, nempe personas non esse confundendas. non enim est vnica tantum persona vnius & veri Dei, sed est vnus & verus Deus, qui distinctis tribus, Patre, Filio, & Spiritu sancto, in sacris literis exprimitur, siue istos tres voces hypostases, personas, siue ὑφιστάμενα, existentia, siue aliis convenientibus nominibus.
units.tr: Reply: The imposture in this argument is manifold. For first, from a philosophical principle, which holds in creatures, the argument proceeds to the Creator himself. Thus the major premise speaks only of creatures, not of the unity of the essence of God. If it were to be referred to God, it would rightly be understood that the persons are not to be confounded. For it is not merely a single person of the one and true God, but it is the one and true God who, with three distinct persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, is expressed in Holy Scripture, whether we call these three hypostases, persons, or ὑφιστάμενα, existing things, or by other suitable names.

units.la: Deinde, in Minori est insufficiens enumeratio proprietatum eius vnitatis, qua Pater & Filius vnum sunt. Nam existentia seu essentia quoque vnum sunt: id quod callidè isti veteratores omittunt. Ratio firmissima est, quia sacrae literae de Deo, vbi non expresse de distinctis personis loquuntur, simpliciter affirmant, vnum esse Deum. Ergo illi tres, quos aliàs distinctè nominat sancta scriptura, sunt vnus ille Deus, de quo primum praeceptum ait, Non habebis Deos alienos.
units.tr: Next, in the minor premise there is an insufficient enumeration of the properties of that unity by which the Father and the Son are one. For they are one also in existence or essence: a point which these cunning cheats slyly omit. The reasoning is most firm, because Holy Scripture, wherever it does not expressly speak of distinct persons, simply affirms that God is one. Therefore those three, whom Holy Scripture elsewhere names distinctly, are that one God, of whom the first commandment says, You shall have no other gods.

units.la: Declaratio Minoris dissimile adsert. Ergo nihil probat. Nam Filius Dei nequaquam est vnū nobiscum, sicut est vnum cum Patre. Nam de Christo dicitur, plenitudinem diuinitatis in eo habitare σωματικῶς. Hæc proprietas non conuenit Petro aut Paulo. Ita etiam non admensuram Christus accepit Spiritum sanctum. Comprehenditur Filius Dei in primo præcepto, & in illo illustri dicto, Deus tuus vnus est. Item, Nō est alius præter eum. Sed Iacobus, Iohannes, non comprehenduntur tali ratione in istis dictis, nisi quòd eum verum Deum agnoscere & colere debent. Conclusio igitur argumenti Ariani vana est.
units.tr: The declaration of the minor premise is dissimilar, and so proves nothing. For the Son of God is by no means one with us as he is one with the Father. Of Christ it is said that the fullness of the Godhead dwells in him bodily [σωματικῶς]. This property does not belong to Peter or Paul. Likewise, Christ did not receive the Holy Spirit by measure. The Son of God is included in the first commandment, and in that famous saying, Your God is one God. Likewise, there is no other besides him. But James and John are not included in these sayings in such a way, except that they ought to acknowledge and worship him as the true God. Therefore the conclusion of the Arian argument is empty.

units.la: XXVI.
units.tr: XXVI.

units.la: Filius non est vnus cum Patre, quia tres sunt. Inde hoc argumentum extruitur:
units.tr: The Son is not one with the Father, because there are three. From this the following argument is built:

units.la: Tres non possunt esse vnus.
units.tr: Three cannot be one.

units.la: Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus, tres sunt.
units.tr: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three.

units.la: Ergo Filius non est vnus cum Patre, nec Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: Therefore the Son is not one with the Father, nor is the Holy Spirit.

units.la: R. A principio Arithmetico, ad ipsam essentiam atque maiestatem Dei, non valet consequentia. Os Domini docet, tres esse, Patrem, & Filium & Spiritum sanctum, & esse vnum Deum, qui non sit alius, quàm Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: Answer: the inference does not hold when an arithmetical principle is applied to the very essence and majesty of God. The mouth of the Lord teaches that there are three, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and that there is one God, who is none other than the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Deinde notanda regula est. Alia dicta scripturæ loquuntur de personis, alia de Vnitate Dei, eaque non seipsa euertunt ac destruunt, sed potius declarant & confirmant. Blasphemum igitur dogma est istorum Arianorum, Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum non esse VNUM Deum. Id enim manifestis & expressis verbis asseuerant.
units.tr: Next, a rule must be noted. Some sayings of Scripture speak of the persons, others of the unity of God, and these do not overthrow and destroy one another, but rather declare and confirm one another. Therefore the doctrine of these Arians, that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not the ONE God, is blasphemous. For they assert this in plain and express words.

units.la: XXVII.
units.tr: XXVII.

units.la: Christus nusquam simpliciter dicitur Deus, sed tantum respectu Patris dicitur Deus.
units.tr: Christ is nowhere simply called God, but is called God only with respect to the Father.

units.la: Ergo Filius Dei non est vnus & idem Deus cum Patre & Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: Therefore the Son of God is not the one and the same God with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: R. Ex falsis asseuerationibus falsæ conclusiones gignuntur. Falsum est, Christum simpliciter nusquam Deum appellari. Nam Thomas eum simpliciter Iehoua & Deum appellat, Dominus, inquit, meus, & Deus meus. Itè, Rom. 8. Qui est super omnia Deus benedictus in secula. Hebr. 3. Qui creauit omnia Deus est. Loquitur autem de Filio Dei. Deus ipse veniet & saluabit nos. Esai. 9. Vocatum est nomen eius, Deus fortis, &c.
units.tr: Answer: false assertions produce false conclusions. It is false that Christ is nowhere simply called God. For Thomas simply calls him Jehovah and God: "My Lord," he says, "and my God." Likewise Rom. 8: "who is God over all, blessed for ever." Heb. 3: "he who built all things is God." And this speaks of the Son of God. "God himself will come and save us." Isa. 9: "his name shall be called God the mighty," etc.

units.la: Falsum & hoc est, Filium semper tantum respectu Patris Deum dici. Nam quod ad personas, sacra scriptura ponit distinctionem & relationem: sed quod ad ipsum esse Dei, affirmat unum esse Deum, qui sit primus & novissimus, α & ω, praeter quem non sit Deus. Ergo Filius & Spiritus sanctus non sunt alius Deus, praeter eum Deum, qui etiam Pater est. Quae igitur sacra vox distincte ponit, & quae coniungit & unit, non sunt confundenda, vel neganda. Tres ait esse, Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum, & tamen unum esse Deum. Ista quidem ratio humana metiri non potest, sed fides mysteriis diuinitus patefactis & traditis, veritatem tribuens, complecti potest. Fides enim non absterretur absurdis rationis, sed claro verbo Dei simpliciter & directe assentitur. Deus enim sapientissimus & veracissimus nequaquam metitur. Audio quidem nobis obiici, Filium esse Deum de Deo genitum, ac vere ista dici credo, sed hic de personis dicitur: alia vero dicta simpliciter de ipso Esse seu existentia Dei loquuntur, atque unitatem urgent. Eo autem isti Ariani suos cuniculos astute agunt, ut subruant hunc sacrosanctae Scripturae & fidei articulum, Filium esse unum Deum cum Patre & Spiritu sancto. Hinc porro illis Arianis sequetur, Filium esse inferiorem Deum Patre, esse sua quadam peculiari ratione DEVM, ita quidem, ut non sit unicus & verus Deus cum Patre & Spiritu sancto. Attendat igitur Ecclesia Dei, quantas praestigias Ariani meditetur in Ecclesia CHRISTI, mirificis suis insidiis spargere. Aperte enim isti Ariani iaciunt hoc fundamentum L.ij. Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum non esse unum Deum: Deitatem quidem & Naturam concedut esse communem istis tribus, perinde ut tribus hominibus ipsa humanitas est eadem seu communis. Sed similitudo ab hominibus ad essentiam atque maiestate Dei inconveniens est. Nam creaturam sic se habere certum est: ipsam vero Dei essentiam eodem modo se habere, nullus Arianus, neque spiritus malignus probare atque evincere ullis argumentis poterit. Referimus autem nos in hisce articulis fidei, non ad creaturas, non ad ratiocinationes cerebri humani, sed ad verbum Dei revelatum, quod inquit unum esse Deum, & de hoc unico Deo differens, nominat Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: It is also false that the Son is always called God only with respect to the Father. For as far as the persons are concerned, holy Scripture makes a distinction and a relation; but as far as the very being of God is concerned, it affirms that there is one God, who is the first and the last, alpha and omega [α καὶ ω], and besides whom there is no God. Therefore the Son and the Holy Spirit are not another God besides that God who is also the Father. So the words of Scripture that set forth a distinction must not be confused or denied, nor those that join and unite. It says there are three, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and yet that there is one God. Human reason cannot measure this, but faith, which yields to the truth of the mysteries divinely revealed and handed down, can embrace it. For faith is not frightened off by the absurdities of reason, but assents simply and directly to the clear word of God. For God, the most wise and most truthful, does not submit to measurement. I hear, to be sure, that it is objected to us that the Son is God begotten of God, and I believe these things are truly said; but here it is spoken of the persons, whereas other sayings speak simply of the very being or existence of God, and press the unity. Yet these Arians cunningly work their little mines, so as to undermine this article of holy Scripture and of faith, that the Son is one God with the Father and the Holy Spirit. From this it will follow for those Arians that the Son is a God inferior to the Father, a God in some peculiar sense of his own, and so not the only and true God together with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Let the Church of God therefore take heed what wonderful deceptions the Arians are devising to scatter in the Church of Christ by their marvellous snares. For these Arians plainly lay this foundation: that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not one God. They concede indeed that the Godhead and the nature are common to these three, just as humanity itself is the same or common to three men. But the comparison from men is unfitting for the essence and majesty of God. For it is certain that this is how a creature stands; but that the very essence of God stands in the same way, no Arian, nor any evil spirit, will be able to prove and establish by any arguments. We, however, in these articles of faith refer ourselves not to creatures, nor to the reasonings of the human brain, but to the revealed word of God, which says that God is one, and, discoursing about this one God, names the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: XXVIII.
units.tr: XXVIII.

units.la: Ubicunque Deus absolute in scripturis est positus, semper est Pater.
units.tr: Wherever God is set down absolutely in the Scriptures, it is always the Father.

units.la: Ergo solus Pater est unicus Deus, non Filius, non Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: Therefore the Father alone is the only God, not the Son, not the Holy Spirit.

units.la: R. Regula Arianorum non est vera. Sed haec regula Ecclesiae Dei, vera est & firma, Ubicunque vocabulum Deus, absolute in scripturis ponitur, nec fit diserte mentio personarum, ibi non solum Patrem, sed Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum complectitur: vt, Audi Israel, Dominus Deus tuus, Deus vnus est. Non habebis Deos alienos. Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & ei soli seruies, &c. Nam hic Deus, tali modo in sacris literis exponitur, quòd sit Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus, & in mundi creatione, in collectione Ecclesiæ, in regeneratione, in donatione vitæ æternæ, ac similibus operibus, pari potentia & maiestate coniunguntur, ac consentit Ecclesiæ Dei vnani-mis fides & confessio omnium temporum: id quod alio loco paulò copiosius explicauimus.
units.tr: Answer: the rule of the Arians is not true. But this rule of the Church of God is true and firm: wherever the word God is set down absolutely in the Scriptures, and no mention of the persons is explicitly made, there it embraces not only the Father but the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit: for example, "Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God, the Lord is one." "You shall have no other gods." "You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone," etc. For this God is set forth in the sacred writings in such a way that he is the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and in the creation of the world, in the gathering of the Church, in regeneration, in the bestowal of eternal life, and in similar works, they are joined together with equal power and majesty; and this agrees with the unanimous faith and confession of the Church of God in all ages, which we have explained somewhat more fully in another place.

units.la: Obseruandum denique & hoc est, Arianos nouos, more suorum maiorum, perplexè & truncatim de Deo loqui. Itaque ab ipsis iure exigimus, vt integram doctrinam de Deo, perspicuis verbis proponant, & in singulis partibus se euoluat & explicent, non studeant ambiguitatibus & obscuritatibus. Dicant clarè, quòd Filius non sit is Deus, qui Pater est: & qualis sit Deus Filius, cùm non sit ille ipse Deus, qui Pater & Spiritus sanctus est: quoto gradu, vel qua ratione Filius, quo ad diuinitatem, sit inferior Deus ipso vnico Deo Patre, cùm non sit vnicus & verus Deus Filius Dei, an sit alia ratione posterior Deus, & quomodo sit Spiritus sanctus Deus, cùm non sit vnicus Deus, qui & Pater & Filius. Cùm enim eam proprietatem, vnicum & verum esse Deum, tantùm tribuant Patri, eámque, inquam, proprietatem Filio & Spiritui sancto adimant, dicendum est plane, an sint ordine secundi vel tertii Dij, vel nuncupatiuè tantùm hoc ipsis epitheton adscribatur, aut alio modo? Vbi se tali pacto prodiderint, iudicium quoque suum, ex verbo Dei & confessione Ecclesiæ accipient, quale merentur.
units.tr: Finally, this too must be observed: the new Arians, after the manner of their forefathers, speak of God in a confused and fragmentary way. Therefore we rightly demand of them that they set forth the whole doctrine of God in plain words, and unfold and explain it in each part, and not strive after ambiguities and obscurities. Let them say clearly that the Son is not that God who is the Father; and what sort of God the Son is, since he is not that very God who is the Father and the Holy Spirit; to what degree, or in what respect, the Son, as to his divinity, is a God inferior to the one God the Father, since he is not the only and true God of God the Son; or whether he is in some other respect a God later in order; and how the Holy Spirit is God, since he is not the only God who is both Father and Son. For since they attribute that property, to be the only and true God, to the Father alone, and take it away from the Son and the Holy Spirit, I say they must plainly state whether they are second or third gods in order, or whether this title is ascribed to them merely as a name, or in some other way. Where they have disclosed themselves in such a manner, they will also receive their judgment from the word of God and the confession of the Church, such as they deserve.

units.la: Hactenus nouorum Arianorum falsas & erroneas doctrinas, contume-liosas in Filium Dei & Spiritum sanctū, recensui, & argumenta excusi, quæ partim ex insciria[?] crassa & affectata, partim verò ex manifesta calumnia nascuntur. Dolendum autem est, inueniri homines, qui tam tetris portentis applau-sum præbent, & orandus Deus est, vt istos nouos Arianos confundat, ac suam doctrinam de sua ipsius existentia, incorruptam in Ecclesia sua custodiat, idque propter inuocationem & glorificationem nominis sui sanctissimi. Amen. Verè enim nouissima nunc ingruunt tēpora, in quibus diabolus omnis generis corruptelas auget, vt quàm plurimos homines secum in æternum exitium abripiat.
units.tr: Hitherto I have reviewed and exposed the false and erroneous doctrines of the new Arians, insulting to the Son of God and the Holy Spirit, and their arguments, which arise partly from crass and affected ignorance, and partly from manifest calumny. It is to be lamented, however, that men are found who give applause to such foul monstrosities; and God is to be prayed to that he would confound these new Arians, and keep his doctrine of his own being uncorrupted in his Church, and this for the invocation and glorification of his most holy name. Amen. For truly the most recent times are now upon us, in which the devil increases corruptions of every kind, so as to snatch away as many men as possible with him to eternal destruction.

units.la: Blasphemæ voces in Deum, quibus isti immundi porci, & ipsum Deum, & Ecclesiam eius, rectè de hoc articulo sentientem, conspuunt, tam sunt tetrae & horrendae, vt eas referre abhorream. Nam istum Deum, qui sit vnus, & sit Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus, hoc est, tres personae, aiunt esse versipellem Deum, qui se interdum occultet in vno, interdum vero dilatet in tribus perso-nis. Et hunc Deum, qui sit vnus in tribus, nihil vnquam egisse, vel verbo vel opere, nec habere Filium, nec Mediatorem, & nihil differre à Deo Baal, Moloch, Bytho, Turcico ac Iudaico. Neque esse vnum Deum Patrem Christi, in essentia & personis quaerendum. Item sub titulo essentiae Dei, Satanam coli inquiunt. Item, Hunc esse Sophistarum & Antichristi, imò fictitium Deum, esse laruam triformem. Ita nostram doctrinam, quòd vnus Deus existat, & sint tres personae, Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus, dicunt esse mera monstra, esse fundamentum Antichristi, esse ipsius Satanae commentum. Quis non cohorrescit toto pectore, tantas blasphemias audiens? Si aliquot legiones diabolorum ex Acheronte prosilirent, posséntne horribiliores blasphemias in verum Deum euomere? Ex hisce igitur de novorum istorum Arianorum delirijs omnes pij iudicent. Non sunt albi & subtiles isti spiritus, qui Ecclesiam per istos furiosos homines impetunt, sed crassi, tetri, nigri: quos propter blasphemias in Deum, ni-si pedem referent & conuertentur, merito DEVS ipse retundet. AMEN Amen.
units.tr: These blasphemous words against God, with which those filthy pigs spit upon both God himself and his Church, which rightly thinks on this article, are so foul and horrible that I shrink from repeating them. For they say that this God, who is one, and is Father, Son and Holy Spirit, that is, three persons, is a shifty God, who at one time hides himself in one and at another time spreads himself out into three persons. And they say that this God, who is one in three, has never done anything, either by word or by deed, nor has he a Son or a Mediator, and that he differs in no way from the god Baal, Moloch, Bytho, or the gods of the Turks and the Jews. Nor, they say, is the one God the Father of Christ to be sought in essence and persons. Likewise, under the title of the essence of God, they say that Satan is worshipped. Likewise, they say that this God is the God of the Sophists and of Antichrist, indeed a fictitious God, a three-formed specter. Thus they say that our doctrine, that there is one God and three persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, is mere monstrosity, the foundation of Antichrist, the very invention of Satan himself. Who does not shudder from the depths of his heart on hearing such blasphemies? If several legions of devils were to leap forth from Acheron, could they vomit forth more horrible blasphemies against the true God? Let all the godly, then, judge from these raving nonsense of these new Arians. It is not pale and subtle spirits that attack the Church through these furious men, but thick, foul, black ones; and unless they turn back their foot and change their minds, God himself will rightly crush them on account of their blasphemies against him. AMEN. Amen.

units.la: ASSERTIO DOCTRINÆ ECCLESIÆ CATHOLICÆ DE SANCTA TRINITATE, cum confutatione erroris Valentini Gentilis, Per Alexandrum Alesium, Academiæ Lipsicæ Theologum.
units.tr: ASSERTION OF THE DOCTRINE OF THE CATHOLIC CHURCH CONCERNING THE HOLY TRINITY, with a refutation of the error of Valentinus Gentilis, by Alexander Alesius, Theologian of the Academy of Leipzig.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: ON voco doctrinam sonantem in Ecclesiis per totum orbem terrarum de sancta & individua Trinitate in dubium, nec de illa more Academico disputo in vtramque partem, neque dubitationem affero, sicut Protagoras apud Ciceronem suum librum incepit: De diis neque vt sint, neque vt non sint, habeo dicere. Et scio huiusmodi disputationes in Codice Iustiniani prohibitas esse. Sed asseuero doctrinâ de Trinitate, sicut exponitur in Symbolo Apostolorum, quod ij qui proximi fuerunt Apostolis, & eos ac eorum discipulos audierunt, Ignatius, Polycarpus, Iustinus, Irenæus, Tertullianus, & alij vocant traditionem Apostolicam & regulam fidei, ac docent, hanc regulam opponendam praescriptionibus haereticorum. Et confirmo hanc doctrinam ex testimoniis Prophetarum & Apostolorum, sicut illi in expositione Symboli eam confirmarunt, & quemadmodum hoc explicatum fuit in Symbolo Niceno & Athanasiano, & in Synodis Antiochena, Constantinopolitana, Ephesina, Chalcedonensi, & sequentibus. Ac ex horum omnium testimoniis haereses omnes refuto.
units.tr: I do not call into doubt the doctrine of the holy and undivided Trinity, which resounds in the Churches throughout the whole world, nor do I dispute about it in the academic manner on either side, nor do I raise doubt, as Protagoras began in Cicero's book: "Concerning the gods I am able to say neither that they exist nor that they do not exist." I know that disputations of this kind are forbidden in the Code of Justinian. But I affirm the doctrine of the Trinity as it is set forth in the Apostles' Creed, which those who were nearest to the Apostles, and heard them and their disciples, Ignatius, Polycarp, Justin, Irenaeus, Tertullian and others, call the apostolic tradition and the rule of faith, and teach that this rule is to be set against the prescriptions of heretics. And I confirm this doctrine from the testimonies of the Prophets and Apostles, just as they confirmed it in their exposition of the Creed, and as it has been explained in the Nicene and Athanasian Creeds, and in the Synods of Antioch, Constantinople, Ephesus, Chalcedon and those that followed. And from the testimonies of all of these I refute all heresies.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Non est autem nouum, vt aliqui, non illi quidem indocti neque hebetes, sed insolentes & inflati opinione scientiae, & impulsi gloriosi nominis ambitione, excerpendo de sacris literis sententiarum aliquas particulas, & ita abhorrens a Catholico consensu dogma condendo, authores existant turbarum & sectionum. Neque tam absurdum quicquam confingi potest, quod in nouitate non inueniat astipulatores, quemadmodum intuentibus veteres haereses facile apparet. Itaque recedentes a Catholicae Ecclesiae orthodoxo consensu non sunt in hac audiendi, quantumuis perstrepant scripturae iactatione. Atque refutat hos Psalmi grauissimum dictum: Peccatori autem dixit Deus, Quare tu enarras iustitias meas? Cum autem multi fraudulenta inculcatione scripturarum decepti, a vera via seducantur: & quidam modo, qui se Gentilem nominat, personatus Eunomianus, alienus prorsus a populo Dei, quae est Ecclesia Christi, nefaria temeritate corrupere summam fidei nostrae, de natura Dei aeterni, quae cernitur in tribus proprietatibus seu personis, & ideo Trinitas unius Dei appellatur, & delirationes suas perscriptas diuulgare ausus fuerit: non debui neque potui haec tacendo dissimulare. Atque conatibus illius obuiam eundum esse duxi, quibus fundamentum veritatis caelestis & doctrinae sanae, sanctae fidei nostrae conuelleretur. Itaque sequentia, de quibus disputaretur pia argumentatione, secundum consuetudinem Academiae nostrae proposui, repetitis iis quae exponuntur commemorata traditaque a piis doctoribus in Ecclesia Christi, confutantibus furores, partim manifeste, partim occulte peruertentes patefacta de Dei aeterni natura & personis. Quibus futilia commenta istius Gentilis quoque refelli & exterminari facile intelligent omnes quibus veritas cordi est, τοῖς τεμὴ[?] ἐξ ἐριθείας[?] καὶ ἀπειθοῦσι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πειθομένοις δὲ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ, vt ait Apostolus.
units.tr: It is not new that some men, not indeed unlearned or dull, but insolent and puffed up with the opinion of their own learning, and driven by the ambition of a glorious name, pick out certain fragments of sentences from the sacred letters and, dogmatising in a way that departs from the Catholic consensus, become the authors of disturbances and schisms. Nor can anything so absurd be invented that in its novelty it finds no supporters, as is easily apparent to those who look at the ancient heresies. Therefore those who depart from the orthodox consensus of the Catholic Church are not to be heard in this matter, however loudly they clamour with the boasting of Scripture. And the most weighty saying of the Psalm refutes them: "But to the wicked God said, Why dost thou declare my statutes?" Since many are deceived by the fraudulent urging of Scripture and are led away from the true way, and a certain man who calls himself a Gentile, a masked Eunomian, altogether alien to the people of God, which is the Church of Christ, has with impious rashness corrupted the sum of our faith concerning the nature of the eternal God, which is discerned in three properties or persons, and for that reason is called the Trinity of the one God, and has dared to publish his written delusions, I ought not and could not keep silent and dissemble these things. And I judged that his attempts must be met, by which the foundation of heavenly truth and of sound doctrine and of our holy faith would be overthrown. Therefore I have set forth the following points, which are to be debated by pious argument according to the custom of our Academy, repeating those things which have been recalled and handed down by the pious teachers in the Church of Christ, refuting the frenzies that partly openly, partly secretly pervert the revealed nature and persons of the eternal God. By these the trifling inventions of this Gentile also will be refuted and driven out, as all who hold the truth dear will easily understand, "to those who are contentious and disobey the truth, but obey unrighteousness," as the Apostle says.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Protestatio ac confessio fidei Gentilis.
units.tr: The protestation and confession of faith of Gentile.

units.la: Valentinus Gentilis Italus, ait se credere libris Canonicis veteris & noui testamenti, tanquam oraculis Dei, & confiteri Symbolum Apostolorum & Nicenum, ac damnare omnes haereses condemnatas ab Ecclesia ex verbo Dei, nec probare doctrinam vllius hominis, quantumuis docti, & in speciem pij, qui a scriptura Prophetica & Apostolica discedit, aut huic aduersatur.
units.tr: Valentinus Gentilis, an Italian, says that he believes the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments as the oracles of God, and that he confesses the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds, and condemns all heresies condemned by the Church on the authority of the Word of God, and that he does not approve the doctrine of any man, however learned and seemingly pious, who departs from or opposes the prophetic and apostolic Scripture.

units.la: IIII.
units.tr: IIII.

units.la: Iuxta hanc regulam, a qua nec transuersum digitum ait se cessurum, fatetur setur se nullum Deum Trinitatem agnoscere. Et ad probandum dogma de per-sonarum Trinitate in uno Deo esse humanum commentum, ignotum Catholi-cis, ait Sophistas docuisse Trinitatem esse nomen substantiale, & significare essentiam extra personam Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti, ac constituere quartam in Trinitate substantiam. Negat etiam tres personas tantum distin-gui relatione, aut proprietatibus, & attributis, & affirmat significare tres ra-tionales, & intelligentes essentias vel substantias. Ait etiam se medium inter haereses oppositas Eunomij & Arij tenere, & neque Deum trinomium, ne-que tripersonatum ponere: sed sicut in Symbolo dicitur, Credere unum Deum Patrem omnipotentem. Et ideo solum Patrem dici Deum unum, propter mo-narchiam, ut dixit Praxeas. Et quod sit origo & principium, causa & effector omnium, ac essentiator Filij. Et propterea Filium, & Spiritum sanctum non posse dici, aut esse unum cum Patre Deum, quod sit pugnantia in adiecto, di-cere quod duo aut tres numero differentes sint simpliciter unus, aut unus Deus. Postremo Patrem tantum in Scriptura dici Deum, Filium autem Do-minum & Mediatorem, & Spiritum Paracletum, non autem Deum.
units.tr: According to this rule, from which he says he will not yield a finger's breadth, he confesses that he acknowledges no God who is a Trinity. And to prove that the dogma of three persons in one God is a human invention, unknown to Catholics, he says that the Sophists taught that Trinity is a substantial name and signifies an essence beyond the person of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and constitutes a fourth substance in the Trinity. He also denies that the three persons are distinguished only by relation, or by properties and attributes, and affirms that they signify three rational and intelligent essences or substances. He further says that he holds a middle position between the opposed heresies of Eunomius and Arius, and that he posits neither a God of three names nor a God of three persons, but, as the Creed says, "I believe in one God the Father almighty." And therefore that only the Father is called the one God, on account of the monarchy, as Praxeas said. And that he is the origin and principle, the cause and maker of all things, and the one who gives being to the Son. And therefore that the Son and the Holy Spirit cannot be called, or be, one God with the Father, since it is a contradiction in terms to say that two or three things numerically different are simply one, or one God. Lastly, that in Scripture only the Father is called God, but the Son is called Lord and Mediator, and the Spirit the Paraclete, and not God.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Summa sophistices Gentilis.
units.tr: The sum of Gentilis's sophistry.

units.la: Ad persuasionem sui dogmatis utitur hac Sophistica, Quòd testimonia scripturæ, ex quibus omnes Catholici probant unum Deum esse propter naturæ & essentiæ unitatem, ipse torquet ad probandum tantum Patrem esse unū Deum, vel unam in Divinitate personam. Et contra omnia scripturæ testimonia, ex quibus Catholici probant tres in una divinitate esse personas, detorquet ad probandum tres essentias, & substantias. Hoc enim artificio trahit in suam sententiam epistolas Ignatij, & ait sic sensisse Iustinum, Irenæum, & Tertullianum.
units.tr: To persuade people of his doctrine, Gentilis uses this sophistry. The testimonies of Scripture by which all Catholics prove that there is one God, on account of the unity of nature and essence, he twists to prove only that the Father is the one God, or one person in the Godhead. And against all the testimonies of Scripture by which Catholics prove that there are three persons in one Godhead, he twists them to prove three essences and substances. By this trick he drags the epistles of Ignatius into his own opinion, and says that Justin, Irenaeus and Tertullian thought the same.

units.la: Ego verò Deo iuvante ex eorum & aliorum omnium Catholicorum scripturæ interpretum testimoniis, doctrinam de uno Deo, Patre, & Filio, & Spiritu sancto confirmabo, & refutabo sophisticam Gentilis.
units.tr: But I, with God's help, will confirm the doctrine of one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, from the testimonies of them and of all other Catholic interpreters of Scripture, and I will refute the sophistry of Gentilis.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Possem breviter & rotundè ei respondere, redactis argumentis ad formam syllogismi, & collectis antinomiis ex dictis Patrum, quos ait Scripturam pro sua sententia interpretari, clauum, ut dicitur, clavo pellere: sed non volo truncatas citare sententias, ac potius ex plena & perfecta totius doctrinæ Ignatij, Tertulliani & aliorum expositione quæ fuerit perpetua eorum sententia de hoc dogmate demonstrare. Quare peto ut si prolixior in citandis testimoniis fuero, lector hanc meam diligentiam pro eruenda & vindicanda veritate à sophistica, boni consulat.
units.tr: I could answer him briefly and bluntly, reducing the arguments to the form of a syllogism and gathering contradictions from the sayings of the Fathers, whom he claims interpret Scripture for his view, to drive a nail with a nail, as the saying goes. But I do not wish to cite truncated sentences. Rather, from a full and complete exposition of the whole teaching of Ignatius, Tertullian and the others, I will show what their constant view of this dogma was. So I ask that, if I am rather lengthy in citing testimonies, the reader will kindly accept this care of mine, for the sake of bringing out and defending the truth against sophistry.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Recitabo autem ordine testimonia interpretum scripturæ, inde à temporibus Apostolorum usque ad hæc nostra: & incipiam ab Ignatio, discipulo Apostolo-rum. Deinde veniam ad Iustinum, & Irenæum discipulum Polycarpi, & ad Clementem Alexandrinum discipulum Pantæni, & Tertullianum, & Originem discipulum Clementis Alexandrini, & Cyprianum, & alios qui præ-cesserunt Nicenam Synodum.
units.tr: I will recite in order the testimonies of the interpreters of Scripture, from the times of the Apostles down to our own. I will begin with Ignatius, a disciple of the Apostles. Then I will come to Justin, and to Irenaeus, a disciple of Polycarp, and to Clement of Alexandria, a disciple of Pantaenus, and to Tertullian, and Origen, a disciple of Clement of Alexandria, and Cyprian, and others who preceded the Nicene Synod.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Ignatius in epistola ad Trallianos hos in Christum contumeliosos vocat, qui eum à Patre alienant, & neque quòd sit Spiritus sanctus, confitentur. Et in epistola ad Magnesianos: Christum verò ante secula genitū à Patre, Deum verbum, & unigenitum Filium, quia unus est, Deus omnipotens qui manifestavit seipsum per Iesum Christum Filium suum, qui est verbum, ipsius nō prolatiuum scilicet, sed substantiale, non loquutio articulatæ vocis, ἀλλὰ ἐνεργείας θεϊκῆς[?] οὐσία γεννητὴ, id est, ut in epistola ad Hebræos dicitur, ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δό-ξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ. Et in eadem epistola Ignatij dicitur: Qui ante secula genitus est à Patre, postea autem factus ex Maria virgine ἄνευ ὁμιλίας viri, solùm, verum, Deù Patrè suum annunciauit. Et in epistola ad Colossenses: Et quòd iste qui natus est ex muliere, Filius est Dei, & qui crucifixus est, primogenitus est universæ creaturæ, & Deus verbum, & ipse fecit omnia iussione Patris. quod Apostolus corroborat dicens: Unus Deus Pater ex quo omnia, & unus Dominus Iesus Christus per quem omnia. Et iterum, Unus enim Deus, unus est Mediator Dei & hominum homo Iesus Christus, qui est imago Dei invisibilis, primogenitus universæ creaturæ: quoniam in ipso creata sunt omnia, quæ sunt in cælo & in terra, visibilia & invisibilia. Et ipse est ante omnes, & omnia in ipso constant. Et quia non est ipse ille qui est super omnia, Deus, sed Filius ipsius, qui & ascendere se ad eum profitetur dicens: Ascendo ad Patrem meum & Patrem vestrum, & ad Deum meum & Deum vestrum. Et quando ei fuerint omnia subiecta, tunc & ipse subiectus erit illi, qui ei subdidit omnia, ut sit Deus omnia in omnibus.
units.tr: In his epistle to the Trallians, Ignatius calls insulters of Christ those who alienate him from the Father and do not confess that he is also the Holy Spirit. And in his epistle to the Magnesians: Christ, begotten from the Father before the ages, God the Word and only-begotten Son, since he is one, is almighty God, who manifested himself through Jesus Christ his Son, who is the Word, not uttered but substantial, not the utterance of articulate voice, but a begotten substance of divine energy [ἀλλὰ ἐνεργείας θεϊκῆς οὐσία γεννητή], that is, as it is said in the epistle to the Hebrews, "the brightness of his glory and the express image of his person" [ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ]. And in the same epistle of Ignatius it is said: he who was begotten from the Father before the ages, but afterwards was made from the Virgin Mary without intercourse with a man [ἄνευ ὁμιλίας ἀνδρός], made known only the true God as his Father. And in the epistle to the Colossians: that he who was born of a woman is the Son of God, and he who was crucified is the firstborn of all creation, and God the Word, and he himself made all things at the command of the Father. The Apostle confirms this, saying: "One God the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things." And again: "For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and men, the man Jesus Christ, who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation; for in him were created all things that are in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible. And he is before all, and in him all things consist." And since he is not himself that one who is God over all, but his Son, he also professes that he ascends to him, saying: "I ascend to my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God." And when all things have been subjected to him, then he himself will be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Ergo alius est ille, qui subiecit Filio omnia, & qui est omnia in omnibus: & alius Filius cui subiecta sunt omnia, qui & post hæc omnia subiectus erit illi qui ei subdidit omnia. Et nō est purus homo ille δί' ἕ[?] καὶ ἐν ᾧ γέγονε τὰ πάντα, id est, id est, per quem, & in quo facta sunt omnia. Omnia enim, inquit, per ipsum facta sunt. Et in libro Sapientiæ ipse de seipso refert dicens: Quum faceret cælum aderam illi. Et iterum: Ego eram apud eum cuncta componens, & congaudebat mihi quotidie.
units.tr: Therefore that one is other who subjected all things to the Son and who is all in all, and the other is the Son to whom all things are subjected, who also after all these things will be subjected to him who subjected all things to him. And he is not a mere man, through whom [δι' οὗ] and in whom [ἐν ᾧ] all things came to be, that is, through whom and in whom all things were made. For, he says, all things were made through him. And in the Book of Wisdom he speaks of himself, saying: "When he prepared the heavens, I was there." And again: "I was with him, arranging all things, and I rejoiced with him every day."

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Quomodo autem homo purus audiret, Sede ad dextram meam? Aut quomodo diceret, Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum? Vel illud quod ait: Gloria illa glorifica me, quam habui apud te priusquam mundus fieret? Quis autem homo possit dicere, Descendi de cælo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem eius qui misit me? Vel de quo homine diceretur, Erat lumen illud lumen verum, quod illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum. In mundo erat, & mundus per ipsum factus est, & mundus eum non cognouit. In propria venit, & sui eum non receperunt?
units.tr: But how would a mere man hear, "Sit at my right hand"? Or how would he say, "Before Abraham was, I am"? Or that saying: "Glorify me with that glory which I had with you before the world was"? Who among men could say, "I came down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me"? Or of what man could it be said: "That was the true light, which enlightens every man coming into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him. He came to his own, and his own did not receive him"?

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Quomodo ergo huiusmodi homo est purus ex Maria demū habens initium ut esset, & non potius Deus verbum, & Filius unigenitus, de quo dictum est: In principio erat Verbum, & Verbum erat apud Deum, & Deus erat Verbum. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt, & sine ipso factum est nihil. Et paulò post: Vidimus gloriam eius, gloriam quasi unigeniti à Patre, plenum gratia & veritate. Et iterum: Unigenitus qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarrauit. Qui & per Salomonem refert dicēs: Ante omnes colles genuit me Dominus. Et resuscitaturus est corpora nostra. Dixit enim: Amen dico vobis quoniā venit hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audiét voce Filij Dei. Et qui audierint, viuét.
units.tr: How, then, is such a man merely a man, who had his beginning from Mary alone, in order to exist, and is not rather God the Word and the only-begotten Son, of whom it is said: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made." And a little later: "We saw his glory, the glory of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth." And again: "The only-begotten, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him." He also speaks through Solomon, saying: "Before all the hills the Lord begat me." And he is going to raise our bodies. For he said: "Amen, I say to you, the hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live."

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Ecce quomodo Ignatius exponit primum & secundum articulum Symboli, & confutat hæreses sui temporis Cherinti, Ebionis, & aliorum, qui negabant Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum esse natura Deum: aut contendebāt eum non esse alium à Patre, id est, aliam ab ipso personam distinctam. Ex illis scripturæ Propheticæ & Apostolicæ testimoniis, ex quibus omnes in hunc usque diem orthodoxi probant Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum, esse unum Deum, & distinctas inter se personas.
units.tr: See how Ignatius expounds the first and second articles of the Creed, and refutes the heresies of his time, those of Cerinthus, Ebion and others, who denied that our Lord Jesus Christ is God by nature, or contended that he was not other than the Father, that is, not a person distinct from him. Ignatius does this from those prophetic and apostolic testimonies of Scripture by which all orthodox believers to this day prove that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God and distinct persons.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Hic enim est scopus, & status omnium disputationum Ignatij contra hæreses de Trinitate. Et in hanc sententiam ipse illa quæ præcesserunt exponit, in Epistola ad Philippenses: Unus est enim Deus omnium, Pater Christi, ex quo omnia. Et unus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius Dei unigenitus, dominator vniuersorum, per quem omnia: vnus etiam Spiritus sanctus, qui operabatur in Mose & Prophetis & Apostolis. Vnum quoque est baptisma, quod datur in morte Christi: vna itaque Ecclesia esse debet, & vna fides, quae est in Christo, secundum dictum eiusdem Apostoli dicentis: Vnus Deus, vna fides, & vnum baptisma: vnus Deus & Pater omnium, & per omnia, & in omnibus.
units.tr: For this is the aim and the state of all Ignatius's disputations against the heresies about the Trinity. To this same effect he sets out, in the epistle to the Philippians, what went before: "For there is one God of all, the Father of Christ, from whom are all things. And one Lord, our Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, lord of all, through whom are all things; also one Holy Spirit, who worked in Moses and the Prophets and the Apostles. There is also one baptism, which is given in the death of Christ. So there ought to be one Church and one faith, which is in Christ, according to the saying of the same Apostle, who says: 'One God, one faith, and one baptism: one God and Father of all, and through all, and in all.'"

units.la: XIIII.
units.tr: XIIII.

units.la: Vnus igitur Deus & Pater, & non duo, neque tres, vnus existens, & non est praeter eum solus verus. Dominus enim dicit: Deus tuus Dominus vnus est. Et rursum: Nonne vnus Deus creauit nos? nonne vnus Pater omnium nostrum? vnus vere etiam Filius λόγος Deus vnigenitus, qui est in sinu Patris. Et iterum, Vnus Dominus Iesus Christus. Et alibi: Quod nomen eius, aut quod nomen Filij eius? Scitote autem, quia vnus est Paracletus, vnus Spiritus, sicut vocati estis in vnam spem vocationis vestrae. Et iterum, Omnes in vno Spiritu ἐποτίσθημεν[?]. Manifeste autem omnia dona gratiarum ipse atque idem Spiritus operatur. Ergo neque tres sunt Patres, neque tres Filij, sed neque tres Paracleti, sed vnus Paracletus: ac propterea Dominus mittens Apostolos docere omnes gentes, praecepit eis, Baptizate eos in nomine Patris & Filij & Spiritus sancti. Non in vnum quendam trinomium, neque εἰς τρεῖς ἐνανθρωπήσαντας[?], ἀλλ' εἰς τρεῖς ὁμοτίμως[?], quia vnus est tantum qui homo factus est, non Pater scilicet, neque Paracletus, sed solus Filius.
units.tr: Therefore one God and Father, and not two, nor three, one existing, and there is no true God besides him alone. For the Lord says: "Your God, the Lord, is one." And again: "Has not one God created us? Has not one Father of us all?" Truly also one Son, the Word [λόγος], the only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father. And again: "One Lord Jesus Christ." And elsewhere: "What is his name, or what is the name of his Son?" Know, however, that there is one Paraclete, one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling. And again: "All were given to drink of one Spirit [ἐποτίσθημεν]." Moreover, the same Spirit works all the gifts of grace. Therefore there are neither three Fathers, nor three Sons, nor three Paracletes, but one Paraclete. And so the Lord, sending the Apostles to teach all nations, commanded them: "Baptize them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit", not into some one three-named [trinomium] being, nor into three who became incarnate [εἰς τρεῖς ἐνανθρωπήσαντας], but into three equally honoured [εἰς τρεῖς ὁμοτίμως], because only one is he who was made man, not the Father, certainly, nor the Paraclete, but the Son alone.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Et hic rursus vide in quam sententiam, & contra quos Ignatius dicit vnum Deum Patrem, videlicet contra haereticos, qui docebant, Vnam tantum esse ὑπόστασιν, id est, personam diuinam, quae haberet tria nomina, propter tria officia: & quod dicatur Pater, quia creauit nos: Filius, quia in assumpta humana natura mortuus est: & Spiritus sanctus, quia sanctificat Ecclesiam, vel ne putentur plures dij, aut Patres, aut Filij, aut Spiritus sancti, sicut Valentiniani, & alij haeretici confinxerunt, de quibus in principio Epistolae Ignatius meminit. Et in sequenti Epistola ad Philadelphienses, vbi ait: Si quis vnum Deum dicit, confiteturque IESVM CHRISTVM, hominem vero purum putans Dominum, & non Deum vnigenitum, & Sapientiam & Verbum Dei, huiusmodi est pauper sensu sicut Ebion.
units.tr: And here again, see in what sense, and against whom, Ignatius says "one God the Father": namely against the heretics who taught that there is only one hypostasis, that is, one divine person, which had three names on account of three offices. It is called Father because it created us, Son because in the assumed human nature it died, and Holy Spirit because it sanctifies the Church. Or they taught this lest there be thought to be several gods, or several fathers, sons or holy spirits, as the Valentinians and other heretics devised, of whom Ignatius makes mention at the beginning of his Epistle. And in the following Epistle to the Philadelphians, where he says: "If anyone says there is one God, and confesses Jesus Christ, yet thinks of him as a mere man and not as the Lord, the only-begotten God, and the Wisdom and Word of God, such a person is poor in understanding, like Ebion."

units.la: Et in Epistola ad Ephesios clarissimè refutat mendacia Gentilis, quum ait: Medicus autem noster est solus verus Deus vnigenitus & invisibilis Dominus omnium, vnigeniti Pater & genitor.
units.tr: And in the Epistle to the Ephesians he clearly refutes the lies of Gentilis, when he says: "Our physician is the only true God, only-begotten and invisible Lord of all, Father and begetter of the only-begotten."

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Falsum est igitur Patrem solum dici unum Deum exclusò Filio, & Filium dici, Dominum, non autem unum Deum cum Patre. Imò Ignatius & nomen Veri Dei, & Medici commune facit Patri & Filio in divina natura. Et postea idem nomen tribuit Filio etiam in assumpta humanitate. Et docet eum vocari Dominum nostrum, propter incarnationem, passionem, mortem, & resurrectionem, ascensionem in cælum, & reditu ad iudicium, quum addit, Habemus autem Medicum Dominum nostrum IESVM CHRISTVM, ante secula Filium unigenitū, & in principio Verbum: postea verò & hominem ex Maria virgine. Verbum enim, inquit, caro factum est, incorporalis in corpore, impassibilis in corpore passibili, immortalis in corpore mortali, vita in corruptione, ut de corruptione & morte liberet animas nostras, & sanet eas infusas morbo impietatis, & iniquis desideriis.
units.tr: It is therefore false that the Father alone is called the one God with the Son excluded, and that the Son is called Lord but not one God with the Father. Rather, Ignatius makes the name of true God and of Physician common to the Father and the Son in the divine nature. And afterwards he gives the same name to the Son also in the assumed humanity. He teaches that the Son is called our Lord on account of the incarnation, passion, death and resurrection, ascension into heaven, and return to judgment, when he adds: "We have as our physician our Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son before the ages, and the Word in the beginning, but afterwards also man from the Virgin Mary. For the Word, he says, was made flesh: incorporeal in the body, impassible in a passible body, immortal in a mortal body, life in corruption, so that he might free our souls from corruption and death, and heal them, infected with the disease of impiety and with unrighteous desires."

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Hic Ignatius nomen Dei & Medici commune facit Patri & Filio, & quidem in utraque natura: & docet Filium Dei factum hominem passibilem & mortalem, ut nos à morte liberaret, & sanaret animas nostras. Imo tribuit proprietates utriusque naturæ divinæ & humanæ personæ Christi, ut dicatur Deus verus incorporalis, impassibilis, immortalis, & incorruptibilis: & homo passibilis, corporalis, mortalis, & corruptibilis, iuxta Regulam περὶ κοινωνίας ἰ-διωμάτον, id est, de communicatione proprietatum. Hæc tam copiosè ex omnibus epistolis Ignatij excripsi, ut confirmarem doctrinam Ecclesiæ de expositione Symboli Apostolorum, & confutarem mendacia Gentilis, qui ex truncatis quibusdam sententiis suum errorem stabilire conatur.
units.tr: Here Ignatius makes the name of God and of Physician common to the Father and the Son, and indeed in both natures. He teaches that the Son of God became a passible and mortal man, so that he might free us from death and heal our souls. Indeed, he attributes the properties of each nature, divine and human, to the one person of Christ, so that he is called true God, incorporeal, impassible, immortal and incorruptible, and man, passible, corporeal, mortal and corruptible, according to the rule [περὶ κοινωνίας ἰδιωμάτων], that is, concerning the communication of properties. I have excerpted these things so fully from all the epistles of Ignatius in order to confirm the Church's teaching in the exposition of the Apostles' Creed, and to refute the lies of Gentilis, who tries to establish his error from certain truncated sayings.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Nunc ad Iustinum venio, cuius etsi authoritatem pro suo errore producit: nullam tamen affert ex eo sententiam. Ego verò contra eius testimonia confirmata ex sacris literis profero ad confutandam illam eius impietatem & impudentiam, qua asserit Patri tantùm in scriptis Propheticis & Apostolicis tribui nomen Dei, & Filio nomen Domini.
units.tr: Now I come to Justin, whose authority Gentilis brings forward for his error, yet he cites no sentence from him. But I set against his testimonies those confirmed from the sacred letters, to refute that impiety and impudence of his, by which he asserts that the name of God is attributed to the Father alone in the prophetic and apostolic writings, and the name of Lord to the Son.

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: In colloquio cum Tryphone, in quo ille negat Iesum Christum crucifixum dici in scriptura prophetica Deum. Principio ait, Dominus etiam sibiipsi nomen imposuit, ut qui te redemit, is Deus Israelitici populi in omnium terra vocaretur, Esaiæ 54. Et hanc suam sententiam confirmat ex dicto Esaiæ 55. Nationes quæ te ignorant, te invocabunt & appellabunt. Populíque ij quibus ignotus es ad te confugient, propter Dominum Deum tuum, sanctum Israelis, qui tibi gloriam tribuit. Quaerite Dominum dum inveniri potest, invocate eum dum in propinquo est. Derelinquat impius vias suas, & pravas cogitationes suas eiiciat, redeatque ad Deum. Deinde ex his versibus Psalmi 49. Deus deorum Dominus loquutus est, & vocavit terram, Deus noster aperte veniet, Deus noster nec silebit. Annunciabit[?] caeli iusticiam eius, quod iudex sit Deus. Audi, populemeus, & tecum loquar. Israel, & tibi testificabor, Deus Deus tuus ipse sum. Immola Deo sacrificium laudis, reddeque vota tua Altissimo. Invoca me in die tribulationis, eruam te, & honore me afficies. Peccatori autem dixit Deus.
units.tr: In his dialogue with Trypho, in which he denies that Jesus Christ crucified is called God in the prophetic Scripture, he first says: "The Lord also gave himself a name, so that he who redeemed you should be called the God of the Israelite people in all the earth," Isaiah 54. And he confirms this sentence of his from the saying of Isaiah 55: "The nations that do not know you will call upon you and name you, and the peoples to whom you are unknown will flee to you, on account of the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, who gives you glory. Seek the Lord while he may be found, call on him while he is near. Let the wicked forsake his ways and cast out his wicked thoughts, and return to God." Then from these verses of Psalm 49: "God, the Lord of gods, has spoken and called the earth. Our God will come openly, our God will not be silent. His righteousness will proclaim the heavens, for God is judge. Hear, my people, and I will speak with you. Israel, I will testify to you: I am God, your God. Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High. Call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall honour me." But God said to the sinner...

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: Et ex Psalmo 116. Dixit Dominus Domino meo, Sede ad dextrā meam, quem Psalmum vindicat à falsis Pharisaorum commentis. Et ex versu Psal-mi 62. Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, qui facit mirabilia solus. Hunc e-tiam Psalmum probat exponendum esse non de Salomone, sed de Christo. Et ex versu Psalmi 23: Hic benedictionem consequetur à Domino, & misericor-diam à Deo salutari suo. Tollite portas principes vestras, & introibit rex glo-riae, Dominus exercituum ipse est rex gloriae. Et ex versu Psalmi 45. Thronus tuus Deus in seculum, & in perpetuum: virga aequitatis, virga regni tui. Dile-xisti iusticiam & odisti iniquitatem, propterea unxit te, ô Deus, Deus tuus o-leo laetitiae, & cocupiscet rex decorem tuum, quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, & adorabunt eum.
units.tr: And from Psalm 116: "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand," a psalm which he vindicates from the false inventions of the Pharisees.
