And from a verse of Psalm 62: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who alone does wonders." He also proves that this psalm must be understood not of Solomon but of Christ. And from a verse of Psalm 23: "He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his saviour. Lift up your gates, O princes, and the King of glory shall come in; the Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory." And from a verse of Psalm 45: "Your throne, O God, endures for ever and ever; the sceptre of your kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness. You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness, and the King shall desire your beauty, since he is the Lord your God, and they shall worship him."

units.la: XXI.
units.tr: XXI.

units.la: Hæc loca cùm ab authore epistolæ ad Hebræos citétur cap. 1. ad probãdum Christum esse, dicíque Deum in propheticâ scriptura, & non solum Patrem: nihil opus est, ut plura ex colloquio Iustini cum Tryphone testimonia proferamus, ad probandum, non solum Patrem, sed Filium Dei in Scriptura di-ci Deum.
units.tr: Since the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews cites these passages in chapter 1 to prove that Christ is God, and that he is called God in the prophetic Scripture and not only the Father, there is no need for us to bring forward more testimonies from Justin's dialogue with Trypho, to prove that not only the Father but also the Son of God is called God in Scripture.

units.la: XXII.
units.tr: XXII.

units.la: Hanc potius inspiciamus quaestionem, quam Tryphon Iudaeus quaerit à Iustino, Ut doceat ex prophetica scriptura alium Deum positum & praedica-tum praeter effectorem universi. Hoc enim quaerit Gentilis. cui respondeo cum Iustino, Ad scripturas me refero, tibique persuadere conabor hùc qui Abraha-mo & Iacobo atq; Mosi visus esse dicitur, diversum esse ab eo Deo, qui omnia condidit, numero duo, non consilio & sententia. Scriptura dicit Genes. 19. Sol in terra ortus est, & Loth ingressus est Segor. Túmque Dominus pluit sulphur & ignem à Domino. Et, Dixit Dominus Domino meo, Sede ad dextra meam. Et, Solium tuum Deus in perpetuum. dilexisti iusticiam & odisti iniquitatem, propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus oleo lætitiæ. Et Genesis 31. Ego sum Dominus quem vidisti in loco Dei, ubi mihi columnam unxisti. Eodem capite, Quod si Deũ viribus superasti, & homines superabis. Et, Vidi Deum facie ad faciem. cap. 33. Apparuit ei rursus Dominus postquam ex Mesopotamia Syriæ redisset, eique benedixit. Et Genesis 28. Ego sum Dominus Deus Abrahami, Isaaci. Exo. 2. Moses ait: Dominus Deus patrum nostrorum mihi apparuit. Genesis primo, Faciamus hominem ad imaginem, & similitudinem nostram. Genesis 3. Ecce Adam factus est quasi unus ex nobis. Esaiæ 42. Ego Dominus Deus, hoc nomen meum est, gloriam meam alteri non tradam. Hoc ex contextu orationis dictum Iustinus probat de Filio Dei, non de Patre intelligendum esse, & refutat argumenta Tryphonis, quæ Gentilis nunc repetit.
units.tr: Let us rather consider the question which Trypho the Jew puts to Justin, namely, that he should show from the prophetic Scripture that another God is set forth and proclaimed besides the maker of the universe. For this is what Gentilis asks. To him I answer with Justin: "I refer to the Scriptures, and I will try to persuade you that he who is said to have appeared to Abraham, Jacob and Moses is different from the God who made all things, two in number, though not in purpose and opinion." Scripture says, Genesis 19: "The sun rose upon the earth, and Lot entered Zoar; then the Lord rained brimstone and fire from the Lord." And: "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand." And: "Your throne, O God, is for ever; you have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness." And Genesis 31: "I am the Lord whom you saw in the place of God, where you anointed a pillar for me." In the same chapter: "If you have prevailed against God by strength, you will also prevail against men." And: "I have seen God face to face." Chapter 33: "The Lord appeared to him again, after he had returned from Mesopotamia to Syria, and blessed him." And Genesis 28: "I am the Lord God of Abraham and Isaac." Exodus 2: "Moses says: The Lord God of our fathers appeared to me." Genesis 1: "Let us make man in our image and likeness." Genesis 3: "Behold, Adam has become as one of us." Isaiah 42: "I am the Lord God; this is my name; I will not give my glory to another." Justin proves from the context of this speech that it is to be understood of the Son of God, not of the Father, and he refutes the arguments of Trypho, which Gentilis now repeats.

units.la: X XIII.
units.tr: XXIII.

units.la: Eadem in Apologia ad Antoninum pium proferuntur, contra eos, qui negant Filium Dei esse unum cum Patre Deum. Exodi 3. Ego sum is, qui est Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, Deus Iacob, Deus patrum vestrorum.
units.tr: The same passages are brought forward in the Apology to Antoninus Pius, against those who deny that the Son of God is one God with the Father. Exodus 3: "I am who am, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers."

units.la: X XIIII.
units.tr: X XIIII.

units.la: Eodem loco refutat duas hæreses, quarum prima unam tantum esse personam Patris & Filii, alia Filium non esse unum cum Patre Deum docet. Qui enim, inquit, Filium Patrem esse censent, nec Patrem scire coarguuntur, nec Patri omnium Filium esse cognoscere, qui cum etiam Verbum primogenitum Dei sit, Deus quoque est, qui Mosi cæterisque Prophetis se patefecit.
units.tr: In the same passage he refutes two heresies: the first teaches that the Father and the Son are only one person, the other that the Son is not one God with the Father. For those who suppose that the Son is the Father, he says, are convicted of not knowing the Father, nor of recognising the Son as the Son of the Father of all. Since he is also the firstborn Word of God, he is God too, and he revealed himself to Moses and the other prophets.

units.la: X XV.
units.tr: X XV.

units.la: In expositione fidei est clara confutatio hæresis Gentilis. Igitur inquit, unum Deum colere nos & divinæ scripturæ, & patrum doctrinæ docent. Sit enim unus oportet author omnium, maximè ut nihil extra circumstans ea quæ fiunt labefactet. Etenim si quid ab initio extra Deum erat, id profecto necesse erat, aut Deum, aut vim aliam quamlibet esse confiteri. Ac si Deum quidem id esse dicat quispiam, in divinas voces lituram induxit, quæ aperte clamant, Ego Deus primus sum. Et postea, Et præter me non est Deus.
units.tr: In his exposition of the faith there is a clear refutation of Gentilis's heresy. Therefore, he says, both divine Scripture and the teaching of the Fathers instruct us to worship one God. For there must be one author of all things, above all so that nothing outside him may overturn the things that come to be. For if anything existed from the beginning outside God, it would necessarily follow that we must confess it to be either God or some other power of whatever kind. And if someone should say that it is God, he has drawn a line through the divine words, which plainly cry out: "I am the first God," and afterwards, "And besides me there is no God."

units.la: XXVI.
units.tr: XXVI.

units.la: Ecce, ex his ex quibus Gentilis probat Filium non unum cum Patre Deum esse, Iustinus confirmat eum cum Patre esse Deum. Et addit: Unus igitur verè est Deus omnium, ísque in Patre, Filio, Spiritúque sancto cognoscitur, & intelligitur. Quoniam enim ex sua natura & essentia Pater Filium genuit, & ex eadem processit profectúsque est Spiritus sanctus, iure ac merito ea quæ unius eiusdémque essentiæ sunt, unius etiam atque eiusdem habentur diuinitatis. Respondet etiam ad argumenta cum aliorum hæreticorum, tum Eunomij & Gentilis. Quomodo ergo, dicet aliquis, non differat id quod generat, ab eo quod generatur? & quod processit, ab eo a quo profectum est? Atqui Pater ingenitus est, a quo & Filius generatus est, & profectus Spiritus. Non igitur est idem Filius & Spiritus sanctus, qui Pater. Nam hæc verba Ingenitum, Genitum, Profectum, non naturæ, essentiæque sunt nomina, sed modi quibus res constant. Modus enim constandi (Græcus est τρόπος ὑπάρξεως) his nominibus notatur. Essentiæ vero explicatio, Dei significatur ac declaratur appellatione, ut sit Patris à Filio & Spiritu ex modo constandi distinctio: Identitas autem (ut hoc verbo utar) sit ex ratione essentiæ. Si enim Pater id quod est (τὸ εἶναι) habet ἀγεννήτως, id est ingenito modo, Filius autem γεννητῶς, id est genito modo, & Spiritus cum processione seu profectione, ea quæ distinctionis sunt proprie debent considerari. Si vero etiam personæ ipsius id quod est secundum essentiam significatur, simul id communi diuinitatis declaratur nomine. Non igitur Ingeniti, Geniti & Profecti nomina essentiam declarant, sed hypostases.
units.tr: See, from the very passages by which Gentilis proves that the Son is not one God with the Father, Justin confirms that he is God with the Father. And he adds: "Therefore there is truly one God of all, and he is known and understood in Father, Son and Holy Spirit. For since the Father begat the Son from his own nature and essence, and the Holy Spirit proceeded and issued forth from the same, those things which are of one and the same essence are rightly and deservedly held to have one and the same divinity." He also replies to the arguments both of other heretics and of Eunomius and Gentilis. "How then," someone will say, "does that which begets not differ from that which is begotten, and that which proceeds from that from which it issued? Yet the Father is unbegotten, from whom the Son was begotten and the Spirit proceeded. Therefore the Son and the Holy Spirit are not the same as the Father." For these words, unbegotten, begotten, proceeded, are names not of nature and essence but of the modes in which things subsist. For the mode of subsisting (in Greek it is τρόπος ὑπάρξεως [tropos hyparxeōs]) is designated by these names. But the explanation of essence is signified and declared by the name God, so that the distinction of the Father from the Son and the Spirit lies in the mode of subsisting, while identity (to use this word) lies in the account of essence. For if the Father has what he is (τὸ εἶναι [to einai]) ἀγεννήτως [agennētōs], that is, in an unbegotten mode, and the Son γεννητῶς [gennētōs], that is, in a begotten mode, and the Spirit with procession or proceeding, then the things that belong to distinction ought properly to be considered. But if what the person itself is according to essence is also signified, this is at the same time declared by the common name of divinity. Therefore the names Unbegotten, Begotten and Proceeding do not declare essence, but hypostases."

units.la: XXVII.
units.tr: XXVII.

units.la: Probat etiam Patrem & Filium, & Spiritum sanctum esse unum Deum, ex dicto Christi Matthæi 26. Euntes ergo docete omnes Gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris & Filii, & Spiritus sancti. Et Pauli 2. ad Corinthios 13. Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi, & charitas Dei, & communicatio sancti Spiritus sit cum omnibus vobis. Et ad Ephesios 2. In ipso summo angulari lapide Iesu Christo, in quo omnis ædificatio constructa, crescit. In quo & vos coædificamini in habitaculū Dei in Spiritu sancto. Videsne, inquit, ut ædificiū quod Christi nomine paratur docens, quo Christi templum efficimur, quemadmodum scriptū est: Inhabitabo in eis, & inambulabo, eróque eorum Deus? tres nobis personas coniunctè colligit.
units.tr: He also proves that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God, from Christ's saying in Matthew 26: "Go therefore, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit." And from Paul, 2 Corinthians 13: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all." And Ephesians 2: "In Jesus Christ himself, the chief cornerstone, in whom the whole building, fitly framed together, grows. In whom you also are built together into a habitation of God in the Spirit." Do you see, he says, how the building that is prepared in the name of Christ, by teaching through which we are made the temple of Christ, as it is written: "I will dwell in them, and walk among them, and I will be their God," gathers three persons together for us?

units.la: XXVIII.
units.tr: XXVIII.

units.la: Et post similia testimonia ut ad Ephesios: Huius rei gratia flecto genua mea ad Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ut det vobis corroborari per eius Spiritum in nouum hominem, vt Christus per fidem habitet in cordibus vestris, &c. Et 2. ad Corinthios 1. Deus qui nos vobiscum in Christo confirmat, nósque vnxit, & nos signauit, deditque pignus Spiritus in cordibus nostris. Ad Galatas 4. Quoniam autem estis filii Dei, misit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda vestra, clamantem, Abba Pater.
units.tr: And after similar testimonies, such as Ephesians: "For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, that he would grant you to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith," etc. And 2 Corinthians 1: "God, who establishes us with you in Christ, and has anointed us, and sealed us, and given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts." Galatians 4: "Because you are sons of God, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father."

units.la: XXIX.
units.tr: XXIX.

units.la: Post haec inquam testimonia & similia, tandem sic concludit: Quamobrem unum Deum par est nos profiteri, qui in Patre ac Filio, & Spiritu sancto intelligatur: ita tamen ut hoc quidem ipso, quod Pater, ac Filius, & Spiritus sanctus sunt unius divinitatis, personas cognoscamus: eo autem ipso quod Deus sunt, ad quod commune est personarum, in natura & essentia intelligamus. Nam & unitas in trinitate, & trinitas in unitate intelligitur. Quod quomodo fiat, nec quaerere alios velim, nec mihi ipsi persuadere possum, me verba quae de rebus abstrusis sunt, lingua lutea impuraque caruncula audere profiteri.
units.tr: After these and similar testimonies, I say, he finally concludes thus: "Wherefore it is fitting that we confess one God, who is understood in Father, Son and Holy Spirit; yet in such a way that by the very fact that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are of one divinity, we recognise them as persons, but by the very fact that they are God, which is common to the persons, we understand them in nature and essence. For both unity is understood in trinity, and trinity in unity. How this is done, I would not wish to ask others, nor can I persuade myself, I who dare to profess things that are hidden with a muddy tongue, an impure little scrap of flesh."

units.la: Vade nunc mendax & impudens haeretice, & frontem perfrica, negando Filium, & Spiritum sanctum unum cum Patre Deum esse, & affirmando sanctam & individuam trinitatem Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum unum Deum, humanum commentum scripturae sacrae & Catholicis ignotum esse, & Iustinum tibi patrocinari.
units.tr: Go now, lying and shameless heretic, and rub your forehead, denying that the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God with the Father, and affirming that the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, one God, is a human invention unknown to Holy Scripture and to Catholics, and that Justin is your patron.

units.la: XXX.
units.tr: XXX.

units.la: Iustino coaevus fuit Irenaeus, discipulus Polycarpi, qui lib. 3. contra haereses Valentini capite 6. scriptum reliquit: Neque igitur Dominus, neque Spiritus sanctus, neque Apostoli cum qui non esset Deus, definitiue & absolute Deum nominassent, nisi esset verus Deus: neque Dominum appellassent aliquem ex sua persona, nisi qui Dominus omnium Deum Patrem & Filium eius, qui dominium accepit a Patre suo, omnis conditionis, quemadmodum habet illud: Dixit Dominus Domino meo, Sede a dextris meis, quousque ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum. Patre enim Filio colloquutum ostendit, qui & dedit ei haereditatem Gentium, & subiecit ei omnes inimicos. Vere igitur quum pater sit Dominus, & Filius vere sit Dominus, merito Spiritus sanctus Domini appellatione signauit eos. Et iterum in euersione Sodomitarum Scriptura ait: Et pluit Dominus super Sodomam & Gomorram ignem & sulphur a Domino de caelo. Filium enim hic significat qui & Abrahae collocutus sit, a Patre accepisse potestatem ad iudicandum Sodomitas, propter iniquitatem eorum. Similiter habet illud: Sedes tua Deus in aeternum, virga directionis virga regni tui. Dilexisti iustitiam, & odisti iniquitatem, propterea unxit te o Deus, Deus tuus. Utroque enim, Dei appellatione significauit Spiritus, & eum qui ungitur, Filium, & eum qui ungit, id est, Patrem. Et iterum, Deus stetit in Synagoga deorum: in medio autem deos discernit, de Patre, & Filio, & his qui adoptionem meruerūt[?], dicit, Hi autem sunt Ecclesia. Hæc enim est Synagoga Dei, quam Deus, hoc est, Filius per seipsum collegit. de quo iterum dicit: Deus Deorum loquutus est, & vocauit terrā. quis Deus? de quo dicit: Deus manifestè veniet, Deus noster, & non silebit, hoc est, Filius qui secundum manifestationem hominibus aduenit.
units.tr: A contemporary of Justin was Irenaeus, a disciple of Polycarp, who in book 3 against the heresies, chapter 6, against Valentinus, left this in writing: "Therefore neither the Lord, nor the Holy Spirit, nor the Apostles would have named anyone definitively and absolutely God, unless he were true God; nor would they have called anyone Lord from his own person, unless he were the Lord of all, God the Father and his Son, who received dominion from his Father over every creature, as that passage has it: 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.' For he shows that the Father spoke with the Son, who both gave him the inheritance of the Gentiles and subjected all his enemies to him. Truly, then, since the Father is Lord and the Son is truly Lord, the Spirit has rightly marked them both with the appellation of Lord. And again, at the overthrow of the Sodomites, Scripture says: 'And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah fire and brimstone from the Lord out of heaven.' For here it signifies the Son, who also spoke with Abraham, having received from the Father power to judge the Sodomites for their iniquity. In the same way is that passage: 'Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; the sceptre of your kingdom is a sceptre of righteousness. You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you.' For by the name God the Spirit signified both him who is anointed, the Son, and him who anoints, that is, the Father. And again: 'God stood in the congregation of gods; in the midst he judges the gods,' speaking of the Father and the Son and those who have merited adoption; these, he says, are the Church. For this is the congregation of God, which God, that is the Son, gathered by himself. Of him he says again: 'The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken, and called the earth.' What God? He of whom it says: 'Our God shall come manifestly, and shall not keep silent,' that is, the Son, who came to men in manifestation."

units.la: XXXI.
units.tr: XXXI.

units.la: Nemo igitur Deus aut Dominus appellatur, nisi qui est Dominus omnium & Deus: qui & Mosi ait, Ego sum qui sum. Et de quo Elias, Si vnus est Dominus Deus, venite post eum. Et iterum ait sacerdotibus idolorum, Vos inuocabitis in nomine deorum vestrorum, & ego inuocabo in nomine Domini Dei mei: & Deus qui exaudiet hodie, ipse est Deus. Sic autem inuocat: Domine Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, Deus Iacob, exaudi me hodie. Et intelliget omnis populus quoniam tu es Deus Israel.
units.tr: Therefore no one is called God or Lord, except him who is the Lord and God of all; who also said to Moses: "I am who I am." And of whom Elijah said: "If the Lord is God, follow him." And again he said to the priests of the idols: "You shall call on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord my God; and the God who answers by fire, he is God." And he calls thus: "O Lord God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob, hear me this day. And all the people shall know that you are God in Israel."

units.la: XXXII.
units.tr: XXXII.

units.la: Oratio Irenæi.
units.tr: Irenaeus's Prayer.

units.la: Et igitur te inuoco Domine Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, Deus Iacob, Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, Deus qui per multitudinem misericordiæ tuæ bene sensisti in nobis, qui fecisti cœlum & terram, & dominaris omnium, qui es solus & verus Deus, super quem alius Deus non est, præter Dominum nostrum IESVM CHRISTVM, dominatione qua dominaris Spiritus sancti: da omni legenti hanc scripturam cognoscere te, quia solus Deus es, & confirmari in eo, & abscistere ab omni hæretica, & quæ est sine Deo impia sententia. Hæc Irenæus.
units.tr: And so I call upon you, Lord God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, God who in the abundance of your mercy have been well disposed toward us, who made heaven and earth and rule over all things, who alone are the true God, beside whom there is no other God, except our Lord JESUS CHRIST, through the dominion by which you rule the Holy Spirit. Grant that everyone who reads this writing may come to know that you alone are God, and be confirmed in this, and turn away from every heretical and godless opinion that is without God. Thus Irenaeus.

units.la: XXXIII.
units.tr: XXXIII.

units.la: Sequentibus capitibus docet ex scripturis, neminem ex Prophetis, & Apostolis confessum fuisse Dominum Deum alium Dominum atque Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: In the following chapters he teaches from the Scriptures that none of the Prophets and Apostles confessed the Lord God to be another Lord than the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: XXXIIII.
units.tr: XXXIV.

units.la: Clemens Alexandrinus in adhortatione ad Græcos: Hic ergo Verbum Christus, & vt nos olim essemus. Erat enim in Deo, & vt bene essemus causa fuit. Nunc autem apparuit hominibus hic ipse Verbum, qui solus est ambo, Deus & homo, & est nobis omnium causa bonorum, à quo edocti rectè viuere ad vitam æternam transmittimur. Nam vt ait diuinus ille Domini Apostolus: Gratia Dei salutaris omnibus hominibus apparuit, docens nos vt abnegantes impietatem & sæcularia desideria, moderatè & piè viuamus in hoc sæculo, expectantes beatam spem & aduentum gloriæ magni Dei, & saluatoris nostri Iesu Christi. Hoc est canticum nouum aduentus, qui nunc refulsit in nobis verbi, qui erat in principio, & prius fuit. Apparuit autem qui est, in eo qui est verbū, qui erat apud Deū, doctor apparuit, per quē omnia sunt fabricata. Verbum qui cum eo quod finxit vitam simul præbuit in principio vt opifex, bene viuere docuit cùm apparuisset vt Magister, vt postea semper viuere suppeditaret, vt Deus.
units.tr: Clement of Alexandria, in his Exhortation to the Greeks: This Word, then, is Christ, who was the cause of our existence of old, for he was in God, and was the cause of our well-being. But now this same Word has appeared to men, he who alone is both God and man, and he is the cause of all good things for us, by whom, being taught to live rightly, we are sent on to eternal life. For, as that divine Apostle of the Lord says: The saving grace of God has appeared to all men, teaching us that, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly and piously in this world, looking for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ. This is the new song of the coming, which has now shone upon us, of the Word, who was in the beginning and existed before. He has appeared, indeed, who is, in him who is the Word, who was with God, and through whom all things were made. He appeared as Teacher, the Word who, together with what he formed, gave life at the beginning as Maker, and taught us to live well when he appeared as Master, so that afterwards he might always supply us with life, as God.

units.la: XXXV.
units.tr: XXXV.

units.la: In pædagogo cap. 12. Atqui mihi quidem is ipse videtur hominem finxisse ex puluere, aqua autem regenerasse, Spiritu vero auxisse, Verbo autem pædagogi instar instituisse, ad filiorum adoptionem & salutem sanctis præceptis dirigens, vt cum terra genitum, & in Sanctum & supercœlestem hominem suo aduentu transformasset, diuinam illam vocem maximè impleret: Faciamus hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem nostram, atque fuit quidem Christus, Hoc plenum quod dixit Deus.
units.tr: In the Paedagogus, chapter 12: Indeed, it seems to me that he himself formed man from dust, but regenerated him by water, increased him by the Spirit, and instructed him by the Word as a tutor, directing him by holy precepts to adoption and salvation as sons; so that, having transformed him, born of earth, into a holy and heavenly man by his coming, he might most fully fulfil that divine voice: Let us make man in our image and likeness. And indeed it was Christ; this is the full meaning of what God said.

units.la: Eadem oratione adhortatoria ad Gentes, exponit hæc dicta de Patre, Filio & Spiritu sancto. Audi Israel, Dominus Deus tuus, Dominus vnus est. Et: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli seruies. Deus propinquus ego sum, & non Deus procul: si fecerit homo aliquid in occulto, & ego nō videbo ipsum? An non cœlum & terram ego impleo, dicit Dominus? Quis metietur cœlum palmo, & terram omnem pugillo? A facie tua montes liquescent, sicut cera à facie ignis. Is est, inquit, Deus, cuius cœlum est thronus, terra autem scabellum pedum eius. Videte, videte quòd ego sum, & non alius Deus est præter me. Ego occìdam & viuere faciam. Ecce, ego firmans tonitru & creans Spiritum, manus quoque meæ cœli fundarunt militiam. Ego sum Dominus. Ego sum qui loquor iustitiam, & annuncio veritatem. Ego Deus & præter me non est Iustus. Et seruator non est excepto me. Conuertimini ad me, & salui estote qui estis ex finibus terræ. Ego sum Deus & non est alius.
units.tr: In the same hortatory address to the Gentiles, he expounds these sayings concerning the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Hear, Israel, the Lord your God, the Lord is one. And: You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone. I am a God near at hand, and not a God far off: if a man does anything in secret, shall I not see him? Do I not fill heaven and earth, says the Lord? Who shall measure the heavens with a span, and all the earth with a handful? The mountains shall melt from before your face, as wax before the fire. He, he says, is God, whose throne is heaven and the earth the footstool of his feet. See, see that I am, and there is no other God besides me. I will kill, and I will make alive. Behold, I establish thunder and create the Spirit; my hands also have founded the host of heaven. I am the Lord. I am he who speaks righteousness and declares truth. I am God, and there is no other just one beside me. And there is no Saviour apart from me. Turn to me, and be saved, you who are from the ends of the earth. I am God, and there is no other.

units.la: XXXVI. Tertullianus contra Praxeam:
units.tr: XXXVI. Tertullian against Praxeas:

units.la: Nos verò & semper, & nunc magis, vt instructiores per Paracletum, deductorem scilicet omnis veritatis, vnicum quidem Deum credimus, sub hac tamen dispensatione, quam οἰκονομίαν dicimus, vt vnici Dei sit, & Filius sermo ipsius, qui ex ipso Patre in virginem descendit, & ex ea natum hominem, & Deum Filium hominis, & Filium Dei & cognominatum Iesum Christum, hunc passum, hunc mortuum, & sepultum secùdum scripturas, & resuscitatum à Patre, & in cœlo resumptum, sedere ad dextram Patris, venturum p.1. iudicare vivos & mortuos, qui exinde emiserit secundum promissionem suam à Patre, Spiritum sanctum paracletum, sanctificatorem fidei eorum, qui credunt in Patrem, Filium & Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: But we, always, and now more so, as better instructed through the Paraclete, the guide, that is, of all truth, believe indeed in one God, yet under this dispensation, which we call oikonomia [οἰκονομία], that there is one God whose Son is his Word, who came down from the Father himself into the virgin, and was born of her as man and God, the Son of man and Son of God, and named Jesus Christ; that this one suffered, this one died and was buried according to the Scriptures, and was raised again by the Father, and taken up into heaven, and sits at the right hand of the Father, and will come to judge the living and the dead, and who from there sent forth, according to his promise, from the Father, the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, the sanctifier of the faith of those who believe in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: XXXVII.
units.tr: XXXVII.

units.la: Sed salua ista praescriptione, ubique tamen propter instructionem, & munitionem quorundam dandus est etiam tractatibus locus, ne videatur unaquaeque peruersitas, non examinata, sed praeiudicata damnari, maximè haec quae se existimat meram veritatem possidere, dum unicum Deum non aliàs putat credendum, quàm si ipsum eundemque, & Patrem & Filium, & Spiritum sancti dicat, quasi non sic quoque unus sit omnia, dum ex uno omnia per substantiae scilicet unitatem, & nihilominus custodiatur οἰκονομίας sacramentum, quae unitatem & trinitatem disponit, tres dirigens Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum. Tres autem non statu, sed gradu: nec substantia, sed forma: nec potestate, sed specie. Vnius autem substantiae & unius status, & unius potestatis, quia unus Deus, ex quo & gradus isti, & formae & species in nomine Patris, & Filii & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: But, this rule being preserved, nevertheless, for the sake of instruction and defence of some, room must also be given to discussion everywhere, lest every perversity should seem to be condemned unexamined and prejudged, especially this one, which thinks it possesses pure truth, while it supposes that the one God is not to be believed in except by saying that the same one is both Father and Son and Holy Spirit, as if he were not thus also one, all things being from one through the unity of substance; and yet the mystery of the oikonomia [οἰκονομία] is kept, which arranges the unity and the trinity, setting out three, Father and Son and Holy Spirit. But three not in condition, but in degree; not in substance, but in form; not in power, but in appearance. Yet of one substance, one condition and one power, because it is one God from whom those degrees, forms and appearances come, in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: XXXVIII.
units.tr: XXXVIII.

units.la: Simplices enim quique, ne dixerim imprudentes & idiotae, quae maior sem [?] per credentium pars est, quoniam & ipsa regula fidei à pluribus diis seculi ad unicum & verum Deum transfert, non intelligentes, unicum quidem, sed cum sua οἰκονομίᾳ esse credendum: expauescunt ad οἰκονομίας numerum, & dispositionem trinitatis, diuisionem praesumunt unitatis. Quando unitas ex seipsa deriuans trinitatem, non destruatur ab illa, sed administretur.
units.tr: For simple people, not to say unlearned and ignorant, who make up the greater part of believers, since the rule of faith itself transfers them from the many gods of the world to the one and true God, not understanding that the one God is to be believed in with his oikonomia [οἰκονομίᾳ], shrink back from the number of the oikonomia [οἰκονομίας] and the arrangement of the Trinity, and presume a division of the unity. Whereas the unity, deriving the Trinity from itself, is not destroyed by it, but is administered by it.

units.la: XXXIX.
units.tr: XXXIX.

units.la: Colligit Tertullianus loca scripturae quae probant tres personas in uno Deo.
units.tr: Tertullian gathers passages of Scripture which prove three persons in one God.

units.la: Et post longam disputationem addit: Si enim una persona & Dei & Domini in scripturis inueniretur, merito Christus non esset admissus ad nomen Dei, & ad Domini. Nemo enim alius praeter quam unus Deus & unus Dominus praedicabatur, & futurum erat, ut ipse Pater descendere videretur, quia unus Deus, & unus Dominus legebatur, & tota οἰκονομία eius obumbraretur, quae in materiam fidei prospecta atque dispensata est. At vbi venit Christus, & cognitus est à nobis quòd ipse qui numerum retro fecerat, factus secundus à Patre, & cum Spiritu tertius, & tamen Pater per ipsum, Pater, plenius & manifestius redactum est nomen Dei & Domini in vnione: & quia [?]ationis erat, ut à multitudine idolorum transirent ad unicum Deum, ut diffe-rentia ventia constitueretur inter cultores vnius & plurimæ diuinitatis. Nam & lucere in mundo Christianos oportebat vt filios lucis, lumen mundi, vnum & Dominum colentes, & nominantes.
units.tr: And after a long discussion he adds: "For if one person were found in the Scriptures as both God and Lord, Christ would rightly not have been admitted to the name of God and of Lord. For no one else was proclaimed except the one God and the one Lord, and it was going to happen that the Father himself would seem to come down, because it was read that there is one God and one Lord, and the whole economy of him would be overshadowed, which was foreseen and dispensed for the matter of faith. But when Christ came, and was known by us, that he who had made the number earlier, having been made second from the Father, and with the Spirit third, and yet the Father through him remains Father, the name of God and Lord was brought back more fully and more plainly into unity; and because it was [?] of the purpose that they should pass from a multitude of idols to the one God, so that a difference might be established between the worshippers of the one divinity and of the many. For Christians also ought to shine in the world as sons of light, the light of the world, worshipping and naming one God and Lord."

units.la: XL.
units.tr: XL.

units.la: Solum autem Christum potero Deum dicere, sicut Apostolus, Ex quibus Christus, qui est (inquit) Deus super omnia benedictus in secula. Citat etiam ad id probandum dictum Mosis: Pluit super Sodomam & Gomorrham ignem & sulphurem Deus à Deo.
units.tr: I can call Christ alone God, as the Apostle does: "From whom is Christ, who is God over all, blessed for ever." He also cites to prove this the saying of Moses: "The Lord rained fire and brimstone upon Sodom and Gomorrah, from the Lord."

units.la: XLI.
units.tr: XLI.

units.la: Expositio primi articuli symboli,
units.tr: Exposition of the first article of the creed

units.la: Credo in vnum Deum Patrem omnipotentem, à Tertulliano, qui respondet ad argumenta hæreticorum, quibus probabant solum Patrem dici Deum omnipotentem. Omnia inquit, Patris, mea sunt, cur non & nomina? Quum ergo legis, Deum omnipotentem & Altissimum, & Deum virtutum, & Regem Israelis, & Qui est, vide ne per hæc Filius etiam demonstretur suo iure Deus, quia sermo Dei omnipotentis, & quia omnium accepit potestatem: Altissimus, quia dextra Dei exaltatus, & quia omnia sunt illi subiecta à Patre: Rex Israelis, quia illi proprie excidit sors gentis istius. Si autem volunt Christi nomen Patris esse, audient suo loco. Interim hic mihi promotum sit responsum aduersus id quod & de Apocalypsi Iohannis proferunt: Ego Dominus qui est, & qui erat, & qui fuit, & venit omnipotens. Et sicubi alibi Dei omnipotentis appellationem non putant etiam Filio conuenire, quasi qui venturus non sit omnipotens, cùm & Filius omnipotentis tam omnipotens sit Dei Filius, quàm Deus Dei Filius.
units.tr: "I believe in one God the Father almighty": Tertullian, answering the arguments of the heretics, by which they proved that only the Father is called almighty God. "All things," he says, "are the Father's, and they are mine; why not the names too? When therefore you read 'God almighty and Most High,' and 'God of hosts,' and 'King of Israel,' and 'He who is,' see whether through these the Son too is shown to be God by his own right, because he is the Word of God almighty, and because he received the power of all things; Most High, because he was exalted at the right hand of God, and because all things are subjected to him by the Father; King of Israel, because the lot of that nation fell properly to him. But if they want the name of Christ to be the Father's, they will hear it in its place. Meanwhile let this answer be put forward for me against what they also bring from the Apocalypse of John: 'I am the Lord who is, and who was, and who came, almighty.' And wherever elsewhere they think the appellation 'God almighty' does not also belong to the Son, as though he who is to come were not almighty, since the Son of the Almighty is just as almighty as the Son of God is God."

units.la: XLII.
units.tr: XLII.

units.la: Sed hanc societatem nominum paternorum in Filio ne perspiciant, perturbat illos scriptura, si quando vnicum Deum statuit: quasi non eadem & Deos, & dominorum Dominos proposuerit, vt supra ostendimus. Ergo quia duos, & vnū inquirit inuenimus, ideo ambo vnus atque idem, & Filius, & Pater. Porro non periclitatur scriptura, vt illi de tua argumentatione succurras, ne sibi contraria dicere videatur. Habet enim rationem, & quum vnicum Deum statuit, & quum duos Patrem & Filium ostendit, & sufficit sibi. Filium nominari ab ea cõstat Deum. saluo enim Filio recte vnicum Deum potest determinasse, cuius est Filius. Non enim desinit esse qui habet Filium, ipse vnicus suo scilicet nomine quoties sine filio nominatur. Sine filio autem nominatur, cū principaliter determinatur, vt prima persona, quæ ante Filii nomen erat præponēda, quia Pater antè cognoscitur, & post Patrē Filius nominatur.
units.tr: But lest they perceive this fellowship of paternal names in the Son, Scripture disturbs them whenever it sets up one God, as though it had not likewise set forth gods and lords of lords, as we showed above. Therefore, since we find "two" and "one" in the Scriptures, both are one and the same, both Son and Father. Further, Scripture is not in danger, so that you should come to the aid of those who, by your argument, would seem to say contrary things to themselves. For it has its reason: when it sets up one God, and when it shows two, Father and Son, it is sufficient for itself. It is agreed that the Son is named God by it; for, the Son being preserved, it could rightly have declared the one God, whose Son he is. For he who has a Son does not cease to be; he himself is one, in his own name, as often as he is named without the Son. He is named without the Son, however, when he is determined principally, as the first person, who had to be placed before the name of the Son, because the Father is known before, and after the Father the Son is named.

units.la: XLIII.
units.tr: XLIII.

units.la: Igitur unus Deus Pater, & absque eo alius non est. Quod ipse inserens non Filium negat, sed alium Deum. Caeterum alius Deus à Patre solus non est. Denique inspice sequentia huiusmodi pronunciationum, & invenies fere ad idolorum facilitatores atque cultores definitionem earum pertinere, ut multitudinem falsorum deorum unio divinitatis expellat: habens tamen Filium, quanto induiduum & inseparatum à Patre, tanto in Patre reputandum, etsi non nominatum. Atqui si nominasset cum, separasset ita dicens: Alium praeter me non nisi Filius meus: alium etiam Filium fecisset, quem de aliis excepisset, itaque praeter seipsum non esse alium Deum: hoc propter idololatriam tam nationum quàm Israelis: etiam propter haereticos, qui sicut nationes manibus, ita ipsi verbis idola fabricantur, id est, alium Deum & alium Christum.
units.tr: Therefore God the Father is one, and apart from him there is no other. In inserting this, he does not deny the Son, but another God. Moreover, another God is not alone apart from the Father. Finally, examine the following statements of this kind, and you will find that they pertain nearly to the definition of those who make idols easy and worship them, so that the unity of the divinity may drive out the multitude of false gods; having the Son, however, as much as he is inseparable and undivided from the Father, so much is he to be reckoned in the Father, even if not named. And yet if he had named him, separating him, saying thus, "Apart from me there is no other except my Son," he would have made the Son another, whom he had excepted from the others, so that besides himself there is no other God. This is said on account of the idolatry both of the nations and of Israel, and also on account of the heretics, who, as the nations fashion idols with hands, so they themselves fashion idols with words, that is, another God and another Christ.

units.la: XLIIII.
units.tr: XLIIII.

units.la: Ad alia scripturae loca citata ab haereticis, Extendit cælum solus, respondet ex Euangelio: Omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Proinde & Filii vox erit: Extendi cælum solus, sicut in Psalmo dicitur: Verbo Domini cœli firmati sunt: quia sophia in Sermone assistente paratum est cœlum, & omnia per Sermonem sunt facta. competit & Filium solum extendisse cœlum, quia solus operationi Patris ministrauit. Idem erit dicens: Ego primus & in superuentu-ra, & praeter me non est Deus. In principio enim erat sermo, & sermo erat apud Deum, & Deus erat sermo. Et addit:
units.tr: To the other passages of Scripture cited by the heretics, "He alone stretched out the heavens," he answers from the Gospel: "All things were made through him." Therefore the voice of the Son will also be: "I alone stretched out the heavens," as it is said in the Psalm: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were established"; because the Wisdom, standing by in the Word, prepared the heavens, and all things were made through the Word. It is also fitting that the Son alone stretched out the heavens, because he alone ministered to the operation of the Father. He will be the same, speaking: "I am the first, and in the future, and apart from me there is no God." For in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word. And he adds:

units.la: XLV.
units.tr: XLV.

units.la: Nam in veteribus nihil tenent aliud quàm Ego Deus, & alius praeter me non est. Et in Euangelio: Ego & Pater vnum sumus. Et, Qui me videt, videt etiam Patrem meum. His tribus capitulis totam scripturam utriusque testamenti volunt credere. Sed si propter ea eundem & Patrem & Filium credendum putant, ut vnum Deum vindicent, salua est vnio eius, qui cùm sit vnus, habeat & Filium æquè & ipsum eisdem scripturis comprehensum. Si Filium nolunt secundum à Patre reputari, ne secundus duos faciat deos dici, ostendimus duos Deos in scriptura relatos, & duos Dominos: & tamen ne de isto scandaliz-aretur, rationem reddimus, qua Dij non duo dicatur, nec Domini, sed quia Pater & Filius duo, & hoc non ex separatione substantiæ, sed ex dispositione, cùm induiduü & inseparatū Filii à Patre pronunciamus, nec sta-tu, sed gradu, alium, qui etsi Deus dicatur, quando nominatur singularis, non ideo duos Deos faciat, sed unum, hoc ipso quod & Deus ex unitate Patris vocari habeat.
units.tr: For in the old things they hold nothing else than "I am God, and there is no other besides me." And in the Gospel: "I and the Father are one." And: "He who sees me sees also my Father." These three chapters they want to be believed to comprise the whole of Scripture in both Testaments. But if on account of these they think the same one is to be believed both Father and Son, so that they may vindicate one God, the unity of him is safe, who, since he is one, has the Son equally, comprehended in the same Scriptures as himself. If they are unwilling for the Son to be reckoned second from the Father, lest the second makes them say there are two gods, we show that two Gods are related in Scripture, and two Lords; and yet, lest anyone be scandalised by this, we give the reason why they are not said to be two gods, nor two lords, but because the Father and the Son are two. This is not from separation of substance but from disposition, since we pronounce the Son undivided and inseparable from the Father, and another not in standing but in degree, who, although he is called God when he is named in the singular, does not therefore make two gods, but one, by this very fact that he also has to be called God from the unity of the Father.

units.la: Summa. Quæ Tertullianus cōtra Praxeam ex scriptura profert testimonia ad probandum Filium non esse eandem, sed aliam à Patre personam: Gentilis torquet ad probandum Filium nō esse unum cum Patre Deum. Et solum Patrem esse unum Deum, & Filium alium à Patre Deum.
units.tr: Summary. What testimonies from Scripture Tertullian brings forward against Praxeas to prove that the Son is not the same, but another person from the Father, Gentilis twists to prove that the Son is not one God with the Father, and that only the Father is the one God, and the Son is a God other than the Father.

units.la: XLVII.
units.tr: XLVII.

units.la: Cyprianus in expositione Symboli Apostolorū ait Orientales dicere: Crede in uno Deo Patre omnipotente, & in CHRISTO IESU unico Filio eius. Deus autem inquit naturæ ipsius vel substantiæ, quæ est super omnia, est appellatio. Pater arcani & invisibilis sacramenti vocabulū est. Definit etiā Deum, substantiam, sine initio, sine fine, simplicem, sine ulla admixtione, invisibilem, incorpoream, ineffabilem, inæstimabilem, in qua nihil adiunctum, nihil creatum sit. Docet etiam in Patre Filium intelligēdum esse, Patrem, inquit, quum audis, Filium intellige & Patrem, cuius est imago & substantia. Hoc ergo ipso nomine quo Deus Pater appellatur, cum Patre pariter subsistere etiam Filius demonstratur. Credendus est ergo Deus Pater esse unici Filij Domini nostri, non discutiēdus. Neque enim fas est de natalibus Domini disputare. Contestatus est Pater de cælis dicens: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo bene complacui, ipsum audite. Filius dicit: Qui vidit me, vidit & Patrem. An non credis quòd ego in Patre, & Pater in me est? Ego & Pater unum sumus. Qui est qui inter has Patris & Filij voces, medium se interserat, & deitatem dividat, affectum separet, & substantiam rumpat, Spiritum secet, neget esse verū quod veritas dicit?
units.tr: Cyprian, in the exposition of the Apostles' Creed, says that the Easterners say: "Believe in one God the Father almighty, and in CHRIST JESUS his only Son." "God," he says, is the name of his nature or substance, which is above all things. "Father" is the name of the hidden and invisible mystery. He also defines God as substance, without beginning, without end, simple, without any admixture, invisible, incorporeal, ineffable, inestimable, in whom nothing is added and nothing created. He also teaches that the Son is to be understood in the Father: "When you hear 'Father,'" he says, "understand also the Son, whose image and substance the Father is." By this very name by which God is called Father, it is shown that the Son also subsists equally with the Father. God the Father is therefore to be believed to be the Father of the only Son, our Lord, and not to be examined, for it is not lawful to dispute about the birth of the Lord. The Father bore witness from heaven, saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him." The Son says: "He who has seen me has seen also the Father." Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? "I and the Father are one." Who is it who, placing himself between these voices of Father and Son, divides the Godhead, separates the affection, breaks the substance, cuts the Spirit, and denies that to be true which the truth says?

units.la: XLVIII.
units.tr: XLVIII.

units.la: Quod diximus Orientis Ecclesias tradere Patrem omnipotentem, & unum Dominum, hoc modo intelligendum est: Unum non numero dici, sed uniuersitate, ut exempli causa, si dicamus unum solem. Hic unus ita dicitur, ut alius, vel tertius addi non possit, unus sol. Sic Deus propterea unus dicitur, quòd alius non sit. Similiter & de Domino accipiendum est, quòd unus sit Dominus Iesus Christus, per quem Deus Pater dominatum omnium tenet, unde & sequens Sermo omnipotentem pronunciat Dominum. Omnipotens autem ab eo dicitur, quòd omnium teneat potentatum. Tenet autem omnia per Filium, sicut Apostolus dicit, quia per ipsum creata sunt omnia visibilia, & invisibilia. Quia sicut lux de luce, & veritas de veritate, ita de omnipotente omnipotens nascitur, ut in Apocalypsi Iohannis de Seraphin scriptum est: Et requiem non habebant dicentes, Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus qui est, & qui venturus est omnipotens.
units.tr: What we said, that the Eastern Churches hand down God the Father almighty and one Lord, must be understood in this way: "one" is said not by number but by unity, as when we say "one sun," for example. The sun is called one in such a way that no second or third can be added. So God is called one because there is no other. The same must be understood of the Lord, that there is one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom God the Father holds dominion over all things. For this reason the following creed also proclaims the Lord almighty. He is called almighty because he holds power over all things. He holds all things through the Son, as the Apostle says, because all things visible and invisible were created through him. For just as light is born of light, and truth of truth, so the Almighty is born of the Almighty, as is written in the Apocalypse of John concerning the Seraphim: "And they did not rest, saying, Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God, who is and who is to come, the Almighty."

units.la: XLIX.
units.tr: XLIX.

units.la: Origenes περὶ ἀρχῶν cap. 1. seruetur Ecclesiastica praedicatio per successionis ordinem ab Apostolis tradita, & usque ad praesens in Ecclesiis permanes. Illa sola credenda est veritas, quae in nullo ab Ecclesiastica discordat traditione. Primò, quod unus sit Deus, qui omnia creauit atque composuit, quique ex nullis fecit esse universa, Deus a prima creatura, & conditione mundi, & omnium iustorum, Deus Adam, Abel, Seth, Enos, Enoch, Noe, Sem, Abraham, Isaac, Iacob, duodecim Patriarcharum, Mosis & Prophetarum, & quod hic Deus in nouissimis diebus, sicut per Prophetas suos ante promiserat, misit Dominum Iesum Christum: primò quidem vocaturum Israel, secundò vero etiam gentes post perfidiam populi Israel. Hic Deus iustus & bonus, Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, legem & Prophetas, & Euangelia ipse dedit, qui & Apostolorum Deus est, & veteris & noui Testamenti. Tum deinde quia Iesus Christus ipse qui venit ante omnem creaturam natus ex Patre est, qui cum in omnium conditione Patri ministraret (per ipsum enim omnia facta sunt) nouissimis temporibus seipsum exinaniens factus est homo, incarnatus est quum Deus esset, & homo mansit, quod Deus erat.
units.tr: Origen, On First Principles [περὶ ἀρχῶν], chapter 1. The ecclesiastical preaching handed down from the Apostles in an order of succession, and remaining in the Churches until now, is to be kept. Only that truth is to be believed which in no point disagrees with ecclesiastical tradition. First, that there is one God, who created and arranged all things and made the whole universe out of nothing: God from the first creature and the foundation of the world, and God of all the righteous: God of Adam, Abel, Seth, Enos, Enoch, Noah, Shem, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the twelve patriarchs, Moses and the prophets. And that this God, in the last days, as he had promised through his prophets, sent the Lord Jesus Christ, to call Israel first, and afterwards, after the unbelief of the people of Israel, also the nations. This God, just and good, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, himself gave the Law, the Prophets and the Gospels; he is the God of the Apostles and of the Old and New Testaments. Then, because Jesus Christ himself, who came before every creature, was born of the Father, who, when all things were created, served the Father (for all things were made through him), in the last times emptied himself and was made man. He was made flesh, being God, and remained what he was, God.

units.la: L.
units.tr: L.

units.la: Ex cap.2. Nemo putet aliquid nos insubstantiuum dicere, quum Dei Filium Sapientiam nominamus. Si ergo semel rectè receptum est, vnigenitum Filium Dei Sapientiam eius esse substantialiter subsistentem, quomodo extra huius Sapientiae generationem aliquando Deum Patrem vel punctum momenti alicuius quis potest sentire, vel credere? propter quod nos semper Deum Patrem nouimus vnigeniti Filij sui. Extra omne igitur quod vel dici, vel intelligi potest, initium, generatam credendum est Sapientiam. In hac ipsa ergo Sapientiae subsistentia omnia erant praeformata atque disposita.
units.tr: From chapter 2. Let no one think that we say anything unsubstantial when we call the Son of God Wisdom. If, therefore, it has once been rightly accepted that the only-begotten Son of God is his Wisdom, subsisting substantially, how can anyone conceive or believe that there was ever a God the Father outside the generation of this Wisdom, even for a moment? For this reason we always know God the Father as the Father of his only-begotten Son. Therefore we must believe that Wisdom was generated outside everything that can be said or understood to have a beginning. In this very subsistence of Wisdom, therefore, all things were preformed and arranged.

units.la: LI.
units.tr: LI.

units.la: Sicut igitur voluntas procedit è mente, & neque partem aliquam mentis secat, neque ab ea separatur aut diuiditur, tali quadam specie putandus est Pater Filii genuisse imaginem scilicet suam. Vt sicut ipse inuisibilis est per naturam, {ʂ}ita imaginem quoque inuisibilem genuerit.
units.tr: Just as the will proceeds from the mind, and neither divides any part of the mind nor is separated or split from it, so in a similar way we must think that the Father begot the Son, namely his own image. Just as he is invisible by nature, so he also begot an invisible image.

units.la: LII.
units.tr: LII.

units.la: Gregorius Neocæsariensis in Antiochena Synodo convo-cata contra Paulum Samosatenum.
units.tr: Gregory of Neocaesarea, in the Synod of Antioch convened against Paul of Samosata.

units.la: Unus Deus Pater Verbi viventis, Sapientiæ subsistentis, & imaginis suæ integræ, integer genitor, Pater Filij unigeniti, unus Dominus, solus ex solo, i-mago Patris, Verbum efficax, Filius sempiternus ex sempiterno, unus Spiri-tus sanctus, ex Deo substantiam habens, qui per Filium apparuit sanctificans, per quem Deus super omnia, & in omnibus cognoscitur.
units.tr: One God, the Father of the living Word, of the subsisting Wisdom and of his entire image, the entire begetter, the Father of the only-begotten Son, one Lord, alone from alone, the image of the Father, the effective Word, the eternal Son from the eternal, one Holy Spirit, having substance from God, who appeared through the Son sanctifying, through whom God is known above all things and in all things.

units.la: LIII.
units.tr: LIII.

units.la: Synodus Nicena convocata contra Arium.
units.tr: The Nicene Synod, convened against Arius.

units.la: Huic interfuit Athanasius, ut testatur Rufinus Ecclesiasticæ historiæ libro 10.cap.14. Igitur apud Alexandriam defuncto Alexandro, Athanasius susceperat sedem. Quòd vero esset acris ingenij, & in Ecclesiasticis negotiis apprime vigilans, satis jam tunc hæreticis innotuerat, quum ad concilium Ni-ceenum cum Episcopo suo sene Alexandro venerat, cuius suggestionibus hæreticorum doli ac fallaciæ vigilanter detegebantur. Oportet igitur verba Symboli Niceni: Credimus in unum Deum Patrem omnipotentem, visibilium omnium & invisibilium factorem. Et in unum Dominum nostrum IE-SUM CHRISTUM, Filium Dei de Patre natum unigenitum, id est, de substantia Patris, Deum ex Deo, lumen ex lumine, Deum verum ex Deo vero, natum non factum, ὁμοούσιον Patri, hoc est, eiusdem substantiæ cum Pa-tre, &c. Oportet inquam verba eius Symboli intelligere sicut Athanasius, Eusebius Palestinus, & alij qui interfuerunt Synodo, exposuerunt. Nam quum Arius verba Niceni Symboli pro sua doctrina interpretaretur, coactus est Athanasius in suo Symbolo veram sententiam explicare. Quare facilè intelligi potest Gentilem Arianum esse, cùm reiiciat Symbolum Athana-sii, in quo dicitur, Quicunque vult saluus esse, ante omnia opus est ut teneat Catholicam fidem: quam nisi quis integram, inviolatámque servaverit, absque dubio in æternum peribit. Fides autem Catholica hæc est, ut unum Deum in Trinitate, & Trinitatem in unitate veneremur. Hanc fidem Gentilis dicit esse humanum commentum, ignotum sacris literis & Catholicis.
units.tr: Athanasius was present at this, as Rufinus testifies in Book 10, chapter 14 of his Ecclesiastical History. When Alexander had died at Alexandria, Athanasius had taken the see. That he was of keen intellect and especially watchful in church affairs was already well known to the heretics, when he came to the Council of Nicaea with his bishop, the aged Alexander, by whose prompting the frauds and deceits of the heretics were carefully exposed. It is necessary, therefore, to understand the words of the Nicene Creed: "We believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible; and in one Lord our JESUS CHRIST, the Son of God, begotten of the Father, the only-begotten, that is, of the substance of the Father, God of God, light of light, true God of true God, begotten not made, homoousion [ὁμοούσιον] with the Father, that is, of the same substance as the Father, etc. It is necessary, I say, to understand the words of that Creed as Athanasius, Eusebius of Palestine and the others who took part in the Synod explained them. For when Arius interpreted the words of the Nicene Creed in support of his own doctrine, Athanasius was forced to set out the true meaning in his own Creed. Hence it can easily be understood that Gentilis is an Arian, since he rejects the Athanasian Creed, in which it is said: "Whoever wishes to be saved must first of all hold the Catholic faith; unless someone keeps this whole and inviolate, without doubt he will perish forever. Now the Catholic faith is this: that we worship one God in Trinity and Trinity in unity." Gentilis says that this faith is a human invention, unknown to the sacred letters and to the Catholics.

units.la: LIIII.
units.tr: LIIII.

units.la: Quū[?] autem ex omnibus qui sequuti sunt Apostolos, usque ad Niceną Sy-nodum scripturæ interpretibus probatum jam sit, eos sic intellexisse Symbolum Apostolorum, ut Athanasius illud exposuit, & hanc suam interpretationem ex dictis Prophetarum & Apostolorum confirmasse, nihil iam restat, nisi ut addamus testimonia interpretū scripturæ, qui sequuti sunt Synodum Nicenam, & ex illorum dictis atque Ecclesiæ perpetua invocatione impudentia Gentilis mendacia refutemus.
units.tr: Since it has now been proved, from all who followed the Apostles down to the Nicene Synod, by the interpreters of Scripture, that they understood the Apostles' Creed as Athanasius explained it, and confirmed this his interpretation from the sayings of the Prophets and Apostles, nothing remains except that we add the testimonies of the interpreters of Scripture who followed the Nicene Synod, and by their sayings and the perpetual invocation of the Church refute the shameless lies of Gentilis.

units.la: LV.
units.tr: LV.

units.la: Et quidem Basilius eorum testimonia qui eum præcesserunt collegit, inter quæ etiam illud est Eusebÿ Palestini: Sanctum Deum, lucis conditorem per Salvatorem nostrum Iesum Christum, cum sancto Spiritu invocantes.
units.tr: Basil indeed gathered the testimonies of those who came before him, among which is also that of Eusebius of Palestine: "Invoking the holy God, the maker of light, through our Saviour Jesus Christ, with the Holy Spirit."

units.la: LVI.
units.tr: LVI.

units.la: Idem Basilius ex verbis Christi, Baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, & Filÿ & Spiritus sancti, sic colligit: Baptizari oportet ut accepimus, credere autem ut baptizamur, glorificare etiam ut credimus Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum. Huc pertinet disputatio Basilij contra Eunomiū. Et fratris eius Gregorÿ, qua disertissimè exponit & clariss. ac firmiss. refutat errorem Getilis[?]. Hæc nunc edita est à clariss. & doctiss. viro, D. Ioach. Camerario, Græcè & Latinè, & ab eodem typographo, à quo hæc nostra eduntur, expressa. Ideo hortor ut lector eam sibi comparet, & Gregorij refutationem legat. Nam Gentilis contendit unum Deum non posse dici aut esse ἀγεννητὸν καὶ γεννητὸν, & hæc duo ait significare diuersas essentias, sicut Eunomius.
units.tr: The same Basil from the words of Christ, "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit," concludes thus: "We must be baptized as we have received, believe as we are baptized, and also glorify the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit as we believe." To this belongs Basil's disputation against Eunomius, and that of his brother Gregory, in which he most eloquently sets out and most clearly and firmly refutes the error of Gentilis. This has now been published by the most distinguished and learned man, Dr Joachim Camerarius, in Greek and Latin, and printed by the same printer by whom this work of ours is published. I therefore urge the reader to obtain it and read Gregory's refutation. For Gentilis contends that the one God cannot be called or be unbegotten and begotten [ἀγεννητὸν καὶ γεννητὸν], and he says that these two terms signify different essences, just as Eunomius did.

units.la: LVII.
units.tr: LVII.

units.la: Hilarius libro tertio ex dicto Mosis in Genesi: Faciamus hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem nostram, probat unum Deum, & distinctas personas, libro secundo & tertio De Trinitate, ut docet Longobardus in suis sententiis. Ambrosius verba baptismi, In nomine Patris & Filij & Spiritus sancti sic exponit: In nomine, & non nominibus, ut unitas essentiæ ostendatur, & Patrem, & Filium, & Spiritum sanctum tres esse personas.
units.tr: Hilary, in Book 3, from the saying of Moses in Genesis, "Let us make man in our image and likeness," proves one God and distinct persons, in Books 2 and 3 of On the Trinity, as Lombard teaches in his Sentences. Ambrose explains the words of baptism, "In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit," thus: "In the name, and not the names, so that the unity of essence is shown, and that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three persons."

units.la: LVIII.
units.tr: LVIII.

units.la: Augustinus libro primo De Trinitate: Omnes Catholici tractatores, qui de Trinitate (quæ Deus est) scripserunt, hoc intendunt secundum scripturas declarare, quod Pater & Filius & Spiritus sanctus unius sint substantiæ, & inseparabili æqualitate unus sint Deus.
units.tr: Augustine, in Book 1 of On the Trinity: "All Catholic writers who have written about the Trinity, which is God, intend to declare according to the Scriptures that the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are of one substance, and are one God in inseparable equality."

units.la: LIX.
units.tr: LIX.

units.la: Hæc doctrina confirmata est in omnibus Synodis, ut in sexta dicitur: Hic status est Evangelicæ atque Apostolicæ doctrinæ, regularisque traditio, ut inseparabilem Trinitatem, id est, Patrem, & Filium, & Spiritum sanctum unius Deitatis, naturæ & substantiæ sive essentiæ, unius eiusdemque prædicemus & naturalis, volūtatis, virtutis, operationis, dominationis, maiestatis, potestatis, & gloriæ, & quicquid de eadem sancta Trinitate essentialiter dicitur, singulari numero, tanquam de una natura trium substantialium personarum comprehendamus regulari ratione instituti.
units.tr: This doctrine was confirmed in all the Synods, as the Sixth says: "This is the position of the Evangelical and Apostolic teaching and the rule of tradition, that we proclaim the inseparable Trinity, that is, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, of one and the same Deity, nature and substance or essence, and of one and the same will, power, operation, dominion, majesty, authority and glory; and that we comprehend whatever is said essentially of that same holy Trinity in the singular number, as of one nature of three substantial persons, in the manner laid down by rule."

units.la: LX.
units.tr: LX.

units.la: Ex his facilè conspici potest, quàm impudens & impium sit mendacium Gentilis, quo dicit, Deum Trinitatem esse humanum commentum, ignotum Catholicis: & Deum Trinitatem significare aliud quàm tres personas, Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum, ac Trinitatem esse nomen substantiale, & ex eo probari quartam in Trinitate personam, & quartam substantiam distinctam à Patre, Filio, & Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: From these things it can easily be seen how shameless and impious is the lie of Gentilis, when he says that the Trinity of God is a human invention, unknown to Catholics; that "the Trinity of God" signifies something other than three persons, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit; that "Trinity" is a substantial name; and that from this a fourth person in the Trinity is proved, and a fourth substance distinct from the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: LXI.
units.tr: LXI.

units.la: Refutantur hæc mendacia ex invocatione Ecclesiæ Catholicæ
units.tr: These lies are refuted from the invocation of the Catholic Church

units.la: Pater de cælis, Deus. Fili Redemptor mundi, Deus. Spiritus sancte, Deus. Sancta Trinitas unus Deus, miserere nobis.
units.tr: Father in heaven, God. Son, Redeemer of the world, God. Holy Spirit, God. Holy Trinity, one God, have mercy on us.

units.la: Item, Te Deum verum unum in Trinitate, & trinum in unitate, venite adoremus. Et,
units.tr: Likewise: "We worship you, the true God, one in Trinity and Trinity in unity; come, let us adore."

units.la: Te Deum Patrem ingenitum, te Filium unigenitum, te Spiritum sanctum Paracletum: Sanctam & individuam Trinitatem toto corde, & ore confitemur, laudamus atque benedicimus. Et.
units.tr: "We confess, praise and bless you, God the Father unbegotten, you the Son only-begotten, you the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, the holy and undivided Trinity, with our whole heart and mouth." And:

units.la: Te Deum laudamus[?], te Dominum confitemur. Te æternum Patrem omnis terra veneratur[?]. Tibi omnes Angeli, tibi cœli & universæ potestates. Tibi Cherubin & Seraphin incessabili voce proclamant, Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dominus Deus Zebaoth. Pleni sunt cœli & terra maiestatis gloriæ tuæ. Te gloriosus Apostolorum Chorus. Te Prophetarum laudabilis numerus. Te Martyrum candidatus laudat exercitus. Te per orbem terrarum sancta confitetur Ecclesia, Patrem immensæ maiestatis, venerandum tuum verum, & unicum Filium. Sanctum quoque Paracletum Spiritum. Et in præfatione Eucharistica: Qui cum unigenito Filio tuo unus es Deus, unus es Dominus. Non in unius singularitate personæ, sed in unius Trinitate substantiæ. Quod enim de tua gloria revelante te credimus, hoc de Filio tuo, hoc de Spiritu sancto sine differentia discretione sentimus, ut in Confessione veræ sempiternæque Trinitatis, & in personis proprietas, & in essentia unitas, & in maiestate adoretur æqualitas.
units.tr: "We praise you, O God; we acknowledge you as Lord. Eternal Father, all the earth worships you. To you all the Angels, to you the heavens and all the powers. To you the Cherubim and Seraphim cry out with unceasing voice: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth; the heavens and the earth are full of the majesty of your glory. The glorious choir of the Apostles praises you; the praiseworthy number of the Prophets; the white-robed army of the Martyrs. Through all the world the holy Church confesses you: the Father of immeasurable majesty, your true and unique Son, and the Holy Spirit the Paraclete." And in the Eucharistic preface: "Who with your only-begotten Son are one God, one Lord; not in the singularity of one person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For what we believe of your glory, revealed by you, that we feel without difference or distinction concerning your Son and concerning the Holy Spirit; so that in the confession of the true and everlasting Trinity, the property is adored in the persons, the unity in the essence, and the equality in the majesty."

units.la: LXII.
units.tr: LXII.

units.la: Quod autem Gentilis ait, Trinitatem esse nomen essentiale, & significare substantiam distinctam à tribus per-sonis, & quartam in Trinitate personam, refutatur ab Augustino dicête: Præterea est vnum nomen quod de nulla per-sona singulatim dicitur, sed de omnibus simul, vt Trinitas, quod non dicitur se-cundum substantiam, sed quasi collectiuum pluralitatem designat personarum. Et lib.9. De Trinitate: Quapropter credamus Patrem, & Filiū, & Spiritum sanctum vnum esse Deum, vniuersæ creaturæ conditorem, & rectorem, nec Patrem esse Filium, nec Spiritum sanctum, vel Patrem vel Filium Trinitatem relatarum adinuicem personarum.
units.tr: As for Gentilis's claim that "Trinity" is an essential name, signifying a substance distinct from the three persons, and a fourth person in the Trinity, it is refuted by Augustine, who says: "Besides, there is one name which is not said of any single person, but of all together, as Trinity; which is not said according to substance, but as a collective name designating a plurality of persons." And in Book 9 of On the Trinity: "Therefore let us believe that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God, the creator and ruler of the whole creation; nor is the Father the Son, nor the Holy Spirit the Father or the Son, but the Trinity of persons related to one another."

units.la: LXIII.
units.tr: LXIII.

units.la: Vt enim ipse in libro De fide ad Petrū ait, Vna est natura seu essentia Pa-tris & Filij, & Spiritus sancti, non vna persona. Si enim sic esset vna persona, sicut est substantia Patris, & Filij & Spiritus sancti, veraciter Trinitas non diceretur. Rursus quidem Trinitas esset vera, sed vnus Deus Trinitas ipsa non esset, si quemadmodum Pater, & Filius & Spiritus sanctus, personarum sunt abinuicem proprietate distincti, sic fuissent naturarum diuersitate discreti. Fi-des autem Patriarcharum, Prophetarum, & Apostolorum, vnum Deū præ-dicat Trinitatem esse.
units.tr: For as he himself says in the book On the Faith to Peter: "The nature or essence of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit is one, not one person. For if it were one person, just as the substance of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit is one, it would not truly be called a Trinity. Again, the Trinity would indeed be true, but the Trinity itself would not be one God, if, just as the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are distinguished from one another by the property of their persons, so they were distinguished by a diversity of natures. But the faith of the Patriarchs, Prophets and Apostles proclaims that the Trinity is one God."

units.la: LXIIII.
units.tr: LXIV.

units.la: Gentilis ait, se medium inter Sabellium & Arium tenere, & neque ponere Deum trinomium, ne videatur vnum Sabellii[?] sentire, neque tripersonatum, ne cum Ario: sed affirmare Patrem esse vnum Deum, non numero, aut natura, vt Arius, sed ratione originis. Filiū autem & Spiritū esse quidem naturæ Deum, cum Filius per generationem, Spiritus sanctus per processionem sit ex immensa & infinita vnius Dei Patris substantia, à qua nec dæmones eximi possunt. sed se non posse fateri Filiū & Spiritum sanctū esse vnum cum Patre Deum, ideo quòd sint tres res subsistentes, rationales, & intelligentes, & repugnantia sit in adiecto, eudem Deum esse Patrem & Filium, & quod scriptura vbique vocet vnum Deum Patrem omnipotetem, & vnum Dominum Iesum Chri-stum. Et hanc esse doctrinam Tertulliani.
units.tr: Gentilis says that he holds a middle position between Sabellius and Arius: he does not posit a God of three names, lest he seem to hold with Sabellius, nor a God of three persons, lest he agree with Arius; but he affirms that the Father is one God, not in number or nature, as Arius says, but by reason of origin. The Son and the Spirit are indeed God by nature, since the Son is so by generation and the Holy Spirit by procession, from the immense and infinite substance of the one God the Father, from which not even demons can be excluded. But he cannot confess that the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God together with the Father, because they are three subsisting, rational and intelligent things, and there is a contradiction in the terms if the same God is both Father and Son; and because Scripture everywhere calls the one God the Father almighty and the one Lord Jesus Christ. He says that this is the doctrine of Tertullian.

units.la: LXV.
units.tr: LXV.

units.la: Sed suprà induxi Tertullianum ex claris scripturæ testimoniis probantem, Patrem & Filium esse vnum Deum, propter vnam eandemque diuinæ naturæ essentiam, & alicubi dici duos non statu, sed gradu, hoc est, vt Pater sit prima in Trinitate persona, Filius secunda, Spiritus S.tertia: & tamen Filius unione divinitatis à Patre separari nō possit, sed individuum & inseparatum, (ut Tertulliani verbis dicam) cum eo Deum esse, vel, ut Ecclesia nunc loqui nos ex scripturis docuit, unum Deum, & distinctam à Patre personam.
units.tr: But above I have cited Tertullian, who from clear testimonies of Scripture proves that the Father and the Son are one God, on account of the one and the same essence of the divine nature; and who elsewhere says that they are called two not by state but by degree, that is, that the Father is the first person in the Trinity, the Son the second, and the Holy Spirit the third; and yet the Son cannot be separated from the Father by the unity of the divinity, but (to use Tertullian's words) is undivided and inseparable, God together with him; or, as the Church has now taught us to speak from the Scriptures, one God, and a person distinct from the Father.

units.la: LXVI.
units.tr: LXVI.

units.la: Quod si pleno ore Gentilis fateretur, Patrem & Filium & Spiritum S. esse tres ὑποστάσεις id est, personas subsistentes in una divina natura sive essentia, & Filium alium dici à Patre, id est, aliam ὑπόστασιν à persona Patris, & ideo dictum esse, Tres sunt qui testimonium dant in cælo, Pater, Verbum & Spiritus S. & ij tres unum sunt natura & divinitate, vel unus Deus, quod idem est, quia Deus est nomen essentiæ & naturæ: & in hanc sententiam Trinitatem dici unum Deum, id est, ὑποστάσεις Patris & Filij & Spiritus S. habere eandem divinitatem, iam inter nos conueniret. Sed quia contendit Deum Trinitatem esse humanum commentum, ignotum scripturis, & Ecclesiæ, & negat Filium posse dici unū cum Patre Deum, propter eandem divinæ naturæ essentiam: sed tantùm dici Deum ratione originis, id est, quòd ab uno Deo habeat originem, & sit ex immensa eius infinitaque substantia, à qua nihil quod subsistit seiungi potest, ac ne dæmones quidem, nisi voluntate, ipse se prodit, quòd eligat sibi novam formam doctrinæ, & omnino constituisse ex Ecclesia discedere, imitatione ambitionis eorum, qui visitatam & receptam doctrinam, & definitiones Ecclesiasticas non ex ignorantia, sed scientes & volentes oppugnant, ut clari & celebres sint. Nam scripturæ, quas citat, nihil pro ipsius dogmate faciunt, & ratiocinationes eius nullæ sunt, ut prius ex Ignatio, Iustino, Irenæo, Tertulliano, Cypriano, Clemente Alexandrino, & aliis qui præcesserunt Synodum Nicenam demonstrauimus, & nunc quoque ex illis qui hanc sequuti sunt, ostendemus.
units.tr: If Gentilis would confess with a full mouth that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three hypostases [ὑποστάσεις], that is, persons subsisting in one divine nature or essence, and that the Son is said to be other than the Father, that is, another hypostasis from the person of the Father, and that therefore it was said, "There are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one in nature and divinity," or "one God," which is the same thing, because "God" is the name of the essence and nature; and if he agreed with us that in this sense the Trinity is called one God, that is, that the hypostases of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have the same divinity: then there would be agreement between us already. But because he contends that the Trinity of God is a human invention, unknown to the Scriptures and to the Church, and denies that the Son can be called one God together with the Father on account of the one essence of the divine nature, but says he is called God only by reason of origin, that is, because he has his origin from the one God and is from his immense and infinite substance, from which nothing that subsists can be separated, not even demons except by their will: he betrays himself, that he chooses for himself a new form of doctrine, and has altogether resolved to depart from the Church, in imitation of the ambition of those who attack the accepted and received doctrine and the ecclesiastical definitions not out of ignorance but knowingly and willingly, so that they may become famous and renowned. For the Scriptures he cites do nothing for his doctrine, and his reasonings are nothing; as we have already shown from Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus, Tertullian, Cyprian, Clement of Alexandria and others who preceded the Nicene Synod, and now we shall show also from those who have followed it.

units.la: LXVII.
units.tr: LXVII.

units.la: Sic enim ratiocinaris: Ille solus unus est Deus, qui est à nullo principio, & à quo sunt omnia: Sed solus Pater originem nescies, est omnino infinitus, principiū sine principio, causa causarum, author & monarcha omnium: Igitur solus est unus Deus. Expectabam ut clarè diceres, solus est Deus. Hoc enim vis, etiamsi negas, te excludere à divinitate Filium, sed ab unitate cum Patre.
units.tr: For you reason thus: "He alone is the one God who has no beginning, and from whom all things are; but the Father alone is without knowledge of origin, is wholly infinite, a beginning without beginning, the cause of causes, the author and monarch of all; therefore he alone is the one God." I expected you to say clearly, "He alone is God." For this is what you mean, even though you deny that you exclude the Son from the divinity, but only from unity with the Father.

units.la: LXVIII.
units.tr: LXVIII.

units.la: Ad hoc argumentum Praxeas supra responsum est per Tertullianum, Monarchiam seruari per οἰκονομίαν[?], & non tantū per solitudinem. Et nunc respondeo, & distinguo Maiorem. Si enim intelligatur de rebus à Deo conditis, vera est. Si autem de Filio genito à Patre, & Spiritu sancto ab utroque proceden-te, falsa est.
units.tr: Praxeas was answered on this argument above by Tertullian: the monarchy is preserved through the economy [οἰκονομίαν], and not through solitude alone. Now I also answer by distinguishing the major premise. If it is understood of things created by God, it is true. But if it is understood of the Son begotten of the Father, and of the Holy Spirit proceeding from both, it is false.

units.la: LXIX.
units.tr: LXIX.

units.la: Ad probationem maioris: Deus clamat per Esaiam: Ego sum primus & novissimus, & præter me non est Deus. Hoc solum competit Patri, qui Filij & Spiritus sancti est essentiator. Quomodo enim Filius dicet, Et absque me non est Deus?
units.tr: To the proof of the major premise: God cries out through Isaiah, "I am the first and the last, and there is no God besides me." This belongs to the Father alone, who is the essentiator of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. For how would the Son say, "And apart from me there is no God"?

units.la: Agnosco argumentum Arij. Si Deus Pater genuit Filium Deum: Igitur genuit seipsum Deum, aut alium Deum, non seipsum Deum. Nihil autem gignit seipsum, Ergo alium Deum. Respondeo ex Ambrosio: Dic mihi, hæretice, fuitne quando omnipotens Pater erat Deus, & Pater non erat, & postea factus est, Igitur generationis accessione mutatus est?
